# Introduction

> Vittal Design is a React 19 component library built with TypeScript and Tailwind CSS 4.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/getting-started

## Overview

**Vittal Design** (`@fed/vital-design`) is a production-ready React component library designed for enterprise applications. It provides a comprehensive set of accessible, customizable UI components, with the current registry-backed `src-v2/` layer serving as the primary source for new components.

> **Distribution note:** New projects and newly added components should use the registry-backed `src-v2/` layer. The published `@fed/vital-design` npm package remains available for legacy compatibility with existing projects, but the package targets the older `src/` surface and does not expose registry-only `src-v2` assets.

## Features

- **React 19** — Built for modern React with hooks and concurrent features
- **TypeScript** — Full type safety with exported type definitions
- **Tailwind CSS 4** — Utility-first styling with a custom design token system
- **Base UI** — Accessible, unstyled primitives for complex interactions in `src-v2/`
- **shadcn Registry** — Primary installation path for new components via the shadcn CLI

## Component Categories

To see every component at once, open the [component overview](/docs/components).

### Foundation

Small building blocks for labels, actions, status indicators, and decoration.

| Component                                    | Description                                |
| -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| [Button](/docs/components/button)            | Filled and text action button variants     |
| [ButtonGroup](/docs/components/button-group) | Group related buttons with shared borders  |
| [Avatar](/docs/components/avatar)            | Profile image with color fallback initials |
| [Chip](/docs/components/chip)                | Compact selectable token for filters       |
| [Tag](/docs/components/tag)                  | Read-only label with color variants        |
| [Label](/docs/components/label)              | Accessible form label primitive            |
| [Separator](/docs/components/separator)      | Horizontal or vertical divider             |
| [Skeleton](/docs/components/skeleton)        | Loading placeholder                        |
| [Spinner](/docs/components/spinner)          | Inline loading indicator                   |
| [Icons](/docs/components/icons)              | Registry-ready icon components             |

### Inputs

Text entry controls and form composition helpers.

| Component                                    | Description                                         |
| -------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| [Field](/docs/components/field)              | Form field, label, description, and error UI        |
| [Input](/docs/components/input)              | Single-line, password, and grouped input patterns   |
| [NumberInput](/docs/components/number-input) | Numeric input with increment and decrement controls |
| [SearchBar](/docs/components/search-bar)     | Search input preset built on `InputGroup`           |
| [Checkbox](/docs/components/checkbox)        | Checkbox with indeterminate state                   |
| [RadioGroup](/docs/components/radio-group)   | Mutually exclusive radio choices                    |
| [Switch](/docs/components/switch)            | Boolean on/off control                              |
| [Slider](/docs/components/slider)            | Numeric range input                                 |

### Pickers and Menus

Components that own popup state, search, or keyboard navigation.

| Component                                      | Description                                      |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| [Select](/docs/components/select)              | Flat single or multiple dropdown picker          |
| [Autocomplete](/docs/components/autocomplete)  | Suggestion dropdown for free-text input          |
| [Combobox](/docs/components/combobox)          | Searchable input picker with optional tag values |
| [Command](/docs/components/command)            | Command palette and custom searchable list base  |
| [DropdownMenu](/docs/components/dropdown-menu) | Action menu                                      |
| [Popover](/docs/components/popover)            | Anchored floating content                        |
| [Calendar](/docs/components/calendar)          | Date picker calendar                             |
| [TimePicker](/docs/components/time-picker)     | Time selection input                             |

### Overlays and Feedback

Surfaces and status messages that appear above or alongside content.

| Component                           | Description                |
| ----------------------------------- | -------------------------- |
| [Alert](/docs/components/alert)     | Status or feedback message |
| [Toast](/docs/components/toast)     | Transient notification     |
| [Dialog](/docs/components/dialog)   | Modal overlay              |
| [Sheet](/docs/components/sheet)     | Slide-in side panel        |
| [Tooltip](/docs/components/tooltip) | Contextual hover hint      |

### Layout and Navigation

Structural components for arranging and navigating content.

| Component                                               | Description                                      |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| [Tabs](/docs/components/tabs)                           | Tabbed content sections                          |
| [Breadcrumb](/docs/components/breadcrumb)               | Navigation trail of parent pages                 |
| [Collapsible](/docs/components/collapsible)             | Expandable and collapsible content region        |
| [Item](/docs/components/item)                           | Reusable media, title, description, actions row  |
| [Table](/docs/components/table)                         | Data table primitives                            |
| [Table of Contents](/docs/components/table-of-contents) | Page section rail that expands on hover or focus |
| [Toolbar](/docs/components/toolbar)                     | Horizontal command surface                       |
| [SplitButton](/docs/components/split-button)            | Primary action with adjacent secondary trigger   |
| [Progress](/docs/components/progress)                   | Linear progress indicator                        |
| [ScrollArea](/docs/components/scroll-area)              | Custom scrollbar container                       |
| [Resizable](/docs/components/resizable)                 | Resizable panel layout                           |

### Composite Blocks

Pre-composed patterns combining multiple atomic components for common UI scenarios.

| Block                                                                             | Description                                                                               |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Sidebar — Flat](/docs/blocks/sidebar/cloud/flat)                                 | Frosted-glass cloud sidebar with a flat nav and no account footer                         |
| [Sidebar — Inline Submenus](/docs/blocks/sidebar/cloud/inline-submenus)           | Nested items as inline submenus, with an account footer                                   |
| [Sidebar — Collapsible Submenus](/docs/blocks/sidebar/cloud/collapsible-submenus) | Inline submenus that fold with Collapsible                                                |
| [Sidebar — Dropdown Submenus](/docs/blocks/sidebar/cloud/dropdown-submenus)       | Submenus open as a dropdown-menu                                                          |
| [Sidebar — Secondary Nav](/docs/blocks/sidebar/cloud/secondary-nav)               | Secondary navigation pinned above the account footer                                      |
| [Sidebar — Header Actions](/docs/blocks/sidebar/cloud/header-actions)             | Mark-only logo, header search and notifications, and an account footer                    |
| [Data Table](/docs/blocks/data-table)                                             | Grouped, sortable, resizable table with row selection and inline and popover cell editing |
| [Tree Select](/docs/blocks/tree-select)                                           | Searchable hierarchical path picker built from Command and Popover                        |

## Design Principles

- **Predictable** — Consistent props API across all components
- **Composable** — Components work well together and with custom code
- **Accessible** — ARIA attributes and keyboard navigation via Base UI
- **Themeable** — CSS custom properties for design token customization

# Installation

> Install Vittal Design in your React project.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/getting-started/installation

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 18+
- React 19
- Tailwind CSS 4

## Initialize shadcn

Before installing components, your project needs a `components.json` configuration file. Run the initializer once:

```bash
npx shadcn@latest init
```

When prompted, configure the paths to match your project structure (CSS file, component aliases, etc.). See the [shadcn documentation](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/installation) for framework-specific setup.

Then declare the Vittal Design registry in `components.json` so the CLI can resolve `@vital-design/` dependencies:

```json
{
  "registries": {
    "@vital-design": "https://vittal.design/r/{name}.json"
  }
}
```

> **Recommended path:** For new projects and newly added components, use the Vittal Design registry. This is the primary delivery channel for the current `src-v2/` component layer.

## Install via shadcn CLI (Recommended)

Install individual components directly into your project using the shadcn CLI. Components are copied into your codebase so you have full ownership.

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @vital-design/<component-name>
```

For example, to add the Button component:

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @vital-design/button
```

> The `@vital-design/<name>` alias is recommended because it also resolves `@vital-design/*` dependencies declared by registry items. Newly added components may be available only through the registry.

See the [Registry](/docs/registry) page for the full list of available components.

## Install as npm Package (Legacy Compatibility)

If you are maintaining an existing project that already depends on the published package, you can continue installing the full library as a package:

```bash
# pnpm
pnpm add @fed/vital-design

# npm
npm install @fed/vital-design

# yarn
yarn add @fed/vital-design
```

> **Legacy compatibility:** The npm package remains supported for existing consumers, but it is not the primary delivery channel for new components. If you need the latest additions, use the registry path above.
>
> **Boundary note:** The npm package targets the legacy `src/` distribution. It does not expose registry-only `src-v2/` files such as the Tailwind theme stylesheet.
>
> **Note:** The npm package is published to a private GitLab registry. Make sure your `.npmrc` is configured to authenticate with `https://git.gss.com.tw/api/v4/projects/5615/packages/npm/`.

## Peer Dependencies

Vittal Design requires the following peer dependencies:

```bash
pnpm add react react-dom
```

If you use the legacy npm package flow, also install `styled-components` because the published `src/` distribution still depends on it:

```bash
pnpm add styled-components
```

Most frameworks already include `react` and `react-dom`, but verify they are present in your app before using Vittal Design.

# Migration Guide v0 to v1

> Move from the legacy npm package surface to the registry-backed src-v2 components.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/getting-started/migration-guide

## What Changes

v0 means the published `@fed/vital-design` package built from `src/`.
v1 means registry-installed components built from `src-v2/`.

The main change is ownership:

- v0: import components from `@fed/vital-design`
- v1: install components with the Vittal Design registry, then import the copied files from your app

```tsx
// v0
import { Button, Select } from '@fed/vital-design';

// v1
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import {
  Select,
  SelectContent,
  SelectItem,
  SelectItemText,
  SelectTrigger,
} from '@/components/ui/Select';
```

Use v1 for new work. Keep v0 only while migrating existing screens.

## Before You Start

1. Add the registry config from [Installation](/docs/getting-started/installation).
2. Complete [Tailwind CSS Setup](/docs/getting-started/tailwind-setup).
3. Migrate one screen at a time.
4. Remove `@fed/vital-design` and `styled-components` only after no v0 imports remain.

## Install Pattern

Install the component you need:

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @vital-design/button
```

After install, import from the local path created by your `components.json`.
Examples in these docs use `@/components/ui/*`.

## Component Mapping

The v0 package barrel exports `Avatar`, `Button`, `Checkbox`, `Chip`,
`RadioGroup`, `SearchBar`, `Select`, `SplitButton`, `Switch`, `Tag`,
and `TreeSelect`. `ActionList` and `ActionInfiniteList` are no longer
exposed from v0 — see the rows below for the v1 replacements. Other
rows cover legacy source files with v1 registry equivalents.

| v0 component or source       | v0 source file                                         | v1 registry item               | v1 source file                                             | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Avatar`                     | `src/components/avatar/Avatar.tsx`                     | `@vital-design/avatar`         | `src-v2/components/avatar/Avatar.tsx`                      | Same role                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `Button`                     | `src/components/button/Button.tsx`                     | `@vital-design/button`         | `src-v2/components/button/Button.tsx`                      | Icon and loading API changed                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `SplitButton`                | `src/components/button/split-button/SplitButton.tsx`   | `@vital-design/split-button`   | `src-v2/components/button/split-button/SplitButton.tsx`    | Uses `ButtonGroup` internally                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `Checkbox`                   | `src/components/checkbox/Checkbox.tsx`                 | `@vital-design/checkbox`       | `src-v2/components/checkbox/Checkbox.tsx`                  | Same role                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `Chip`                       | `src/components/chip/Chip.tsx`                         | `@vital-design/chip`           | `src-v2/components/chip/Chip.tsx`                          | Same role                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `RadioGroup`                 | `src/components/radio-group/RadioGroup.tsx`            | `@vital-design/radio-group`    | `src-v2/components/radio-group/RadioGroup.tsx`             | Same role                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `SearchBar`                  | `src/components/search-bar/SearchBar.tsx`              | `@vital-design/search-bar`     | `src-v2/components/search-bar/SearchBar.tsx`               | Built on `InputGroup`                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `Select`                     | `src/components/select/Select.tsx`                     | `@vital-design/select`         | `src-v2/components/select/Select.tsx`                      | Flat single or multiple dropdown                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `Switch`                     | `src/components/switch/Switch.tsx`                     | `@vital-design/switch`         | `src-v2/components/switch/Switch.tsx`                      | Same role                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `Tag`                        | `src/components/tag/Tag.tsx`                           | `@vital-design/tag`            | `src-v2/components/tag/Tag.tsx`                            | Same role                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `TextInput`                  | `src/components/input/textInput/TextInput.tsx`         | `@vital-design/input`          | `src-v2/components/input/input/Input.tsx`                  | Use `Input`; use `InputGroup` for addons; prefer Base UI `onValueChange` for value-style callers                                                                                                   |
| `TextareaInput` → `Textarea` | `src/components/input/textareaInput/TextareaInput.tsx` | `@vital-design/textarea`       | `src-v2/components/textarea/Textarea.tsx`                  | Native textarea primitive; use `InputGroupTextarea` only for custom input shells                                                                                                                   |
| `PasswordInput`              | `src/components/input/passwordInput/PasswordInput.tsx` | `@vital-design/password-input` | `src-v2/components/input/password-input/PasswordInput.tsx` | Built on `InputGroup`                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `Mask`                       | `src/components/mask/Mask.tsx`                         | `@vital-design/scroll-area`    | `src-v2/components/scroll-area/ScrollArea.tsx`             | No direct wrapper replacement; compose `ScrollArea` when a viewport needs edge fade                                                                                                                |
| `ActionList`                 | (removed)                                              | Pick by intent — see notes     | —                                                          | Action menu → `@vital-design/dropdown-menu`; value picker → `@vital-design/combobox`; hierarchical picker → `@vital-design/command` + `@vital-design/popover`; display rows → `@vital-design/item` |
| `ActionInfiniteList`         | (removed)                                              | Pick by intent — see notes     | —                                                          | Same as `ActionList`; own loading and paging in app                                                                                                                                                |
| `TreeSelect`                 | `src/components/tree-select/TreeSelect.tsx`            | `@vital-design/tree-select`    | `src-v2/blocks/tree-select/components/tree-select.tsx`     | Install the block and edit it in place; the screen owns the data, loading, and selected path                                                                                                       |

## New v1-Only Components

These components do not exist in the v0 npm package:

| Component     | Registry item                | Use when                            |
| ------------- | ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| `ButtonGroup` | `@vital-design/button-group` | Group buttons or split button parts |
| `Input`       | `@vital-design/input`        | Single-line text fields             |
| `InputGroup`  | `@vital-design/input-group`  | Build custom input shells           |
| `Item`        | `@vital-design/item`         | Display rows with media and actions |
| `Label`       | `@vital-design/label`        | Form control labels                 |
| `Combobox`    | `@vital-design/combobox`     | Searchable picker or tag picker     |
| `Skeleton`    | `@vital-design/skeleton`     | Loading placeholder                 |
| `Spinner`     | `@vital-design/spinner`      | Loading indicator                   |

## Picker Choice

Use the new picker split:

| Need                                            | v1 component                                              |
| ----------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Flat single or multiple value picker            | `Select`                                                  |
| Searchable value picker, autocomplete, or chips | `Combobox`                                                |
| Hierarchical path picker                        | `tree-select` block (`Command` + `Popover`)               |
| Action menu where each item fires a callback    | `DropdownMenu`                                            |
| Display row list                                | `Item` + `ItemGroup` (`size="list"` for picker-like rows) |
| Command panel                                   | `Command`                                                 |

`Command` is shipped as a public primitive (`@vital-design/command`) for command palettes, custom searchable popups, and paged hierarchical pickers.

Changing the trigger appearance does not change the component choice. Keep `Select` and `Combobox` as their own roots; build hierarchical path pickers from `Popover` + `Command`.

Do not wrap `Select`, `Combobox`, or custom `Command` pickers inside `DropdownMenu` to get a button trigger. Use `DropdownMenu` only when the popup rows are commands rather than a bound value.

## Code Changes

### Imports

Replace package imports with local imports:

```tsx
// v0
import { SearchBar } from '@fed/vital-design';

// v1
import { SearchBar } from '@/components/ui/SearchBar';
```

Compound components use named exports:

```tsx
import {
  Select,
  SelectContent,
  SelectItem,
  SelectItemText,
  SelectTrigger,
} from '@/components/ui/Select';
```

### Button

Button no longer owns icons or loading state. Move icons and spinners into `children`, and mark them with `data-icon="inline-start"` or `data-icon="inline-end"`.

```tsx
// v0
import { Button } from '@fed/vital-design';
import { MagnifyingGlassIcon } from './icons/MagnifyingGlassIcon';

<Button icon={<MagnifyingGlassIcon />} iconPlacement="left">
  Search
</Button>;

// v1
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import { MagnifyingGlassIcon } from '@/components/icons/MagnifyingGlassIcon';

<Button>
  <MagnifyingGlassIcon data-icon="inline-start" />
  Search
</Button>;
```

Replace `isLoading` with an explicit disabled button plus `Spinner`.
Install `@vital-design/spinner` if your app needs the shared spinner.

```tsx
// v0
import { Button } from '@fed/vital-design';

<Button isLoading>Saving</Button>

// v1
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import { Spinner } from '@/components/ui/Spinner';

<Button disabled>
  <Spinner data-icon="inline-start" />
  Saving
</Button>
```

Icon-only buttons now use size variants instead of empty children or icon props:

```tsx
<Button size="icon-md" aria-label="Search">
  <MagnifyingGlassIcon data-icon="inline-start" />
</Button>

<Button size="icon-lg" aria-label="Search">
  <MagnifyingGlassIcon data-icon="inline-start" />
</Button>
```

Keep `size="md"` or `size="lg"` for buttons with labels. For filled label buttons, v1 keeps the v0 spacing contract: the icon side is 12px, and the non-icon side is 16px.
If you used earlier v1 draft size names, rename `medium` to `md`, `large` to `lg`, `icon-medium` to `icon-md`, and `icon-large` to `icon-lg`.

The `variant` prop renamed `filled` to `default`. The new `ghost` variant is a transparent button with hover background — use it inside popovers, toolbars, and split-button menus (it backs the Popup Button pattern).

```tsx
// v0 / earlier v1 draft
<Button variant="filled" theme="primary">Save</Button>

// v1
<Button variant="default" theme="primary">Save</Button>

// New ghost variant
<Button variant="ghost" theme="primary">Open</Button>
```

The `theme` enum keeps `alarm` (filled red) and `dangerous` (white surface with red text) as distinct intents — `alarm` is only available on `variant="default"`. The `dangerous` theme renders bordered at `size="md"` and shadow-elevated at `size="lg"`, mirroring the Figma "Outlined" guideline.

### Text input value changes

`Input` is built on Base UI's input primitive. For controlled value
updates, prefer `onValueChange`; keep native `onChange` only when the
caller needs the DOM change event.

```tsx
// v0
<TextInput value={name} onChange={(event) => setName(event.target.value)} />

// v1
<Input value={name} onValueChange={setName} />
```

### Invalid form controls

V1-only `isError` props are removed from v2 form controls. Use `aria-invalid` on the actual control instead.

```tsx
// v0
<Input isError />
<InputGroup isError>
  <InputGroupInput />
</InputGroup>
<PasswordInput isError value={password} onChange={setPassword} />

// v1
<Input aria-invalid />
<InputGroup>
  <InputGroupInput aria-invalid />
</InputGroup>
<PasswordInput
  aria-invalid
  value={password}
  onChange={setPassword}
/>
```

When using `Field`, set invalid state on both the field wrapper and the control: `Field data-invalid` handles label/help text styling, while `aria-invalid` on the actual control handles control semantics and the visible border.

### Switch

Switch now follows the Base UI callback name. Replace `onChange` with `onCheckedChange`; root props such as `defaultChecked`, `name`, `value`, `disabled`, and `aria-invalid` pass through.

```tsx
// v0
import { Switch } from '@fed/vital-design';

<Switch checked={enabled} onChange={setEnabled} />;

// v1
import { Switch } from '@/components/ui/Switch';

<Switch checked={enabled} onCheckedChange={setEnabled} />;
```

### Label

Install `@vital-design/label` when a migrated screen has standalone text associated with a form control.

```tsx
// v1
import { Input } from '@/components/ui/Input';
import { Label } from '@/components/ui/Label';

<div className="flex flex-col gap-2">
  <Label htmlFor="email">Email</Label>
  <Input id="email" placeholder="name@example.com" />
</div>;
```

Use `Label` for visible field labels that point at `Input`, `InputGroupInput`, `Textarea`, or `PasswordInput` with `htmlFor`.

Do not hide low-level label composition inside primitives:

- `Checkbox` and `RadioGroupItem` are control primitives. Pair them with `Label htmlFor` at the callsite.
- `InputGroupAddon` is presentational. Use `Label htmlFor` outside the group when the field has visible label text.

Current v2 label audit:

| Location                                                                         | Migrate to `Label`? | Notes                                                     |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `src-v2/components/label/Label.tsx`                                              | No                  | The primitive implementation                              |
| `src-v2/components/checkbox/Checkbox.tsx`                                        | Yes                 | Pair with `Label htmlFor` at callsites                    |
| `src-v2/components/radio-group/RadioGroup.tsx`                                   | Yes                 | Pair items with `Label htmlFor` at callsites              |
| `src-v2/components/input/input-group/InputGroup.test.tsx`                        | No                  | Test-only render override for addon semantics             |
| App/docs examples around `Input`, `InputGroupInput`, `Textarea`, `PasswordInput` | Yes                 | Add `Label htmlFor` when the field has visible label text |

### Styling

v0 components depend on `styled-components`.
v1 components use Tailwind CSS 4 utilities and Vittal Design CSS variables.

Do not import `src-v2/styles/*` from the npm package. Use the registry install so the theme is written to your app CSS.

### Lists

`ActionList` and `ActionInfiniteList` are removed in v1. Pick the v1 replacement by intent:

- **Action menu** (each item fires a callback, no value binding) → `DropdownMenu`.
- **Searchable value picker** → `Combobox`. Hierarchical → `Command` + `Popover`.
- **Display row or detail list** → `Item` + `ItemGroup`. Use `size="list"` for select-option density.
- **Searchable command panel** (you own search, loading, paging, empty text) → `Command`.

```tsx
import {
  Item,
  ItemContent,
  ItemGroup,
  ItemTitle,
} from '@/components/ui/Item';

<ItemGroup>
  <Item size="list">
    <ItemContent>
      <ItemTitle>Option</ItemTitle>
    </ItemContent>
  </Item>
</ItemGroup>;
```

### TreeSelect

Move `TreeSelect` screens to the [Tree Select](/docs/blocks/tree-select) block, built from `Command` and `Popover`.
The old component owned more data behavior. In v1, the screen owns the data, loading state, and child loading; the block keeps the path and search value, and you edit it in place when a screen needs more.

Use `Combobox` instead if the old screen only needed searchable flat options.

## Migration Checklist

- Install the v1 registry item.
- Replace `@fed/vital-design` imports on the screen.
- Update props to the v1 component API.
- Add the Tailwind and theme setup once per app.
- Test keyboard behavior for pickers, popups, and list rows.
- Remove v0 dependencies after the last v0 import is gone.

# Tailwind CSS Setup

> Configure Tailwind CSS 4 to work with Vittal Design components and design tokens.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/getting-started/tailwind-setup

## Overview

This page applies to **registry-installed Vittal Design components**. When you install `src-v2/` components through the shadcn-compatible registry, the CLI copies them into your app and injects the Vittal Design theme tokens plus small base CSS rules into the CSS file configured in `components.json`.

If you are maintaining an existing project that still uses the published `@fed/vital-design` npm package, keep that legacy `src/` integration as-is. The npm package does **not** expose the registry-only `src-v2` stylesheet as a public import.

## Registry-Installed Local Components

In the global CSS file configured in your `components.json` (for example `app/globals.css` in Next.js), keep the Tailwind import:

```css
@import 'tailwindcss';
@import 'tw-animate-css';
```

When you install a Vittal Design component from the registry, shadcn also installs the `@vital-design/vital-theme` dependency and writes the required CSS variables, Tailwind theme tokens, and Vittal Design base rules into that CSS file for you.

Because the copied component files live inside your app source tree, Tailwind CSS 4 will usually detect them automatically. In the common `app/` or `src/` setup, you do not need an extra `@source` line for registry-installed components.

If your `components.json` points to a custom directory outside Tailwind's automatic source detection, add an `@source` rule that matches your local component path.

## Design Tokens

Registry installs expose the Vittal Design design tokens as CSS custom properties and Tailwind utilities. The shadcn flow writes the required theme variables and the `not-disabled` custom variant into your configured global CSS file for you.

For example, the following tokens become available:

```css
/* Available after registry install */
--primary-500: #0e86fe;
--grayscale-opacity-900: #232332;
--success-500: #2bcd86;
```

These are exposed as Tailwind color utilities via `@theme inline`:

```html
<!-- Use them in your markup -->
<div class="text-primary-500 bg-primary-50">...</div>
<p class="text-grayscale-opacity-900">...</p>
```

Dark values for those same variables are installed under `.dark`. Put `class="dark"` on `<html>` to switch. The theme does not follow `prefers-color-scheme`. The install also adds `@custom-variant dark (&:is(.dark *));` so `dark:` utilities use that class. Paper surfaces use `bg-background`. `bg-white` and `text-white` stay white. See [Colors → Dark mode](/docs/design-tokens/colors#dark-mode).

## PostCSS Configuration

Tailwind CSS 4 requires `@tailwindcss/postcss`. Create or update `postcss.config.js` (or `postcss.config.cjs`, depending on your project) like this:

```js
export default {
  plugins: {
    '@tailwindcss/postcss': {},
  },
};
```

If your project already uses `autoprefixer`, you can keep it.

## Fonts

Vittal Design uses the following font stack (defined in `--font-sans`):

```
'Roboto', 'Noto Sans TC', 'PingFang TC', 'Microsoft JhengHei', sans-serif
```

To load Roboto, add it to your HTML or import via a font provider. With Next.js:

```tsx
import { Roboto } from 'next/font/google';

const roboto = Roboto({
  subsets: ['latin'],
  weight: ['400', '500', '700'],
});
```

## Style isolation with data-slot

Vittal Design components expose stable `data-slot` attributes on their styled DOM parts. Use these hooks to scope Tailwind utilities and custom CSS so VD styles do not leak into your app's native elements (and vice versa).

This aligns with the [shadcn data-slot convention](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/changelog): every **DOM surface** gets a predictable selector.

### Naming

| Part    | `data-slot` value    | Example element              |
| ------- | -------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| Root    | `{component}`        | `data-slot="button"`         |
| Subpart | `{component}-{part}` | `data-slot="select-trigger"` |

### Scoping styles in your app

**Descendant selector** — limit utilities to VD parts inside a container:

```html
<div class="[&_[data-slot=button]]:rounded-lg">
  <Button>Save</Button>
</div>
```

**Custom variant** (Tailwind CSS 4) — reusable scope in `globals.css`:

```css
@custom-variant vd (& [data-slot]);
```

```html
<div class="vd:[&_[data-slot=button]]:shadow-md">
  <Button>Save</Button>
</div>
```

**Target a specific part**:

```html
<div class="[&_[data-slot=table-head]]:sticky [&_[data-slot=table-head]]:top-0">
  <Table>...</Table>
</div>
```

### Which parts get a slot?

Vittal Design uses a three-tier policy:

| Tier               | Rule                                                              | Examples                                       |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| **Required**       | Every exported part that renders a styleable DOM node             | `button`, `select-trigger`, `dialog-popup`     |
| **No passthrough** | Interactive parts must be wrapped; never `const X = Base.Trigger` | `DialogTrigger` (good), `PopoverTrigger` (gap) |
| **Exempt**         | Parts with no styleable DOM output                                | `Provider`, state-only `Root`, bare `Portal`   |

`@base-ui/react` and `cmdk` do **not** ship `data-slot`. Direct re-exports have no slot until Vittal Design wraps them. Do not expect slots on `Select` root or `ToastPortal` — scope via child parts such as `select-trigger` or `toast-content` instead.

### Coverage status

Last updated: 2026-07-03. Applies to `src-v2/components/` (43 folders).

| Status                                       | Components                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| -------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Full**                                     | alert, avatar, badge, breadcrumb, button, button-group, card, checkbox, chip, collapsible, combobox (incl. tags value), command, dropdown-menu, editable, field, input, number-input, item, label, password-input, popover, progress, radio-group, resizable, scroll-area, search-bar, separator, skeleton, slider, spinner, split-button, switch, table, table-of-contents, tabs, tag, textarea, time-picker, toolbar |
| **Near-full** (root/portal passthrough only) | select, dialog, sheet, tooltip, toast, input-group, autocomplete                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **Partial**                                  | calendar (month/year dropdown triggers in caption)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

Tier 3 exemptions (no slot by design): `Provider`, state-only `Root`, bare `Portal` on select, dialog, dropdown-menu, popover, tooltip, toast, and autocomplete. `AutocompleteValue` / `ComboboxValue` also exempt — they render no DOM (text/children only).

# Design Lint

> Lint your app against the Vital Design theme with @shadcn/lint and Oxlint.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/getting-started/design-lint

## Overview

`@vital-design/vital-design-lint` installs the Vital Design lint policy for [`@shadcn/lint`](https://github.com/shadcn-ui/lint). It checks Tailwind classes against the theme that the registry wrote into your CSS, and each error explains what to use instead. That makes it useful for people and coding agents alike.

The policy currently turns on two rules:

| Rule                        | Catches                                                           | Example                                                    |
| --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `shadcn/no-raw-colors`      | Tailwind palette colors and undeclared color tokens               | `bg-pink-500` → use a theme color such as `bg-primary-500` |
| `shadcn/no-unknown-classes` | Classes your Tailwind setup cannot generate, so no CSS is emitted | `break-anywhere` → `wrap-anywhere`                         |

Both rules only check tokens and class validity. They do not restrict how you compose or restyle components, so installed components and blocks pass as-is.

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @vital-design/vital-design-lint
```

This adds `vital-design.lint.json` to your project root and installs `@shadcn/lint` and `oxlint` as dev dependencies.

## Configuration

Create `.oxlintrc.json` in your project root, or add these keys to your existing one:

```json
{
  "jsPlugins": ["@shadcn/lint"],
  "extends": ["./vital-design.lint.json"]
}
```

Then run:

```bash
npx oxlint
```

Add it to your `lint` script and CI. For coding agents, add this to `AGENTS.md`:

```md
After making changes, run `npm run lint` and fix all errors.
```

The linter finds your theme and components through `components.json`, which the shadcn CLI already created. You do not need a `settings.shadcn` block unless your setup has no `components.json`. See the [@shadcn/lint settings](https://github.com/shadcn-ui/lint#settings).

## Adding your own rules

Keep `vital-design.lint.json` unchanged so that re-running the install command can update it. Put project rules in your own `.oxlintrc.json`. Rules there override the policy:

```json
{
  "jsPlugins": ["@shadcn/lint"],
  "extends": ["./vital-design.lint.json"],
  "rules": {
    "shadcn/no-unknown-classes": ["error", { "allow": ["not-prose"] }]
  }
}
```

When you override a policy rule, write out its full options. Changing only the severity (for example `"warn"`) drops the options from the policy.

For an intentional one-off exception, add a disable comment with a reason:

```tsx
// oxlint-disable-next-line shadcn/no-raw-colors -- Partner brand color, approved by design.
<span className="bg-amber-400">Sponsor</span>
```

# Your First Component

> Add your first Vittal Design component to a React app.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/getting-started/first-component

## Example: Button

Once installation and Tailwind setup are complete, import a component and use it:

> These examples assume you installed components through the registry and are importing the copied local files generated by your `components.json` aliases.

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';

// shadcn CLI path

export default function App() {
  return (
    <Button
      theme="primary"
      size="lg"
      onClick={() => alert('Hello!')}
    >
      Get Started
    </Button>
  );
}
```

If you are maintaining an existing npm-based integration, import from the package entry instead for the components that are available there:

```tsx
import { Button } from '@fed/vital-design';
```

Newer components may be registry-only until the legacy package distribution is updated.

## Example: Form with Input and Button

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import { Input } from '@/components/ui/Input';
import { useState } from 'react';

export default function LoginForm() {
  const [email, setEmail] = useState('');

  return (
    <form className="flex flex-col gap-4">
      <Input
        placeholder="Enter your email"
        value={email}
        onChange={(event) => setEmail(event.currentTarget.value)}
      />
      <Button theme="primary" size="lg">
        Sign In
      </Button>
    </form>
  );
}
```

## TypeScript Support

Install paths follow the exported file names. Import prop types from the generated local component file when they are re-exported there:

```tsx
import type { InputProps } from '@/components/ui/Input';
```

## Next Steps

- Browse the [Button docs](/docs/components/button) to explore a complete component example
- View [Design Tokens](/docs/design-tokens/colors) to understand the color and spacing system
- Read the [Registry](/docs/registry) guide to install components via the shadcn CLI

# Overview

> Every Vital Design component at a glance. Open a card for its docs, examples, and API.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/components

## Foundation

- [Button](/docs/components/button): Trigger actions with default, text, and ghost variants, multiple themes, and icon support.
- [ButtonGroup](/docs/components/button-group): A composable layout primitive for grouped button controls.
- [Avatar](/docs/components/avatar): Display a user's profile picture with fallback to initials or a default icon, available in 12 color variants.
- [Badge](/docs/components/badge): Small status indicator pill with semantic color variants and number or text content.
- [Chip](/docs/components/chip): A toggleable pill component for filters, tags, and multi-select options.
- [Tag](/docs/components/tag): A label component for categorization, status, and filtering. Supports 12 colors, two variants, and optional remove action.
- [Label](/docs/components/label): Accessible label text associated with a form control.
- [Separator](/docs/components/separator): Horizontal or vertical divider.
- [Skeleton](/docs/components/skeleton): Placeholder blocks for content that is still loading.
- [Spinner](/docs/components/spinner): Loading indicator for pending actions and async content.
- [Icons](/docs/components/icons): Built-in SVG icon set used across Vittal Design components.

## Inputs

- [Field](/docs/components/field): Composable form field layout with labels, descriptions, errors, and groups.
- [Input](/docs/components/input): Text input components including Input, PasswordInput, and Textarea.
- [InputGroup](/docs/components/input-group): A composable input shell for prefixes, suffixes, inline text, and actions around an input or textarea.
- [NumberInput](/docs/components/number-input): A numeric input with stepper buttons, locale-aware formatting, and clamped step interactions.
- [Textarea](/docs/components/textarea): Multi-line text input with consistent border, focus, and disabled states.
- [SearchBar](/docs/components/search-bar): A search input with an icon. Supports instant onChange and explicit onSearch (Enter / icon click).
- [Editable](/docs/components/editable): Inline editable text field with display, input, and textarea parts.
- [Checkbox](/docs/components/checkbox): A checkbox input supporting checked, unchecked, and indeterminate states. Built on Base UI for accessibility.
- [RadioGroup](/docs/components/radio-group): A single-selection group of radio buttons.
- [Switch](/docs/components/switch): A toggle control for boolean on/off settings.
- [Slider](/docs/components/slider): Select a numeric value or range from a bounded scale.

## Pickers and Menus

- [Select](/docs/components/select): A dropdown for choosing one or many options from a flat list.
- [Autocomplete](/docs/components/autocomplete): Free-form text input with filtered suggestions and optional inline completion.
- [Combobox](/docs/components/combobox): An input picker for searching and selecting one or many options.
- [Command](/docs/components/command): A composable command palette primitive built on cmdk, with input, list, items, groups, and shortcut display.
- [DropdownMenu](/docs/components/dropdown-menu): An action menu where each item fires a callback. Use this when items invoke actions rather than bind to a form value.
- [Popover](/docs/components/popover): A floating panel anchored to a trigger element, used for tooltips with rich content, profile cards, and contextual overlays.
- [Calendar](/docs/components/calendar): Date picker calendar built on react-day-picker. Single, range, and multi-select modes with full classNames and components overrides.
- [Time Picker](/docs/components/time-picker): Three-column time picker (hours, minutes, seconds) with click-to-select and CSS scroll-snap.

## Overlays and Feedback

- [Alert](/docs/components/alert): A composable message surface for confirmations, warnings, and contextual notices.
- [Toast](/docs/components/toast): Status-coloured notifications dispatched imperatively from anywhere in the app.
- [Dialog](/docs/components/dialog): A modal surface for focused confirmations, decisions, and short forms.
- [Alert Dialog](/docs/components/alert-dialog): A modal confirmation that interrupts the user and needs a response before they continue.
- [Sheet](/docs/components/sheet): A side-anchored dialog that slides in from any edge — for navigation, filters, forms, and inspectors.
- [Tooltip](/docs/components/tooltip): A short, transient hint anchored to a trigger element with arrow and side controls.

## Layout and Navigation

- [Card](/docs/components/card): Composable card surface with header, title, description, action, content, and footer slots.
- [Tabs](/docs/components/tabs): Switch between related panels with underline or pill tab styles.
- [Breadcrumb](/docs/components/breadcrumb): A trail of links that shows where the current page sits in the site hierarchy.
- [Pagination](/docs/components/pagination): Composable page navigation with page links, first and last controls, and ellipsis.
- [Sidebar](/docs/components/sidebar): Application sidebar with structure, behavior, and a basic neutral default skin. Product-specific looks live on blocks.
- [Table of Contents](/docs/components/table-of-contents): A compact rail of section ticks that expands into the full list of headings on hover or focus.
- [Collapsible](/docs/components/collapsible): An interactive panel that expands and collapses to reveal additional content.
- [Item](/docs/components/item): Content rows with media, title, description, and actions.
- [Table](/docs/components/table): Semantic \<table> primitives with VD tokens for static tables and custom compositions.
- [Toolbar](/docs/components/toolbar): Flex layout primitive with role="toolbar". Lays out actions, separators, and spacers above tables, editors, or panels.
- [SplitButton](/docs/components/split-button): A split action built from ButtonGroup with a primary action and a separate toggle trigger.
- [Progress](/docs/components/progress): Progress primitives and segmented status indicators.
- [Scroll Area](/docs/components/scroll-area): Scrollable viewport with optional edge fade.
- [Resizable](/docs/components/resizable): Accessible resizable panels backed by react-resizable-panels.

# Alert

> A composable message surface for confirmations, warnings, and contextual notices.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/components/alert

## Preview

```tsx
import {
  Alert,
  AlertAction,
  AlertDescription,
  AlertTitle,
} from '@/components/ui/Alert';
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';

export function AlertExample() {
  return (
    <Alert className="w-105 max-w-full">
      <AlertTitle>Request submitted</AlertTitle>
      <AlertDescription>
        The approval flow has started. You can keep editing the draft
        until the reviewer opens it.
      </AlertDescription>
      <AlertAction>
        <Button size="md" variant="text" theme="primary">
          View request
        </Button>
      </AlertAction>
    </Alert>
  );
}
```

## Usage

Compose `AlertTitle`, `AlertDescription`, and an optional `AlertAction` inside `Alert`. The alert fills its container's width; set the width on the parent or with `className`.

## With Icon

Use an icon as the first child when the message needs stronger visual context.

```tsx
import {
  Alert,
  AlertDescription,
  AlertTitle,
} from '@/components/ui/Alert';
import { ClearIcon } from '@/components/icons/ClearIcon';

export function AlertWithIconExample() {
  return (
    <Alert role="status" className="w-105 max-w-full">
      <ClearIcon className="text-destructive-500" />
      <AlertTitle>Payment method expired</AlertTitle>
      <AlertDescription>
        Update the billing card before the next renewal date to avoid
        service interruption.
      </AlertDescription>
    </Alert>
  );
}
```

## With Actions

`AlertAction` aligns its buttons to the end. Put the dismissive action first and the primary action last.

```tsx
import {
  Alert,
  AlertAction,
  AlertDescription,
  AlertTitle,
} from '@/components/ui/Alert';
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';

export function AlertWithActionExample() {
  return (
    <Alert className="w-105 max-w-full">
      <AlertTitle>Delete this draft?</AlertTitle>
      <AlertDescription>
        The draft and its attachments will be removed.
      </AlertDescription>
      <AlertAction>
        <Button size="md" variant="text" theme="default">
          Cancel
        </Button>
        <Button size="md" variant="text" theme="primary">
          Delete
        </Button>
      </AlertAction>
    </Alert>
  );
}
```

## Custom Content

`AlertDescription` can contain additional controls when the notice needs a small follow-up decision.

```tsx
import {
  Alert,
  AlertAction,
  AlertDescription,
  AlertTitle,
} from '@/components/ui/Alert';
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import { Checkbox } from '@/components/ui/Checkbox';
import { Field, FieldLabel } from '@/components/ui/Field';
import { useState } from 'react';

export function AlertWithCustomExample() {
  const [hiddenToday, setHiddenToday] = useState(false);

  return (
    <Alert className="w-105 max-w-full">
      <AlertTitle>Unsaved changes</AlertTitle>
      <AlertDescription>
        Leaving this page will discard the edits in the current form.
        <Field orientation="horizontal" className="mt-4 w-auto">
          <Checkbox
            id="alert-hide-today"
            checked={hiddenToday}
            onCheckedChange={setHiddenToday}
          />
          <FieldLabel htmlFor="alert-hide-today">
            Do not remind me again today
          </FieldLabel>
        </Field>
      </AlertDescription>
      <AlertAction>
        <Button size="md" variant="text" theme="default">
          Cancel
        </Button>
        <Button size="md" variant="text" theme="primary">
          Leave page
        </Button>
      </AlertAction>
    </Alert>
  );
}
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Alert>
  <AlertTitle />
  <AlertDescription />
  <AlertAction />
</Alert>
```

## Props

### Alert

`Alert` accepts native `div` props and renders `role="alert"` by default.

| Prop        | Type            | Default   | Description                                |
| ----------- | --------------- | --------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `role`      | `string`        | `'alert'` | ARIA live-region role for the message      |
| `children`  | `ReactNode`     | -         | Alert content and composed sub-parts       |
| `className` | `string`        | -         | Additional CSS classes on the root element |
| `style`     | `CSSProperties` | -         | Inline styles on the root element          |

### AlertTitle

| Prop        | Type        | Default | Description            |
| ----------- | ----------- | ------- | ---------------------- |
| `children`  | `ReactNode` | -       | Title content          |
| `className` | `string`    | -       | Additional CSS classes |

### AlertDescription

| Prop        | Type        | Default | Description                     |
| ----------- | ----------- | ------- | ------------------------------- |
| `children`  | `ReactNode` | -       | Body copy or supporting content |
| `className` | `string`    | -       | Additional CSS classes          |

### AlertAction

| Prop        | Type        | Default | Description                        |
| ----------- | ----------- | ------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `children`  | `ReactNode` | -       | Action buttons, links, or controls |
| `className` | `string`    | -       | Additional CSS classes             |

## Accessibility

Keep the default `role="alert"` for urgent messages that should be announced immediately. Use `role="status"` for lower-priority confirmations that should not interrupt the current task.

# Alert Dialog

> A modal confirmation that interrupts the user and needs a response before they continue.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/components/alert-dialog

## Preview

```tsx
import {
  AlertDialog,
  AlertDialogBackdrop,
  AlertDialogBody,
  AlertDialogClose,
  AlertDialogDescription,
  AlertDialogFooter,
  AlertDialogHeader,
  AlertDialogMedia,
  AlertDialogPopup,
  AlertDialogPortal,
  AlertDialogTitle,
  AlertDialogTrigger,
  AlertDialogViewport,
} from '@/components/ui/AlertDialog';
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import { CircleExclamationSolidIcon } from '@/components/icons/CircleExclamationSolidIcon';

export function AlertDialogExample() {
  return (
    <AlertDialog>
      <AlertDialogTrigger
        render={<Button theme="dangerous">Delete project</Button>}
      />
      <AlertDialogPortal>
        <AlertDialogBackdrop />
        <AlertDialogViewport>
          <AlertDialogPopup>
            <AlertDialogBody>
              <AlertDialogMedia className="text-warning-500">
                <CircleExclamationSolidIcon />
              </AlertDialogMedia>
              <AlertDialogHeader>
                <AlertDialogTitle>
                  Delete this project?
                </AlertDialogTitle>
                <AlertDialogDescription>
                  The project and its files will be removed for
                  everyone. This can&apos;t be undone.
                </AlertDialogDescription>
              </AlertDialogHeader>
            </AlertDialogBody>
            <AlertDialogFooter>
              <AlertDialogClose
                render={
                  <Button
                    variant="text"
                    size="lg"
                    className="text-grayscale-opacity-600"
                  >
                    Cancel
                  </Button>
                }
              />
              <AlertDialogClose
                render={
                  <Button variant="text" size="lg" theme="alarm">
                    Delete
                  </Button>
                }
              />
            </AlertDialogFooter>
          </AlertDialogPopup>
        </AlertDialogViewport>
      </AlertDialogPortal>
    </AlertDialog>
  );
}
```

## Usage

`AlertDialog` is built on Base UI Alert Dialog. Use it instead of [Dialog](/docs/components/dialog) when the user must answer before continuing, such as confirming a deletion. It renders with `role="alertdialog"` and does not close when the user clicks outside it; it closes from an `AlertDialogClose` action or the Escape key.

Compose the root, trigger, portal, backdrop, viewport, and popup the same way as `Dialog`. Inside the popup, `AlertDialogBody` lays out an optional `AlertDialogMedia` icon next to `AlertDialogHeader`, which holds the title and description. Put the actions in `AlertDialogFooter` as text buttons, with the cancel action first: the first action gets focus when the dialog opens.

The preview uses `Button` and a `CircleExclamationSolidIcon`; add `button` and `icon-circle-exclamation-solid` from the registry as well.

## Message

```tsx
import {
  AlertDialog,
  AlertDialogBackdrop,
  AlertDialogBody,
  AlertDialogClose,
  AlertDialogDescription,
  AlertDialogFooter,
  AlertDialogHeader,
  AlertDialogMedia,
  AlertDialogPopup,
  AlertDialogPortal,
  AlertDialogTitle,
  AlertDialogTrigger,
  AlertDialogViewport,
} from '@/components/ui/AlertDialog';
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import { CircleCheckSolidIcon } from '@/components/icons/CircleCheckSolidIcon';
import { CircleExclamationSolidIcon } from '@/components/icons/CircleExclamationSolidIcon';
import { CircleXmarkSolidIcon } from '@/components/icons/CircleXmarkSolidIcon';
import type { ReactNode } from 'react';

const messages: {
  status: string;
  icon: ReactNode;
  title: string;
  description: string;
}[] = [
  {
    status: 'Warning',
    icon: <CircleExclamationSolidIcon className="text-warning-500" />,
    title: 'Storage almost full',
    description: 'You have used 90% of your workspace storage.',
  },
  {
    status: 'Success',
    icon: <CircleCheckSolidIcon className="text-success-500" />,
    title: 'Import complete',
    description: 'All 128 records were imported.',
  },
  {
    status: 'Error',
    icon: <CircleXmarkSolidIcon className="text-destructive-500" />,
    title: 'Something went wrong',
    description:
      'The report could not be generated. Try again later.',
  },
];

export function AlertDialogMessageExample() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-3">
      {messages.map((message) => (
        <AlertDialog key={message.status}>
          <AlertDialogTrigger
            render={<Button theme="default">{message.status}</Button>}
          />
          <AlertDialogPortal>
            <AlertDialogBackdrop />
            <AlertDialogViewport>
              <AlertDialogPopup>
                <AlertDialogBody>
                  <AlertDialogMedia>{message.icon}</AlertDialogMedia>
                  <AlertDialogHeader>
                    <AlertDialogTitle>
                      {message.title}
                    </AlertDialogTitle>
                    <AlertDialogDescription>
                      {message.description}
                    </AlertDialogDescription>
                  </AlertDialogHeader>
                </AlertDialogBody>
                <AlertDialogFooter>
                  <AlertDialogClose
                    render={
                      <Button
                        variant="text"
                        size="lg"
                        theme="primary"
                      >
                        OK
                      </Button>
                    }
                  />
                </AlertDialogFooter>
              </AlertDialogPopup>
            </AlertDialogViewport>
          </AlertDialogPortal>
        </AlertDialog>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

When the user only needs to acknowledge something, use a single `OK` action. Color the icon with the status: `text-warning-500`, `text-success-500`, or `text-destructive-500`.

## With checkbox

```tsx
import {
  AlertDialog,
  AlertDialogBackdrop,
  AlertDialogBody,
  AlertDialogClose,
  AlertDialogDescription,
  AlertDialogFooter,
  AlertDialogHeader,
  AlertDialogMedia,
  AlertDialogPopup,
  AlertDialogPortal,
  AlertDialogTitle,
  AlertDialogTrigger,
  AlertDialogViewport,
} from '@/components/ui/AlertDialog';
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import { Checkbox } from '@/components/ui/Checkbox';
import { Field, FieldLabel } from '@/components/ui/Field';
import { CircleExclamationSolidIcon } from '@/components/icons/CircleExclamationSolidIcon';
import { useState } from 'react';

export function AlertDialogCheckboxExample() {
  const [skipToday, setSkipToday] = useState(false);

  return (
    <AlertDialog>
      <AlertDialogTrigger
        render={<Button theme="default">Merge items</Button>}
      />
      <AlertDialogPortal>
        <AlertDialogBackdrop />
        <AlertDialogViewport>
          <AlertDialogPopup>
            <AlertDialogBody>
              <AlertDialogMedia className="text-warning-500">
                <CircleExclamationSolidIcon />
              </AlertDialogMedia>
              <AlertDialogHeader>
                <AlertDialogTitle>
                  Merge the selected items?
                </AlertDialogTitle>
                <AlertDialogDescription>
                  Their comments and attachments will be combined into
                  one item.
                </AlertDialogDescription>
                <Field orientation="horizontal" className="mt-2">
                  <Checkbox
                    id="alert-dialog-skip-today"
                    checked={skipToday}
                    onCheckedChange={setSkipToday}
                  />
                  <FieldLabel htmlFor="alert-dialog-skip-today">
                    Don&apos;t ask again today
                  </FieldLabel>
                </Field>
              </AlertDialogHeader>
            </AlertDialogBody>
            <AlertDialogFooter>
              <AlertDialogClose
                render={
                  <Button
                    variant="text"
                    size="lg"
                    className="text-grayscale-opacity-600"
                  >
                    Cancel
                  </Button>
                }
              />
              <AlertDialogClose
                render={
                  <Button variant="text" size="lg" theme="primary">
                    Merge
                  </Button>
                }
              />
            </AlertDialogFooter>
          </AlertDialogPopup>
        </AlertDialogViewport>
      </AlertDialogPortal>
    </AlertDialog>
  );
}
```

Extra controls, such as a "Don't ask again today" checkbox, go in `AlertDialogHeader` below the description.

## Anatomy

```tsx
<AlertDialog>
  <AlertDialogTrigger />
  <AlertDialogPortal>
    <AlertDialogBackdrop />
    <AlertDialogViewport>
      <AlertDialogPopup>
        <AlertDialogBody>
          <AlertDialogMedia />
          <AlertDialogHeader>
            <AlertDialogTitle />
            <AlertDialogDescription />
          </AlertDialogHeader>
        </AlertDialogBody>
        <AlertDialogFooter>
          <AlertDialogClose />
        </AlertDialogFooter>
      </AlertDialogPopup>
    </AlertDialogViewport>
  </AlertDialogPortal>
</AlertDialog>
```

## Props

`AlertDialog` accepts Base UI `AlertDialog.Root` props, including `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange`, and `actionsRef`. Every other part accepts the props of its Base UI part or of a `div`, plus `className`.

### AlertDialogPortal

| Prop          | Type                                                  | Default         | Description                                      |
| ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `container`   | `HTMLElement \| ShadowRoot \| RefObject<...> \| null` | `document.body` | Element the backdrop and popup are portaled into |
| `keepMounted` | `boolean`                                             | `false`         | Keeps the popup in the DOM while it is closed    |

### AlertDialogClose

| Prop     | Type        | Default | Description                                  |
| -------- | ----------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `render` | `ReactNode` | -       | Renders a custom element, such as a `Button` |

## Accessibility

Always include `AlertDialogTitle`; it names the dialog, and `AlertDialogDescription` describes it. `AlertDialogMedia` is hidden from assistive technology, so the title must make sense without the icon. Write action labels that say what happens, such as "Delete" rather than "OK", when the action is destructive.

# Autocomplete

> Free-form text input with filtered suggestions and optional inline completion.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/components/autocomplete

## Preview

```tsx
import {
  Autocomplete,
  AutocompleteClear,
  AutocompleteContent,
  AutocompleteIcon,
  AutocompleteInput,
  AutocompleteInputGroup,
  AutocompleteItem,
  AutocompleteItemText,
  AutocompleteTrigger,
} from '@/components/ui/Autocomplete';

type Tag = {
  id: string;
  value: string;
};

const tags: Tag[] = [
  { id: 't1', value: 'feature' },
  { id: 't2', value: 'fix' },
  { id: 't3', value: 'bug' },
  { id: 't4', value: 'docs' },
  { id: 't5', value: 'internal' },
  { id: 't6', value: 'mobile' },
  { id: 'c-autocomplete', value: 'component: autocomplete' },
  { id: 'c-combobox', value: 'component: combobox' },
  { id: 'c-select', value: 'component: select' },
  { id: 'c-toast', value: 'component: toast' },
  { id: 'c-tooltip', value: 'component: tooltip' },
];

export function AutocompleteExample() {
  return (
    <Autocomplete<Tag>
      items={tags}
      itemToStringValue={(tag) => tag.value}
      openOnInputClick
    >
      <label className="flex w-80 flex-col gap-1 font-sans text-sm leading-5 text-grayscale-opacity-800">
        Search tags
        <AutocompleteInputGroup>
          <AutocompleteIcon />
          <AutocompleteInput placeholder="e.g. feature" />
          <AutocompleteClear />
          <AutocompleteTrigger />
        </AutocompleteInputGroup>
      </label>
      <AutocompleteContent emptyText="No tags found.">
        {(tag: Tag) => (
          <AutocompleteItem key={tag.id} value={tag}>
            <AutocompleteItemText>{tag.value}</AutocompleteItemText>
          </AutocompleteItem>
        )}
      </AutocompleteContent>
    </Autocomplete>
  );
}
```

## Usage

`Autocomplete` is built on Base UI's
[Autocomplete](https://base-ui.com/react/components/autocomplete). Use it
when the user can type any value, with suggestions as assistance. If the
component must remember a selected option as component state, use
`Combobox` instead.

## Modes

The default `mode="list"` filters the suggestion list without changing
the input value. Use `mode="both"` when the highlighted item should also
temporarily complete the text inline.

```tsx
import {
  Autocomplete,
  AutocompleteClear,
  AutocompleteContent,
  AutocompleteIcon,
  AutocompleteInput,
  AutocompleteInputGroup,
  AutocompleteItem,
  AutocompleteTrigger,
} from '@/components/ui/Autocomplete';

type Tag = {
  id: string;
  value: string;
};

const tags: Tag[] = [
  { id: 't1', value: 'feature' },
  { id: 't2', value: 'fix' },
  { id: 't3', value: 'bug' },
  { id: 't4', value: 'docs' },
  { id: 't5', value: 'internal' },
  { id: 't6', value: 'mobile' },
  { id: 'c-autocomplete', value: 'component: autocomplete' },
  { id: 'c-combobox', value: 'component: combobox' },
  { id: 'c-select', value: 'component: select' },
  { id: 'c-toast', value: 'component: toast' },
  { id: 'c-tooltip', value: 'component: tooltip' },
];

export function AutocompleteInlineAutocompleteExample() {
  return (
    <Autocomplete<Tag>
      items={tags}
      itemToStringValue={(tag) => tag.value}
      mode="both"
      openOnInputClick
    >
      <label className="flex w-80 flex-col gap-1 font-sans text-sm leading-5 text-grayscale-opacity-800">
        Search tags
        <AutocompleteInputGroup>
          <AutocompleteIcon />
          <AutocompleteInput placeholder="Type com..." />
          <AutocompleteClear />
          <AutocompleteTrigger />
        </AutocompleteInputGroup>
      </label>
      <AutocompleteContent emptyText="No tags found.">
        {(tag: Tag) => (
          <AutocompleteItem key={tag.id} value={tag}>
            {tag.value}
          </AutocompleteItem>
        )}
      </AutocompleteContent>
    </Autocomplete>
  );
}
```

## Grouped Suggestions

Use grouped `items` with `AutocompleteGroup` and
`AutocompleteGroupLabel` when results need sections.

```tsx
import {
  Autocomplete,
  AutocompleteClear,
  AutocompleteContent,
  AutocompleteGroup,
  AutocompleteGroupLabel,
  AutocompleteIcon,
  AutocompleteInput,
  AutocompleteInputGroup,
  AutocompleteItem,
  AutocompleteTrigger,
} from '@/components/ui/Autocomplete';

type TagGroup = {
  value: string;
  items: string[];
};

const groups: TagGroup[] = [
  {
    value: 'Work',
    items: ['feature', 'fix', 'bug', 'internal'],
  },
  {
    value: 'Components',
    items: ['autocomplete', 'combobox', 'select', 'tooltip'],
  },
];

export function AutocompleteGroupedExample() {
  return (
    <Autocomplete<TagGroup> items={groups} openOnInputClick>
      <label className="flex w-80 flex-col gap-1 font-sans text-sm leading-5 text-grayscale-opacity-800">
        Search grouped tags
        <AutocompleteInputGroup>
          <AutocompleteIcon />
          <AutocompleteInput placeholder="e.g. autocomplete" />
          <AutocompleteClear />
          <AutocompleteTrigger />
        </AutocompleteInputGroup>
      </label>
      <AutocompleteContent emptyText="No tags found.">
        {(group: TagGroup) => (
          <AutocompleteGroup key={group.value} items={group.items}>
            <AutocompleteGroupLabel>
              {group.value}
            </AutocompleteGroupLabel>
            {group.items.map((item) => (
              <AutocompleteItem key={item} value={item}>
                {item}
              </AutocompleteItem>
            ))}
          </AutocompleteGroup>
        )}
      </AutocompleteContent>
    </Autocomplete>
  );
}
```

## Limit Results

Set `limit` to cap the visible matches. `AutocompleteStatus` can add
small helper copy above the result list.

```tsx
import {
  Autocomplete,
  AutocompleteClear,
  AutocompleteContent,
  AutocompleteEmpty,
  AutocompleteIcon,
  AutocompleteInput,
  AutocompleteInputGroup,
  AutocompleteItem,
  AutocompleteList,
  AutocompleteStatus,
  AutocompleteTrigger,
} from '@/components/ui/Autocomplete';

type Tag = {
  id: string;
  value: string;
};

const tags: Tag[] = [
  { id: 't1', value: 'feature' },
  { id: 't2', value: 'fix' },
  { id: 't3', value: 'bug' },
  { id: 't4', value: 'docs' },
  { id: 't5', value: 'internal' },
  { id: 't6', value: 'mobile' },
  { id: 'c-autocomplete', value: 'component: autocomplete' },
  { id: 'c-combobox', value: 'component: combobox' },
  { id: 'c-select', value: 'component: select' },
  { id: 'c-toast', value: 'component: toast' },
  { id: 'c-tooltip', value: 'component: tooltip' },
];

export function AutocompleteLimitedResultsExample() {
  return (
    <Autocomplete<Tag>
      items={tags}
      itemToStringValue={(tag) => tag.value}
      limit={4}
      openOnInputClick
    >
      <label className="flex w-80 flex-col gap-1 font-sans text-sm leading-5 text-grayscale-opacity-800">
        Limit results to 4
        <AutocompleteInputGroup>
          <AutocompleteIcon />
          <AutocompleteInput placeholder="Search tags" />
          <AutocompleteClear />
          <AutocompleteTrigger />
        </AutocompleteInputGroup>
      </label>
      <AutocompleteContent>
        <AutocompleteStatus>
          Keep typing to narrow the result list.
        </AutocompleteStatus>
        <AutocompleteList>
          {(tag: Tag) => (
            <AutocompleteItem key={tag.id} value={tag}>
              {tag.value}
            </AutocompleteItem>
          )}
        </AutocompleteList>
        <AutocompleteEmpty>No tags found.</AutocompleteEmpty>
      </AutocompleteContent>
    </Autocomplete>
  );
}
```

## Command-Like Actions

Autocomplete suggestions can fire `onClick`. This is useful for
free-form command search where the input text remains the main state.
For a full command palette or hierarchical picker, prefer `Command`.

```tsx
import {
  Autocomplete,
  AutocompleteClear,
  AutocompleteContent,
  AutocompleteIcon,
  AutocompleteInput,
  AutocompleteInputGroup,
  AutocompleteItem,
} from '@/components/ui/Autocomplete';
import { useState } from 'react';

const commands = [
  'Create issue',
  'Invite teammate',
  'Archive project',
  'Open settings',
];

export function AutocompleteCommandPickerExample() {
  const [lastCommand, setLastCommand] = useState<string | null>(null);

  return (
    <div className="flex w-80 flex-col gap-2">
      <Autocomplete<string> items={commands} openOnInputClick>
        <AutocompleteInputGroup>
          <AutocompleteIcon />
          <AutocompleteInput placeholder="Run command..." />
          <AutocompleteClear />
        </AutocompleteInputGroup>
        <AutocompleteContent emptyText="No commands found.">
          {(item: string) => (
            <AutocompleteItem
              key={item}
              value={item}
              onClick={() => setLastCommand(item)}
            >
              {item}
            </AutocompleteItem>
          )}
        </AutocompleteContent>
      </Autocomplete>
      {lastCommand ? (
        <p className="text-sm text-grayscale-opacity-600">
          Ran: {lastCommand}
        </p>
      ) : null}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Inline List

Set `inline` and render `AutocompleteList` in place of
`AutocompleteContent` to keep the suggestions visible below the input
instead of in a popup.

```tsx
import {
  Autocomplete,
  AutocompleteClear,
  AutocompleteEmpty,
  AutocompleteIcon,
  AutocompleteInput,
  AutocompleteInputGroup,
  AutocompleteItem,
  AutocompleteList,
} from '@/components/ui/Autocomplete';
import { useState } from 'react';

const commands = [
  'Create issue',
  'Invite teammate',
  'Archive project',
  'Open settings',
];

export function AutocompleteInlineListExample() {
  const [lastCommand, setLastCommand] = useState<string | null>(null);

  return (
    <div className="flex w-80 flex-col gap-2">
      <Autocomplete<string> items={commands} inline>
        <AutocompleteInputGroup>
          <AutocompleteIcon />
          <AutocompleteInput placeholder="Filter inline commands..." />
          <AutocompleteClear />
        </AutocompleteInputGroup>
        <div className="rounded bg-background py-2 shadow-emphasis">
          <AutocompleteList>
            {(item: string) => (
              <AutocompleteItem
                key={item}
                value={item}
                onClick={() => setLastCommand(item)}
              >
                {item}
              </AutocompleteItem>
            )}
          </AutocompleteList>
          <AutocompleteEmpty>No commands found.</AutocompleteEmpty>
        </div>
      </Autocomplete>
      {lastCommand ? (
        <p className="text-sm text-grayscale-opacity-600">
          Ran: {lastCommand}
        </p>
      ) : null}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Submit Search

Use `name` and `submitOnItemClick` for a single-field search form.

```tsx
import {
  Autocomplete,
  AutocompleteClear,
  AutocompleteContent,
  AutocompleteIcon,
  AutocompleteInput,
  AutocompleteInputGroup,
  AutocompleteItem,
  AutocompleteTrigger,
} from '@/components/ui/Autocomplete';
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import { useState } from 'react';

type Tag = {
  id: string;
  value: string;
};

const tags: Tag[] = [
  { id: 't1', value: 'feature' },
  { id: 't2', value: 'fix' },
  { id: 't3', value: 'bug' },
  { id: 't4', value: 'docs' },
  { id: 't5', value: 'internal' },
  { id: 't6', value: 'mobile' },
  { id: 'c-autocomplete', value: 'component: autocomplete' },
  { id: 'c-combobox', value: 'component: combobox' },
  { id: 'c-select', value: 'component: select' },
  { id: 'c-toast', value: 'component: toast' },
  { id: 'c-tooltip', value: 'component: tooltip' },
];

export function AutocompleteSubmitSearchExample() {
  const [query, setQuery] = useState<string | null>(null);

  return (
    <form
      className="flex flex-col gap-3"
      onSubmit={(event) => {
        event.preventDefault();
        const data = new FormData(event.currentTarget);
        const submitted = data.get('query');
        setQuery(typeof submitted === 'string' ? submitted : '');
      }}
    >
      <Autocomplete<Tag> items={tags} name="query" submitOnItemClick>
        <label className="flex w-80 flex-col gap-1 font-sans text-sm leading-5 text-grayscale-opacity-800">
          Search and submit
          <AutocompleteInputGroup>
            <AutocompleteIcon />
            <AutocompleteInput placeholder="Search tags" />
            <AutocompleteClear />
            <AutocompleteTrigger />
          </AutocompleteInputGroup>
        </label>
        <AutocompleteContent emptyText="No tags found.">
          {(tag: Tag) => (
            <AutocompleteItem key={tag.id} value={tag}>
              {tag.value}
            </AutocompleteItem>
          )}
```
