```tsx
        </AutocompleteContent>
      </Autocomplete>
      <Button type="submit">Submit</Button>
      {query !== null ? (
        <p className="text-sm text-grayscale-opacity-600">
          Submitted: {query}
        </p>
      ) : null}
    </form>
  );
}
```

## States

```tsx
import {
  Autocomplete,
  AutocompleteClear,
  AutocompleteContent,
  AutocompleteIcon,
  AutocompleteInput,
  AutocompleteInputGroup,
  AutocompleteItem,
  AutocompleteTrigger,
} from '@/components/ui/Autocomplete';

const tags = ['feature', 'fix', 'bug', 'docs'];

const states = [
  { label: 'Placeholder', props: {} },
  { label: 'With value', props: { defaultValue: 'feature' } },
  {
    label: 'Long value',
    props: {
      defaultValue: 'a long search query that does not fit the input',
    },
  },
  { label: 'Disabled', props: { disabled: true } },
  { label: 'Invalid', props: {}, invalid: true },
];

export function AutocompleteStatesExample() {
  return (
    <div className="grid w-fit grid-cols-[auto_15rem] items-center gap-x-6 gap-y-3 text-sm text-grayscale-opacity-700">
      {states.map(({ label, props, invalid }) => (
        <div key={label} className="contents">
          <span>{label}</span>
          <Autocomplete<string> items={tags} {...props}>
            <AutocompleteInputGroup aria-invalid={invalid}>
              <AutocompleteIcon />
              <AutocompleteInput
                aria-label={`${label} search`}
                placeholder="Search tags"
              />
              <AutocompleteClear />
              <AutocompleteTrigger />
            </AutocompleteInputGroup>
            <AutocompleteContent emptyText="No tags found.">
              {(item: string) => (
                <AutocompleteItem key={item} value={item}>
                  {item}
                </AutocompleteItem>
              )}
            </AutocompleteContent>
          </Autocomplete>
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Props

### Autocomplete

| Prop                | Type                                     | Default  | Description                                     |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `items`             | `readonly Item[] \| grouped items`       | —        | Suggestions used by the render function         |
| `value`             | `string`                                 | —        | Controlled input value                          |
| `defaultValue`      | `string`                                 | —        | Initial uncontrolled input value                |
| `onValueChange`     | `(value, details) => void`               | —        | Called when the input value changes             |
| `mode`              | `'list' \| 'both' \| 'inline' \| 'none'` | `'list'` | Filtering and inline-completion behavior        |
| `autoHighlight`     | `boolean \| 'always'`                    | `false`  | Highlight matching suggestions automatically    |
| `openOnInputClick`  | `boolean`                                | `false`  | Open the popup when the input is clicked        |
| `limit`             | `number`                                 | —        | Maximum visible matches                         |
| `submitOnItemClick` | `boolean`                                | `false`  | Submit the owning form when an item is selected |
| `itemToStringValue` | `(item) => string`                       | —        | Converts object items to input/form text        |

### AutocompleteContent

`AutocompleteContent` is a composite of Portal + Positioner + Popup. Positioning props go to the Positioner; `portalContainer` and `keepMounted` goes to the Portal.

| Prop                    | Type                                                   | Default                        | Description                                           |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `align`                 | `'start' \| 'center' \| 'end'`                         | `'start'`                      | Alignment relative to the anchor                      |
| `alignOffset`           | `number`                                               | `0`                            | Offset along the alignment axis                       |
| `side`                  | `'top' \| 'right' \| 'bottom' \| 'left' \| …`          | `'bottom'`                     | Preferred side of the anchor                          |
| `sideOffset`            | `number`                                               | `4`                            | Distance from the anchor                              |
| `emptyText`             | `ReactNode`                                            | —                              | Empty state content                                   |
| `listClassName`         | `string`                                               | —                              | Classes for the list element                          |
| `positionerClassName`   | `string`                                               | —                              | Classes on the Positioner wrapper                     |
| `anchor`                | `RefObject \| Element \| …`                            | —                              | Custom positioning anchor (defaults to the trigger)   |
| `arrowPadding`          | `number`                                               | `5`                            | Minimum space between the arrow and the popup's edges |
| `collisionAvoidance`    | `{ side?, align?, fallbackAxisSide? }`                 | `{ fallbackAxisSide: 'none' }` | How the popup flips or shifts to avoid collisions     |
| `collisionBoundary`     | `'clipping-ancestors' \| Element \| Element[] \| Rect` | `'clipping-ancestors'`         | Area the popup is kept inside                         |
| `collisionPadding`      | `number \| { top?, right?, bottom?, left? }`           | `5`                            | Space kept from the edge of the collision boundary    |
| `disableAnchorTracking` | `boolean`                                              | `false`                        | Stop following layout shifts of the anchor            |
| `positionMethod`        | `'absolute' \| 'fixed'`                                | `'absolute'`                   | CSS `position` of the positioner                      |
| `sticky`                | `boolean`                                              | `false`                        | Keep the popup in view after the anchor scrolls out   |
| `portalContainer`       | `HTMLElement \| ShadowRoot \| RefObject \| null`       | —                              | Custom portal container (defaults to `document.body`) |
| `keepMounted`           | `boolean`                                              | `false`                        | Keep the popup in the DOM while closed                |

### Parts

| Part                     | Description                                                |
| ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Autocomplete`           | Root; manages input value, filtering, popup, and highlight |
| `AutocompleteInputGroup` | Styled input shell                                         |
| `AutocompleteInput`      | Native input connected to autocomplete behavior            |
| `AutocompleteIcon`       | Search icon slot                                           |
| `AutocompleteClear`      | Clears the input value                                     |
| `AutocompleteTrigger`    | Opens or closes the popup                                  |
| `AutocompleteContent`    | Preset portal + positioner + popup + optional list wrapper |
| `AutocompleteList`       | Scrollable list primitive                                  |
| `AutocompleteItem`       | Highlightable suggestion row                               |
| `AutocompleteItemText`   | Text slot inside an item                                   |
| `AutocompleteEmpty`      | Empty state                                                |
| `AutocompleteStatus`     | Status/helper row                                          |
| `AutocompleteGroup`      | Suggestion group                                           |
| `AutocompleteGroupLabel` | Label for a suggestion group                               |
| `AutocompletePortal`     | Lower-level portal                                         |
| `AutocompletePositioner` | Lower-level floating positioner                            |
| `AutocompletePopup`      | Lower-level popup surface                                  |

# Avatar

> Display a user's profile picture with fallback to initials or a default icon, available in 12 color variants.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/components/avatar

## Preview

```tsx
import { Avatar } from '@/components/ui/Avatar';

export function AvatarExample() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-4">
      <Avatar src="/images/ray.jpg" alt="Ray" name="Ray" size="lg" />
      <Avatar name="Arthur Lu" color="blue" size="lg" />
      <Avatar name="Sean Chen" color="tiffany" size="lg" />
      <Avatar size="lg" />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Usage

When `src` is provided, the image is displayed. While it loads, or if it fails, the avatar shows `fallback`, the initials from `name`, or a default icon.

## Sizes

```tsx
import { Avatar } from '@/components/ui/Avatar';

export function AvatarAllSizesExample() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-4">
      <Avatar size="xs" alt="Extra small" />
      <Avatar size="sm" alt="Small" />
      <Avatar size="md" alt="Medium" />
      <Avatar size="lg" alt="Large" />
      <Avatar size="xl" alt="Extra large" />
    </div>
  );
}
```

| Size | Dimensions           |
| ---- | -------------------- |
| `xs` | 24 × 24 px           |
| `sm` | 32 × 32 px           |
| `md` | 40 × 40 px (default) |
| `lg` | 48 × 48 px           |
| `xl` | 60 × 60 px           |

## Color Variants

```tsx
import { Avatar } from '@/components/ui/Avatar';

const colors = [
  'default',
  'tiffany',
  'green',
  'orange',
  'pink',
  'blue',
  'sky',
  'purple',
  'light-gold',
  'salmon',
  'ice',
  'lavender',
] as const;

export function AvatarColorsExample() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-4">
      {colors.map((color) => (
        <Avatar key={color} color={color} alt={color} />
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Fallback

Without `fallback` or `name`, the avatar shows the default person icon. `fallback` takes precedence over `name`. With only `name`, the avatar shows the first letters of up to two words.

```tsx
import { Avatar } from '@/components/ui/Avatar';

export function AvatarFallbackExample() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-start gap-8 text-xs text-grayscale-opacity-600">
      <figure className="flex flex-col items-center gap-2">
        <Avatar />
        <figcaption>Default icon</figcaption>
      </figure>
      <figure className="flex flex-col items-center gap-2">
        <Avatar name="Vittal Design" fallback="BZ" />
        <figcaption>fallback</figcaption>
      </figure>
      <figure className="flex flex-col items-center gap-2">
        <Avatar name="Vittal Design" />
        <figcaption>name only</figcaption>
      </figure>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Group

Use `AvatarGroup` to stack multiple avatars. Add `AvatarGroupCount` at the end when the list is truncated.

```tsx
import {
  Avatar,
  AvatarGroup,
  AvatarGroupCount,
} from '@/components/ui/Avatar';

export function AvatarGroupExample() {
  return (
    <AvatarGroup>
      <Avatar color="green" name="Arthur Lu" />
      <Avatar color="blue" name="Dover Shen" />
      <Avatar color="ice" name="Luka Jung" />
      <AvatarGroupCount>+3</AvatarGroupCount>
    </AvatarGroup>
  );
}
```

## Compound Parts

Use `AvatarRoot`, `AvatarImage`, and `AvatarFallback` when you need full control over the image and fallback content. The second avatar's image fails to load, so its fallback shows.

```tsx
import {
  AvatarFallback,
  AvatarImage,
  AvatarRoot,
} from '@/components/ui/Avatar';

export function AvatarCompoundExample() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-4">
      <AvatarRoot color="blue" size="lg">
        <AvatarImage src="/images/ray.jpg" alt="Ray" />
        <AvatarFallback color="blue">RA</AvatarFallback>
      </AvatarRoot>
      <AvatarRoot color="tiffany" size="lg">
        <AvatarFallback color="tiffany">SC</AvatarFallback>
      </AvatarRoot>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Bordered

`bordered` is `true` by default. Set `bordered={false}` to remove the colored border ring.

```tsx
import { Avatar } from '@/components/ui/Avatar';

export function AvatarBorderExample() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-4">
      <Avatar bordered={false} />
      <Avatar />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Disabled

```tsx
import { Avatar } from '@/components/ui/Avatar';

export function AvatarDisabledExample() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-4">
      <Avatar size="xs" disabled alt="Disabled avatar" />
      <Avatar size="sm" disabled alt="Disabled avatar" />
      <Avatar size="md" disabled alt="Disabled avatar" />
      <Avatar size="lg" disabled alt="Disabled avatar" />
      <Avatar size="xl" disabled alt="Disabled avatar" />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Props

| Prop                    | Type                                                                                                                                        | Default     | Description                                     |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `name`                  | `string`                                                                                                                                    | —           | Used to generate initials fallback              |
| `src`                   | `string`                                                                                                                                    | —           | Image URL; falls back to initials if load fails |
| `alt`                   | `string`                                                                                                                                    | —           | Alt text for the image                          |
| `size`                  | `'xs' \| 'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg' \| 'xl'`                                                                                                      | `'md'`      | Avatar dimensions                               |
| `color`                 | `'default' \| 'tiffany' \| 'green' \| 'orange' \| 'pink' \| 'blue' \| 'sky' \| 'purple' \| 'light-gold' \| 'salmon' \| 'ice' \| 'lavender'` | `'default'` | Background and text color variant               |
| `bordered`              | `boolean`                                                                                                                                   | `true`      | Adds a colored border ring                      |
| `disabled`              | `boolean`                                                                                                                                   | `false`     | Applies disabled overlay                        |
| `fallback`              | `ReactNode`                                                                                                                                 | —           | Custom fallback element                         |
| `onClick`               | `(event: MouseEvent) => void`                                                                                                               | —           | Click handler                                   |
| `onLoadingStatusChange` | `(status: 'idle' \| 'loading' \| 'loaded' \| 'error') => void`                                                                              | —           | Image load status callback                      |
| `style`                 | `CSSProperties`                                                                                                                             | —           | Inline styles                                   |
| `className`             | `string`                                                                                                                                    | —           | Root element class name                         |

## AvatarGroup Props

| Prop        | Type            | Default | Description                |
| ----------- | --------------- | ------- | -------------------------- |
| `children`  | `ReactNode`     | —       | Avatar items and count     |
| `className` | `string`        | —       | Additional CSS classes     |
| `style`     | `CSSProperties` | —       | Inline styles              |
| `...props`  | `div` props     | —       | Native div props forwarded |

## AvatarGroupCount Props

| Prop        | Type            | Default | Description                |
| ----------- | --------------- | ------- | -------------------------- |
| `children`  | `ReactNode`     | —       | Count label or icon        |
| `className` | `string`        | —       | Additional CSS classes     |
| `style`     | `CSSProperties` | —       | Inline styles              |
| `...props`  | `div` props     | —       | Native div props forwarded |

# Badge

> Small status indicator pill with semantic color variants and number or text content.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/components/badge

## Preview

```tsx
import { Badge } from '@/components/ui/Badge';

export function BadgeExample() {
  return <Badge>9</Badge>;
}
```

## Variants

Each column shows one `variant` in every size and type: `lg` number, `lg` text, `md` number, `md` text, and the `sm` dot.

```tsx
import { Badge } from '@/components/ui/Badge';

const variants = [
  'primary',
  'success',
  'warning',
  'destructive',
  'info',
] as const;

export function BadgeAllVariantsExample() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-10">
      {variants.map((variant) => (
        <div
          key={variant}
          className="flex flex-col items-start gap-3"
        >
          <span className="text-xs text-grayscale-opacity-600">
            {variant}
          </span>
          <Badge size="lg" type="number" variant={variant}>
            9
          </Badge>
          <Badge size="lg" type="text" variant={variant}>
            New
          </Badge>
          <Badge size="md" type="number" variant={variant}>
            9
          </Badge>
          <Badge size="md" type="text" variant={variant}>
            New
          </Badge>
          <Badge size="sm" variant={variant} />
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Sizes

`lg` is the default. `md` is a smaller pill. `sm` renders an empty dot and ignores `children`.

```tsx
import { Badge } from '@/components/ui/Badge';

export function BadgeDotExample() {
  return <Badge size="sm" />;
}
```

## Type: Number vs Text

`type="number"` (default) suits counts. `type="text"` adjusts padding and font size for short words.

```tsx
import { Badge } from '@/components/ui/Badge';

export function BadgeTextExample() {
  return <Badge type="text">New</Badge>;
}
```

## Props

| Prop        | Type                                                             | Default     | Description                          |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `variant`   | `'primary' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'destructive' \| 'info'` | `'primary'` | Color variant                        |
| `size`      | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'`                                           | `'lg'`      | Badge size; `sm` is an empty dot     |
| `type`      | `'number' \| 'text'`                                             | `'number'`  | Adjusts padding/typography for label |
| `children`  | `ReactNode`                                                      | —           | Badge content (ignored when `sm`)    |
| `className` | `string`                                                         | —           | Additional CSS classes               |
| `style`     | `CSSProperties`                                                  | —           | Inline styles                        |

# Breadcrumb

> A trail of links that shows where the current page sits in the site hierarchy.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/components/breadcrumb

## Preview

```tsx
import {
  Breadcrumb,
  BreadcrumbEllipsis,
  BreadcrumbItem,
  BreadcrumbLink,
  BreadcrumbList,
  BreadcrumbPage,
  BreadcrumbSeparator,
} from '@/components/ui/Breadcrumb';
import {
  DropdownMenu,
  DropdownMenuContent,
  DropdownMenuItem,
  DropdownMenuTrigger,
} from '@/components/ui/DropdownMenu';

export function BreadcrumbExample() {
  return (
    <Breadcrumb>
      <BreadcrumbList>
        <BreadcrumbItem>
          <BreadcrumbLink href="#projects">Projects</BreadcrumbLink>
        </BreadcrumbItem>
        <BreadcrumbSeparator />
        <BreadcrumbItem>
          <DropdownMenu>
            <DropdownMenuTrigger
              render={
                <BreadcrumbLink
                  render={<button type="button" />}
                  aria-label="Show hidden pages"
                  className="inline-flex items-center data-[popup-open]:text-primary-400"
                />
              }
            >
              <BreadcrumbEllipsis className="text-inherit" />
            </DropdownMenuTrigger>
            <DropdownMenuContent align="start" sideOffset={10}>
              <DropdownMenuItem render={<a href="#website" />}>
                Website
              </DropdownMenuItem>
              <DropdownMenuItem render={<a href="#analytics" />}>
                Analytics
              </DropdownMenuItem>
            </DropdownMenuContent>
          </DropdownMenu>
        </BreadcrumbItem>
        <BreadcrumbSeparator />
        <BreadcrumbItem>
          <BreadcrumbLink href="#reports">Reports</BreadcrumbLink>
        </BreadcrumbItem>
        <BreadcrumbSeparator />
        <BreadcrumbItem>
          <BreadcrumbPage>Settings</BreadcrumbPage>
        </BreadcrumbItem>
      </BreadcrumbList>
    </Breadcrumb>
  );
}
```

## Usage

Use `BreadcrumbPage` for the current page. It is not a link and sets `aria-current="page"`.

The hidden levels open in a [`DropdownMenu`](/docs/components/dropdown-menu), so add `dropdown-menu` from the registry too. On a short path, drop the ellipsis and list every level.

## Router Links

`BreadcrumbLink` renders `<a>` by default. Pass your router's link through `render`:

```tsx
import { Link } from 'react-router-dom';

<BreadcrumbLink render={<Link to="/projects" />}>
  Projects
</BreadcrumbLink>;
```

## Sizes

Set `size` on `BreadcrumbList`. The default is `sm`.

```tsx
import {
  Breadcrumb,
  BreadcrumbItem,
  BreadcrumbLink,
  BreadcrumbList,
  BreadcrumbPage,
  BreadcrumbSeparator,
} from '@/components/ui/Breadcrumb';

export function BreadcrumbSizesExample() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-6">
      {(['lg', 'sm'] as const).map((size) => (
        <Breadcrumb key={size}>
          <BreadcrumbList size={size}>
            <BreadcrumbItem>
              <BreadcrumbLink href="#projects">
                Projects
              </BreadcrumbLink>
            </BreadcrumbItem>
            <BreadcrumbSeparator />
            <BreadcrumbItem>
              <BreadcrumbLink href="#reports">Reports</BreadcrumbLink>
            </BreadcrumbItem>
            <BreadcrumbSeparator />
            <BreadcrumbItem>
              <BreadcrumbPage>Settings</BreadcrumbPage>
            </BreadcrumbItem>
          </BreadcrumbList>
        </Breadcrumb>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Collapsed Items

Use `BreadcrumbEllipsis` in place of the levels you hide on a deep path.

```tsx
import {
  Breadcrumb,
  BreadcrumbEllipsis,
  BreadcrumbItem,
  BreadcrumbLink,
  BreadcrumbList,
  BreadcrumbPage,
  BreadcrumbSeparator,
} from '@/components/ui/Breadcrumb';

export function BreadcrumbCollapsedExample() {
  return (
    <Breadcrumb>
      <BreadcrumbList>
        <BreadcrumbItem>
          <BreadcrumbLink href="#projects">Projects</BreadcrumbLink>
        </BreadcrumbItem>
        <BreadcrumbSeparator />
        <BreadcrumbItem>
          <BreadcrumbEllipsis />
        </BreadcrumbItem>
        <BreadcrumbSeparator />
        <BreadcrumbItem>
          <BreadcrumbLink href="#reports">Reports</BreadcrumbLink>
        </BreadcrumbItem>
        <BreadcrumbSeparator />
        <BreadcrumbItem>
          <BreadcrumbPage>Settings</BreadcrumbPage>
        </BreadcrumbItem>
      </BreadcrumbList>
    </Breadcrumb>
  );
}
```

## Dropdown

Put `BreadcrumbEllipsis` inside a [`DropdownMenu`](/docs/components/dropdown-menu) trigger to open the levels you hid.

Render the trigger as a `BreadcrumbLink` with `render={<button type="button" />}`, so it keeps the link's color, hover, and focus styles. `BreadcrumbEllipsis` only announces "More", so give the trigger a name that says what it opens. Render each hidden level as a link.

```tsx
import {
  Breadcrumb,
  BreadcrumbEllipsis,
  BreadcrumbItem,
  BreadcrumbLink,
  BreadcrumbList,
  BreadcrumbPage,
  BreadcrumbSeparator,
} from '@/components/ui/Breadcrumb';
import {
  DropdownMenu,
  DropdownMenuContent,
  DropdownMenuItem,
  DropdownMenuTrigger,
} from '@/components/ui/DropdownMenu';

export function BreadcrumbDropdownExample() {
  return (
    <Breadcrumb>
      <BreadcrumbList>
        <BreadcrumbItem>
          <BreadcrumbLink href="#projects">Projects</BreadcrumbLink>
        </BreadcrumbItem>
        <BreadcrumbSeparator />
        <BreadcrumbItem>
          <DropdownMenu>
            <DropdownMenuTrigger
              render={
                <BreadcrumbLink
                  render={<button type="button" />}
                  aria-label="Show hidden pages"
                  className="inline-flex items-center data-[popup-open]:text-primary-400"
                />
              }
            >
              <BreadcrumbEllipsis className="text-inherit" />
            </DropdownMenuTrigger>
            <DropdownMenuContent align="start" sideOffset={10}>
              <DropdownMenuItem render={<a href="#website" />}>
                Website
              </DropdownMenuItem>
              <DropdownMenuItem render={<a href="#analytics" />}>
                Analytics
              </DropdownMenuItem>
            </DropdownMenuContent>
          </DropdownMenu>
        </BreadcrumbItem>
        <BreadcrumbSeparator />
        <BreadcrumbItem>
          <BreadcrumbPage>Settings</BreadcrumbPage>
        </BreadcrumbItem>
      </BreadcrumbList>
    </Breadcrumb>
  );
}
```

## Parts

| Part                  | Element | Description                                                                                                       |
| --------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Breadcrumb`          | `nav`   | Navigation landmark. `aria-label` defaults to `breadcrumb`                                                        |
| `BreadcrumbList`      | `ol`    | Ordered list of levels. Takes `size`: `'sm'` (default) or `'lg'`                                                  |
| `BreadcrumbItem`      | `li`    | One level                                                                                                         |
| `BreadcrumbLink`      | `a`     | Link to a parent level. Takes `render` for router links                                                           |
| `BreadcrumbPage`      | `span`  | Current page, with `aria-current="page"`                                                                          |
| `BreadcrumbSeparator` | `li`    | Divider between levels. Pass `children` to replace the chevron                                                    |
| `BreadcrumbEllipsis`  | `span`  | Marks hidden levels. Pass `children` to replace the icon. Put it in a `DropdownMenu` trigger to open those levels |

Each part also accepts the props of its element.

# Button

> Trigger actions with default, text, and ghost variants, multiple themes, and icon support.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/components/button

## Preview

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';

export function ButtonExample() {
  return (
    <Button theme="primary" size="lg">
      Button
    </Button>
  );
}
```

## Usage

Pick a `variant` for the emphasis and a `theme` for the color. Put icons and
spinners in as children; the label sizes are `md` and `lg`.

## Variants

### Default

The `default` variant renders a solid background button. It is the
default rendering style. Each column shows one theme at `lg` and `md`,
enabled and disabled.

```tsx
import {
  Button,
  type DefaultButtonProps,
} from '@/components/ui/Button';

const themes: {
  theme: DefaultButtonProps['theme'];
  label: string;
}[] = [
  { theme: 'primary', label: 'Primary' },
  { theme: 'default', label: 'Default' },
  { theme: 'success', label: 'Success' },
  { theme: 'info', label: 'Info' },
  { theme: 'warning', label: 'Warning' },
  { theme: 'alarm', label: 'Alarm' },
  { theme: 'dangerous', label: 'Dangerous' },
];

export function ButtonDefaultButtonExample() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-5">
      {themes.map(({ theme, label }) => (
        <div
          key={theme}
          className="grid grid-rows-4 justify-items-center gap-5"
        >
          <Button variant="default" theme={theme} size="lg">
            {label}
          </Button>
          <Button variant="default" theme={theme} size="md">
            {label}
          </Button>
          <Button variant="default" theme={theme} size="lg" disabled>
            {label}
          </Button>
          <Button variant="default" theme={theme} size="md" disabled>
            {label}
          </Button>
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Text

The `text` variant renders a transparent background button. Available for all themes except `dangerous`.

```tsx
import {
  Button,
  type TextButtonProps,
} from '@/components/ui/Button';

const themes: { theme: TextButtonProps['theme']; label: string }[] = [
  { theme: 'primary', label: 'Primary' },
  { theme: 'default', label: 'Default' },
  { theme: 'success', label: 'Success' },
  { theme: 'info', label: 'Info' },
  { theme: 'warning', label: 'Warning' },
  { theme: 'alarm', label: 'Alarm' },
];

export function ButtonTextButtonExample() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-5">
      {themes.map(({ theme, label }) => (
        <div
          key={theme}
          className="grid grid-rows-4 justify-items-center gap-5"
        >
          <Button variant="text" theme={theme} size="lg">
            {label}
          </Button>
          <Button variant="text" theme={theme} size="md">
            {label}
          </Button>
          <Button variant="text" theme={theme} size="lg" disabled>
            {label}
          </Button>
          <Button variant="text" theme={theme} size="md" disabled>
            {label}
          </Button>
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Ghost

The `ghost` variant renders a transparent button that surfaces a
background on hover. Use it inside popovers, toolbars, and split-button
menus where the surrounding chrome provides the affordance.

```tsx
import {
  Button,
  type GhostButtonProps,
} from '@/components/ui/Button';

const themes: { theme: GhostButtonProps['theme']; label: string }[] =
  [
    { theme: 'primary', label: 'Primary' },
    { theme: 'default', label: 'Default' },
    { theme: 'success', label: 'Success' },
    { theme: 'info', label: 'Info' },
    { theme: 'warning', label: 'Warning' },
    { theme: 'alarm', label: 'Alarm' },
  ];

export function ButtonGhostButtonExample() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-5">
      {themes.map(({ theme, label }) => (
        <div
          key={theme}
          className="grid grid-rows-4 justify-items-center gap-5"
        >
          <Button variant="ghost" theme={theme} size="lg">
            {label}
          </Button>
          <Button variant="ghost" theme={theme} size="md">
            {label}
          </Button>
          <Button variant="ghost" theme={theme} size="lg" disabled>
            {label}
          </Button>
          <Button variant="ghost" theme={theme} size="md" disabled>
            {label}
          </Button>
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Sizes

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';

export function ButtonSizesExample() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-5">
      <Button size="md" theme="primary">
        Medium
      </Button>
      <Button size="lg" theme="primary">
        Large
      </Button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Icons

Use `data-icon="inline-start"` or `data-icon="inline-end"` on child icons.
Install or import the icon or spinner separately from the button.

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import { AngleDownIcon } from '@/components/icons/AngleDownIcon';
import { FlagIcon } from '@/components/icons/FlagIcon';
import { MagnifyingGlassIcon } from '@/components/icons/MagnifyingGlassIcon';

export function ButtonWithIconsExample() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-5">
      <Button theme="primary">
        <FlagIcon data-icon="inline-start" />
        New Branch
      </Button>
      <Button theme="default">
        Download
        <AngleDownIcon data-icon="inline-end" />
      </Button>
      <Button variant="text" theme="primary">
        Search
        <MagnifyingGlassIcon data-icon="inline-end" />
      </Button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Icon Only

For icon-only buttons, use `size="icon-md"` or `size="icon-lg"` and give the
button an `aria-label`.

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import { AngleUpIcon } from '@/components/icons/AngleUpIcon';
import { MagnifyingGlassIcon } from '@/components/icons/MagnifyingGlassIcon';
import { XmarkIcon } from '@/components/icons/XmarkIcon';

export function ButtonIconOnlyExample() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-5">
      <Button size="icon-md" theme="default" aria-label="Close">
        <XmarkIcon data-icon="inline-start" />
      </Button>
      <Button size="icon-md" theme="primary" aria-label="Search">
        <MagnifyingGlassIcon data-icon="inline-start" />
      </Button>
      <Button size="icon-lg" theme="primary" aria-label="Expand">
        <AngleUpIcon data-icon="inline-start" />
      </Button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Loading State

Render a spinner as a child icon and disable the button while work is in flight.

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import { Spinner } from '@/components/ui/Spinner';

export function ButtonLoadingWithSpinnerExample() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-5">
      <Button theme="primary" disabled>
        <Spinner data-icon="inline-start" />
        Saving
      </Button>
      <Button theme="default" disabled>
        Loading
        <Spinner data-icon="inline-end" />
      </Button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### States

Disable a button with `disabled`. Add `focusableWhenDisabled` to keep it in the
tab order, for example when a tooltip explains why it is disabled.

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';

const variants = [
  { variant: 'default', label: 'Default' },
  { variant: 'text', label: 'Text' },
  { variant: 'ghost', label: 'Ghost' },
] as const;

const states = [
  { label: 'Enabled', props: {} },
  { label: 'Disabled', props: { disabled: true } },
];

export function ButtonStatesExample() {
  return (
    <div className="inline-grid grid-cols-[auto_repeat(3,auto)] items-center justify-items-start gap-x-6 gap-y-3 text-sm text-grayscale-opacity-700">
      <span />
      {variants.map(({ variant, label }) => (
        <span key={variant}>{label}</span>
      ))}
      {states.map(({ label, props }) => (
        <div key={label} className="contents">
          <span>{label}</span>
          {variants.map(({ variant }) => (
            <Button
              key={variant}
              variant={variant}
              theme="primary"
              {...props}
            >
              Button
            </Button>
          ))}
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Link

Use `LinkButton` for navigation that should look like a button. It renders an
`<a>` with the same variants, themes, and sizes, and keeps link semantics, so
screen readers announce it as a link and `getByRole('link')` finds it.

Do not use `<Button nativeButton={false} render={<a />}>` for links: Base UI
adds `role="button"` to every non-`<button>` element.

```tsx
import { LinkButton } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import { AngleRightIcon } from '@/components/icons/AngleRightIcon';

export function ButtonLinkExample() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-5">
      <LinkButton href="#login" size="lg">
        Log in
      </LinkButton>
      <LinkButton href="#docs" theme="default">
        Docs
      </LinkButton>
      <LinkButton href="#more" variant="text" theme="primary">
        Learn more
        <AngleRightIcon data-icon="inline-end" />
      </LinkButton>
    </div>
  );
}
```

For router links, pass the link element through `render`:

```tsx
import { LinkButton } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import Link from 'next/link';

<LinkButton render={<Link href="/login" />}>Log in</LinkButton>;
```

## Props

### Button

| Prop                    | Type                                                                                   | Default                                       | Description                                                      |
| ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `variant`               | `'default' \| 'text' \| 'ghost'`                                                       | `'default'`                                   | Visual variant                                                   |
| `theme`                 | `'primary' \| 'default' \| 'success' \| 'info' \| 'warning' \| 'alarm' \| 'dangerous'` | `'primary'` for default, `'default'` for text | Color theme (`'dangerous'` only available on `default`)          |
| `size`                  | `'md' \| 'lg' \| 'icon-md' \| 'icon-lg'`                                               | `'md'`                                        | Button size                                                      |
| `focusableWhenDisabled` | `boolean`                                                                              | `false`                                       | Keeps the button focusable even when disabled styling is applied |
| `disabled`              | `boolean`                                                                              | `false`                                       | Native disabled attribute                                        |
| `className`             | `string`                                                                               | —                                             | Classes for the `<button>` itself                                |
| `contentClassName`      | `string`                                                                               | —                                             | Classes for the inner content wrapper (see below)                |
| `style`                 | `CSSProperties`                                                                        | —                                             | Inline styles                                                    |

### LinkButton

Accepts `variant`, `theme`, `size`, `className`, and `contentClassName` like
`Button`, plus every `<a>` attribute and `render`. It has no `disabled` prop,
because links cannot be disabled. Render plain text or a `Button` instead. The
root uses `data-slot="link-button"` and the content wrapper uses
`data-slot="link-button-content"`.

### Laying out the content

`Button` wraps its children in a `span[data-slot="button-content"]` that centres
the icon and label and keeps them on one line. Since that span is the button's
only child, flex utilities written on the button itself have nothing to
distribute — use `contentClassName` to reach the wrapper instead of selecting
into it with `[&>span]:*`.

```tsx
// Icon on the left, count pushed to the right, label allowed to wrap
<Button contentClassName="w-full justify-between whitespace-normal">
  <FlagIcon data-icon="inline-start" />
  Reported issues
  <span>12</span>
</Button>
```

Colour, size, radius, and hover states stay owned by the theme — passing those
through `className` will not override the variant. The button also sets
`overflow-hidden` for its hover overlay, so a child positioned outside the
button box (a notification badge at `-top-1 -right-1`) needs
`className="overflow-visible"` on the button.

# ButtonGroup

> A composable layout primitive for grouped button controls.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/components/button-group

## Preview

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import { ButtonGroup } from '@/components/ui/ButtonGroup';

export function ButtonGroupExample() {
  return (
    <ButtonGroup>
      <Button theme="default">Save</Button>
      <Button theme="default">More</Button>
    </ButtonGroup>
  );
}
```

## Usage

Wrap `Button`s in `ButtonGroup` to join them into one control. The group only
handles layout; each button keeps its own `variant`, `theme`, and `size`.

## With Separator

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import {
  ButtonGroup,
  ButtonGroupSeparator,
} from '@/components/ui/ButtonGroup';

export function ButtonGroupWithSeparatorExample() {
  return (
    <ButtonGroup>
      <Button theme="default">Archive</Button>
      <ButtonGroupSeparator />
      <Button theme="default">Snooze</Button>
    </ButtonGroup>
  );
}
```

## With Text

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import {
  ButtonGroup,
  ButtonGroupText,
} from '@/components/ui/ButtonGroup';

export function ButtonGroupWithTextExample() {
  return (
    <ButtonGroup>
      <ButtonGroupText>Status</ButtonGroupText>
      <Button theme="default">Publish</Button>
    </ButtonGroup>
  );
}
```

## Vertical

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import { ButtonGroup } from '@/components/ui/ButtonGroup';

export function ButtonGroupVerticalExample() {
  return (
    <ButtonGroup orientation="vertical" className="w-40">
      <Button theme="default">Action A</Button>
      <Button theme="default">Action B</Button>
    </ButtonGroup>
  );
}
```

## Nested

A nested group stays joined inside, and is spaced apart from its siblings.

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import { ButtonGroup } from '@/components/ui/ButtonGroup';

export function ButtonGroupNestedExample() {
  return (
    <ButtonGroup>
      <ButtonGroup>
        <Button theme="default">Back</Button>
        <Button theme="default">Next</Button>
      </ButtonGroup>
      <Button>Submit</Button>
    </ButtonGroup>
  );
}
```

## Props

### ButtonGroup

| Prop          | Type                         | Default        | Description            |
| ------------- | ---------------------------- | -------------- | ---------------------- |
| `orientation` | `'horizontal' \| 'vertical'` | `'horizontal'` | Layout direction       |
| `className`   | `string`                     | —              | Additional CSS classes |
| `style`       | `CSSProperties`              | —              | Inline styles          |

### ButtonGroupSeparator

| Prop          | Type                         | Default | Description            |
| ------------- | ---------------------------- | ------- | ---------------------- |
| `orientation` | `'horizontal' \| 'vertical'` | auto    | Separator direction    |
| `...props`    | `SeparatorProps`             | —       | Shared separator props |

# Calendar

> Date picker calendar built on react-day-picker. Single, range, and multi-select modes with full classNames and components overrides.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/components/calendar

## Preview

```tsx
import { Calendar } from '@/components/ui/Calendar';
import { useState } from 'react';

export function CalendarExample() {
  const [date, setDate] = useState<Date | undefined>(
    new Date(2026, 0, 1),
  );

  return (
    <Calendar
      mode="single"
      defaultMonth={new Date(2026, 0)}
      selected={date}
      onSelect={setDate}
    />
  );
}
```

## Usage

Control the selection with `selected` and `onSelect`; their shape follows `mode`. The calendar opens on the current month. Pass `defaultMonth` to open on another one.

## Range Selection

```tsx
import { Calendar } from '@/components/ui/Calendar';
import { useState } from 'react';
import type { DateRange } from 'react-day-picker';

export function CalendarRangeExample() {
  const [range, setRange] = useState<DateRange | undefined>({
    from: new Date(2026, 0, 1),
    to: new Date(2026, 0, 9),
  });

  return (
    <Calendar
      mode="range"
      defaultMonth={new Date(2026, 0)}
      selected={range}
      onSelect={setRange}
      numberOfMonths={2}
    />
  );
}
```

## Disabled Dates

Pass one or more react-day-picker [matchers](https://daypicker.dev/selections/disabling-dates) to `disabled`. Here only the days from December 25 to January 8 can be picked.

```tsx
import { Calendar } from '@/components/ui/Calendar';
import { useState } from 'react';

export function CalendarDisabledExample() {
  const [date, setDate] = useState<Date | undefined>();

  return (
    <Calendar
      mode="single"
      defaultMonth={new Date(2026, 0)}
      selected={date}
      onSelect={setDate}
      disabled={[
        { before: new Date(2025, 11, 25) },
        { after: new Date(2026, 0, 8) },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

## Year/Month Dropdown Caption

```tsx
import { Calendar } from '@/components/ui/Calendar';
import { useState } from 'react';

export function CalendarDropdownCaptionExample() {
  const [date, setDate] = useState<Date | undefined>();

  return (
    <Calendar
      mode="single"
      defaultMonth={new Date(2026, 0)}
      selected={date}
      onSelect={setDate}
      captionLayout="dropdown"
      startMonth={new Date(2000, 0)}
      endMonth={new Date(2030, 11)}
    />
  );
}
```

Pass `captionLayout="dropdown"` (or `"dropdown-months"` / `"dropdown-years"`) and bound the navigable range with `startMonth` / `endMonth`. The month picker is a 3-column grid and the year picker a scrollable list (Vittal `Popover`s, not native selects); the year picker centers the current year on open. Override `components={{ MonthsDropdown, YearsDropdown }}` to customize. To translate the dropdown labels, pass a `locale` (see [Localization](#localization)); to change their _format_, override `formatMonthDropdown`.

## Localization

`Calendar` ships **no default formatters** — it stays locale-neutral and leaves translation to the caller. There are two independent layers:

1. **`locale`** — _which language._ Import a locale from `react-day-picker/locale` and pass it as `locale`. It drives the weekday header, caption, and dropdown labels in the right language and order.
2. **`formatters`** — _how it renders._ Override `formatters` only when you want a different format than the locale's default. They are a pure react-day-picker pass-through.

### Locale

```tsx
import { Calendar } from '@/components/ui/Calendar';
import { useState } from 'react';
import { zhTW } from 'react-day-picker/locale';

export function CalendarLocaleExample() {
  const [date, setDate] = useState<Date | undefined>(
    new Date(2026, 0, 1),
  );

  return (
    <Calendar
      mode="single"
      defaultMonth={new Date(2026, 0)}
      selected={date}
      onSelect={setDate}
      locale={zhTW}
      captionLayout="dropdown"
      startMonth={new Date(2000, 0)}
      endMonth={new Date(2030, 11)}
    />
  );
}
```

The locale alone gives CJK weekday labels (`一 二 三 …`), a Monday week start, and Chinese month names in the dropdown (`一月`) — no hand-written formatters.

### Locale + formatter

Layer a formatter on top of the locale to reshape an already-localized value. The `dateLib` argument passed to each formatter carries the active locale, so format **through it** to stay localized. Here the month dropdown shows the short month (`1月`, `2月` …) instead of the locale default full name (`一月`):

```tsx
import { Calendar } from '@/components/ui/Calendar';
import { useState } from 'react';
import { defaultDateLib } from 'react-day-picker';
import { zhTW } from 'react-day-picker/locale';

export function CalendarLocaleWithFormatterExample() {
  const [date, setDate] = useState<Date | undefined>(
    new Date(2026, 0, 1),
  );

  return (
    <Calendar
      mode="single"
      defaultMonth={new Date(2026, 0)}
      selected={date}
      onSelect={setDate}
      locale={zhTW}
      captionLayout="dropdown"
      startMonth={new Date(2000, 0)}
      endMonth={new Date(2030, 11)}
      formatters={{
        formatMonthDropdown: (month, dateLib) =>
          (dateLib ?? defaultDateLib).format(month, 'LLL'),
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

## Navigation

The header ships with year-jump arrows (`«` `»`) flanking the single-month steps (`‹` `›`); year jumps respect `startMonth` / `endMonth`. To use single-month navigation only (e.g. inside a date-time picker), override the `Nav` slot via `components`.

## Date Picker (Popover + Calendar)

There is no separate `DatePicker` component — compose `Popover`, `Calendar`, and an input-style trigger. `defaultMonth={date}` reopens the calendar on the picked month:

```tsx
import { Calendar } from '@/components/ui/Calendar';
import {
  InputGroup,
  InputGroupAddon,
  InputGroupInput,
} from '@/components/ui/InputGroup';
import {
  Popover,
  PopoverContent,
  PopoverTrigger,
} from '@/components/ui/Popover';
import { CalendarDaysIcon } from '@/components/icons/CalendarDaysIcon';
import { format } from 'date-fns';
import { useState } from 'react';

export function CalendarInsideDatePickerExample() {
  const [date, setDate] = useState<Date | undefined>();
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);

  return (
    <div className="w-96">
      <Popover open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
        <PopoverTrigger
          nativeButton={false}
          render={
            <InputGroup className="cursor-pointer">
              <InputGroupInput
                readOnly
                value={date ? format(date, 'yyyy/MM/dd') : ''}
                placeholder="Pick a date"
                className="cursor-pointer"
              />
              <InputGroupAddon align="inline-end">
                <CalendarDaysIcon className="size-4 text-grayscale-opacity-500" />
              </InputGroupAddon>
            </InputGroup>
          }
        />
        <PopoverContent className="p-0" sideOffset={8}>
          <Calendar
            mode="single"
            defaultMonth={date}
            selected={date}
            onSelect={(next) => {
              setDate(next);
              if (next) setOpen(false);
            }}
          />
        </PopoverContent>
      </Popover>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Props

`Calendar` extends [`DayPickerProps`](https://daypicker.dev/api/interfaces/DayPickerProps) from `react-day-picker`. The most common props:

| Prop              | Type                                                             | Default   | Description                                              |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | --------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `mode`            | `'single' \| 'range' \| 'multiple'`                              | —         | Selection mode                                           |
| `selected`        | `Date \| DateRange \| Date[]`                                    | —         | Selected date(s); shape depends on `mode`                |
| `onSelect`        | `(value) => void`                                                | —         | Called when selection changes                            |
| `numberOfMonths`  | `number`                                                         | `1`       | How many months to render side-by-side                   |
| `showOutsideDays` | `boolean`                                                        | `true`    | Render leading/trailing days from adjacent months        |
| `captionLayout`   | `'label' \| 'dropdown' \| 'dropdown-months' \| 'dropdown-years'` | `'label'` | Month/year header style                                  |
| `startMonth`      | `Date`                                                           | —         | Earliest month the user can navigate to                  |
| `endMonth`        | `Date`                                                           | —         | Latest month the user can navigate to                    |
| `disabled`        | `Matcher \| Matcher[]`                                           | —         | Days that cannot be selected (see react-day-picker docs) |
| `formatters`      | `Partial<Formatters>`                                            | —         | Override label formatters (weekday, caption, etc.)       |
| `classNames`      | `Partial<ClassNames>`                                            | —         | Override class names per part                            |
| `components`      | `Partial<CustomComponents>`                                      | —         | Override built-in components (e.g. `Nav`, `DayButton`)   |
| `className`       | `string`                                                         | —         | Additional classes on root                               |

# Card

> Composable card surface with header, title, description, action, content, and footer slots.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/components/card

## Preview

```tsx
import {
  Card,
  CardContent,
  CardDescription,
  CardHeader,
  CardTitle,
} from '@/components/ui/Card';

export function CardBasicExample() {
  return (
    <Card className="w-90 max-w-full">
      <CardHeader>
        <CardTitle>Project dashboard</CardTitle>
        <CardDescription>Last updated 2 days ago.</CardDescription>
      </CardHeader>
      <CardContent>
        Track progress, owners, and review status in one place.
      </CardContent>
    </Card>
  );
}
```

## With Action

`CardAction` is automatically placed in the header's trailing slot.

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import {
  Card,
  CardAction,
  CardContent,
  CardDescription,
  CardHeader,
  CardTitle,
} from '@/components/ui/Card';

export function CardWithActionExample() {
  return (
    <Card className="w-90 max-w-full">
      <CardHeader>
        <CardTitle>Quarterly review</CardTitle>
        <CardDescription>3 items to review</CardDescription>
        <CardAction>
          <Button variant="ghost">View</Button>
        </CardAction>
      </CardHeader>
      <CardContent>Owners must submit by Friday.</CardContent>
    </Card>
  );
}
```

## With Footer

Add a separator class (`border-t`) on the footer or content to surface dividers.

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import {
  Card,
  CardContent,
  CardFooter,
  CardHeader,
  CardTitle,
} from '@/components/ui/Card';

export function CardWithFooterExample() {
  return (
    <Card className="w-90 max-w-full">
      <CardHeader className="border-b border-grayscale-opacity-300">
        <CardTitle>Leave request</CardTitle>
      </CardHeader>
      <CardContent>Fill in the dates and a short reason.</CardContent>
      <CardFooter className="justify-end border-t border-grayscale-opacity-300">
        <Button variant="ghost">Cancel</Button>
        <Button>Submit</Button>
      </CardFooter>
    </Card>
  );
}
```

## Header Only

A card can hold only `CardHeader`, for example as a compact group summary.

```tsx
import {
  Card,
  CardDescription,
  CardHeader,
  CardTitle,
} from '@/components/ui/Card';

export function CardHeaderOnlyExample() {
  return (
    <Card className="w-90 max-w-full">
      <CardHeader>
        <CardTitle>Design review</CardTitle>
        <CardDescription>5 tasks</CardDescription>
      </CardHeader>
    </Card>
  );
}
```

## Compound Parts

| Part              | Description                                                                                        |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Card`            | Root surface — rounded white background with emphasis shadow                                       |
| `CardHeader`      | Grid header that auto-lays out title, description, and action                                      |
| `CardTitle`       | Primary heading slot (`text-base`, `font-medium`)                                                  |
| `CardDescription` | Secondary text slot (`text-sm`, grayscale-opacity-600)                                             |
| `CardAction`      | Trailing slot in the header (e.g., menu button); only shown when present, header switches to 2-col |
| `CardContent`     | Body region with default padding                                                                   |
| `CardFooter`      | Footer region with flex layout                                                                     |

All parts accept native `div` props (`className`, `style`, `...rest`) and forward `ref`.

# Checkbox

> A checkbox input supporting checked, unchecked, and indeterminate states. Built on Base UI for accessibility.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/components/checkbox

## Preview

```tsx
import { Checkbox } from '@/components/ui/Checkbox';
import { Field, FieldLabel } from '@/components/ui/Field';
import { useState } from 'react';

export function CheckboxExample() {
  const [checked, setChecked] = useState(false);

  return (
    <Field orientation="horizontal" className="w-auto">
      <Checkbox
        id="checkbox-terms"
        checked={checked}
        onCheckedChange={setChecked}
      />
      <FieldLabel htmlFor="checkbox-terms">
        Accept terms and conditions
      </FieldLabel>
    </Field>
  );
}
```

## Usage

Put the `Checkbox` and its `FieldLabel` in a horizontal `Field`, and pair the label's `htmlFor` with the checkbox `id`. The whole row then toggles the checkbox and shows its hover ring.

## States

Mark an invalid checkbox with `aria-invalid`. Put `data-disabled` on the `Field` so the label dims with a disabled checkbox.

```tsx
import { Checkbox } from '@/components/ui/Checkbox';
import { Field, FieldLabel } from '@/components/ui/Field';

const states = [
  { label: 'Unchecked', props: {} },
  { label: 'Disabled', props: { disabled: true } },
  { label: 'Checked', props: { checked: true } },
  {
    label: 'Disabled checked',
    props: { checked: true, disabled: true },
  },
  { label: 'Indeterminate', props: { indeterminate: true } },
  {
    label: 'Disabled indeterminate',
    props: { disabled: true, indeterminate: true },
  },
  { label: 'Invalid', props: { 'aria-invalid': true } },
];

export function CheckboxStatesExample() {
  return (
    <div className="grid w-fit grid-cols-[repeat(2,auto)] gap-x-10 gap-y-3">
      {states.map(({ label, props }) => {
        const id = `checkbox-state-${label.toLowerCase().replace(/\W+/g, '-')}`;

        return (
          <Field
            key={label}
            orientation="horizontal"
            className="w-auto"
            data-disabled={props.disabled}
          >
            <Checkbox id={id} {...props} />
            <FieldLabel htmlFor={id}>{label}</FieldLabel>
          </Field>
        );
      })}
    </div>
  );
}
```

The `indeterminate` state is useful for "select all" patterns where only some items are selected.

## Indeterminate Pattern

```tsx
import { Checkbox } from '@/components/ui/Checkbox';
import { Field, FieldLabel } from '@/components/ui/Field';
import { useState } from 'react';

const items = [
  { id: 'email', label: 'Email' },
  { id: 'sms', label: 'SMS' },
  { id: 'push', label: 'Push notifications' },
];

export function CheckboxIndeterminateExample() {
  const [selected, setSelected] = useState<string[]>(['email']);
  const allChecked = selected.length === items.length;
  const someChecked = selected.length > 0 && !allChecked;

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-3">
      <Field orientation="horizontal" className="w-auto">
        <Checkbox
          id="checkbox-select-all"
          checked={allChecked}
          indeterminate={someChecked}
          onCheckedChange={(checked) =>
            setSelected(checked ? items.map((item) => item.id) : [])
          }
        />
        <FieldLabel htmlFor="checkbox-select-all">
          Select all
        </FieldLabel>
      </Field>
      {items.map((item) => (
        <Field
          key={item.id}
          orientation="horizontal"
          className="w-auto pl-6"
        >
          <Checkbox
            id={`checkbox-${item.id}`}
            checked={selected.includes(item.id)}
            onCheckedChange={(checked) =>
              setSelected((current) =>
                checked
                  ? [...current, item.id]
                  : current.filter((id) => id !== item.id),
              )
            }
          />
          <FieldLabel htmlFor={`checkbox-${item.id}`}>
            {item.label}
          </FieldLabel>
        </Field>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Props

| Prop              | Type             | Default | Description                       |
| ----------------- | ---------------- | ------- | --------------------------------- |
| `checked`         | `boolean`        | —       | Controlled checked state          |
| `defaultChecked`  | `boolean`        | `false` | Initial checked state             |
| `indeterminate`   | `boolean`        | `false` | Shows the mixed state             |
| `onCheckedChange` | Base UI callback | —       | Called when checked state changes |
| `disabled`        | `boolean`        | `false` | Disables interaction              |
| `required`        | `boolean`        | `false` | Marks the checkbox as required    |
| `className`       | `string`         | —       | Additional CSS classes            |
| `style`           | `CSSProperties`  | —       | Inline styles                     |

# Chip

> A toggleable pill component for filters, tags, and multi-select options.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/components/chip

## Preview

```tsx
import { Chip } from '@/components/ui/Chip';
import { useState } from 'react';

export function ChipExample() {
  const [selected, setSelected] = useState(true);

  return (
    <Chip selected={selected} onChange={setSelected}>
      Urgent
    </Chip>
  );
}
```

## Usage

`Chip` is controlled: keep `selected` in state and update it from `onChange`, which receives the next selected value.

## With Icon

Pass an icon to `icon` to render it before the label.

```tsx
import { Chip } from '@/components/ui/Chip';
import { FlagIcon } from '@/components/icons/FlagIcon';
import { useState } from 'react';

export function ChipIconExample() {
  const [selected, setSelected] = useState(true);

  return (
    <Chip
      selected={selected}
      onChange={setSelected}
      icon={<FlagIcon className="size-3" />}
    >
      Urgent
    </Chip>
  );
}
```

## States

```tsx
import { Chip } from '@/components/ui/Chip';
import { FlagIcon } from '@/components/icons/FlagIcon';

const states = [
  { label: 'Selected', selected: true },
  { label: 'Unselected', selected: false },
];

export function ChipStatesExample() {
  return (
    <div className="grid grid-cols-[auto_auto_auto] items-center justify-items-start gap-x-6 gap-y-3 text-sm text-grayscale-opacity-700">
      {states.map(({ label, selected }) => (
        <div key={label} className="contents">
          <span>{label}</span>
          <Chip selected={selected}>Urgent</Chip>
          <Chip
            selected={selected}
            icon={<FlagIcon className="size-3" />}
          >
            Urgent
          </Chip>
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

When `selected` is `true`, the chip renders with a primary blue background and text. When `false`, it renders with a grayscale style.

## Multiple Chips (Filter Group)

A common pattern is a group of chips acting as mutually exclusive filters:

```tsx
const filters = ['All', 'Active', 'Inactive', 'Pending'];
const [selected, setSelected] = useState('All');

{
  filters.map((filter) => (
    <Chip
      key={filter}
      selected={selected === filter}
      onChange={() => setSelected(filter)}
    >
      {filter}
    </Chip>
  ));
}
```

## Props

| Prop        | Type                          | Default | Description                                     |
| ----------- | ----------------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `children`  | `ReactNode`                   | —       | Chip label content                              |
| `selected`  | `boolean`                     | —       | **Required.** Controls the selected state       |
| `onChange`  | `(selected: boolean) => void` | —       | **Required.** Called when the chip is clicked   |
| `icon`      | `ReactNode`                   | —       | Optional icon rendered to the left of the label |
| `className` | `string`                      | —       | Additional CSS classes                          |
| `style`     | `CSSProperties`               | —       | Inline styles                                   |

# Collapsible

> An interactive panel that expands and collapses to reveal additional content.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/components/collapsible

## Preview

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import {
  Collapsible,
  CollapsibleContent,
  CollapsibleTrigger,
} from '@/components/ui/Collapsible';
import { AngleDownIcon } from '@/components/icons/AngleDownIcon';

export function CollapsibleExample() {
  return (
    <Collapsible className="w-80 space-y-2">
      <CollapsibleTrigger
        render={
          <Button
            variant="text"
            theme="default"
            className="w-full [&[data-panel-open]_[data-icon]]:rotate-180"
          >
            <span className="flex-1 text-left">
              Can I use this in my project?
            </span>
            <AngleDownIcon
              data-icon="inline-end"
              className="transition-transform duration-150"
            />
          </Button>
        }
      />
      <CollapsibleContent className="rounded-(--radius-sm) bg-grayscale-opacity-100 p-4 text-grayscale-opacity-700">
        Yes. Free to use for personal and commercial projects. No
        attribution required.
      </CollapsibleContent>
    </Collapsible>
  );
}
```

## Usage

`Collapsible` is built on Base UI Collapsible. Compose the trigger and content parts together; the trigger toggles `data-panel-open` on itself when the panel is expanded, which you can use to drive icon rotations or other affordances.

## Product details

Use `Collapsible` for "show more" patterns where supplementary detail belongs out of the way until the user asks for it.

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import {
  Collapsible,
  CollapsibleContent,
  CollapsibleTrigger,
} from '@/components/ui/Collapsible';
import { AngleDownIcon } from '@/components/icons/AngleDownIcon';

export function CollapsibleProductDetailsExample() {
  return (
    <div className="w-96 space-y-4 rounded-(--radius-sm) border border-grayscale-opacity-200 p-4">
      <div>
        <div className="font-medium text-grayscale-opacity-900">
          Vittal Design Hoodie
        </div>
        <div className="text-sm text-grayscale-opacity-600">$48</div>
      </div>
      <Collapsible className="space-y-2">
        <CollapsibleTrigger
          render={
            <Button
              variant="text"
              theme="default"
              size="md"
              className="w-full justify-between"
            >
              <span>Show details</span>
              <AngleDownIcon data-icon="inline-end" />
            </Button>
          }
        />
        <CollapsibleContent className="space-y-1 text-grayscale-opacity-700">
          <p>100% cotton, double-stitched seams.</p>
          <p>Ships within 2 business days.</p>
          <p>Free returns within 30 days.</p>
        </CollapsibleContent>
      </Collapsible>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Collapsible>
  <CollapsibleTrigger />
  <CollapsibleContent />
</Collapsible>
```

## Props

`Collapsible` accepts Base UI `Collapsible.Root` props:

| Prop           | Type                               | Default | Description                          |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `open`         | `boolean`                          | -       | Controlled open state                |
| `defaultOpen`  | `boolean`                          | `false` | Initial uncontrolled open state      |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean, details) => void` | -       | Fires when the panel opens or closes |
| `disabled`     | `boolean`                          | `false` | Disables toggling                    |

### CollapsibleContent

Renders a `<div>` panel with a height transition driven by Base UI's `--collapsible-panel-height` CSS variable. Use the `className` prop to override the default body styles.

| Prop               | Type      | Default | Description                                                                                                 |
| ------------------ | --------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `keepMounted`      | `boolean` | `false` | Keep the panel mounted in the DOM while collapsed                                                           |
| `hiddenUntilFound` | `boolean` | `false` | Use `hidden="until-found"` so browsers' built-in find-in-page can expand the panel; overrides `keepMounted` |

## Accessibility

`CollapsibleTrigger` automatically wires up `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`. Keep the trigger label descriptive of the content it reveals.

# Combobox

> An input picker for searching and selecting one or many options.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/components/combobox

## Preview

```tsx
import {
  Combobox,
  ComboboxContent,
  ComboboxHeader,
  ComboboxItem,
  ComboboxItemCheck,
  ComboboxItemText,
  ComboboxList,
  ComboboxSearchBar,
  ComboboxTrigger,
  ComboboxValue,
} from '@/components/ui/Combobox';
import { useState } from 'react';

type Option = {
  label: string;
  value: string;
};

const countries: Option[] = [
  { label: 'Taiwan', value: 'tw' },
  { label: 'Japan', value: 'jp' },
  { label: 'Singapore', value: 'sg' },
  { label: 'South Korea', value: 'kr' },
];

export function ComboboxExample() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState<Option | null>(null);

  return (
    <Combobox
      autoHighlight
      items={countries}
      itemToStringLabel={(item: Option | null) => item?.label ?? ''}
      itemToStringValue={(item: Option | null) => item?.value ?? ''}
      value={value}
      onValueChange={setValue}
    >
      <ComboboxTrigger className="w-60" aria-label="Open countries">
        <ComboboxValue placeholder="Search countries" />
      </ComboboxTrigger>
      <ComboboxContent emptyText="No results">
        <ComboboxHeader>
          <ComboboxSearchBar placeholder="Search countries" />
        </ComboboxHeader>
        <ComboboxList>
          {(item: Option) => (
            <ComboboxItem key={item.value} value={item}>
              <ComboboxItemText>{item.label}</ComboboxItemText>
              <ComboboxItemCheck />
            </ComboboxItem>
          )}
        </ComboboxList>
      </ComboboxContent>
    </Combobox>
  );
}
```

## Usage

Use `Combobox` when the picker renders an input: search, autocomplete, or removable chips.

Keep `Combobox` as the root when the popup is a searchable value picker. If only the trigger changes, customize `ComboboxTrigger`; do not wrap the combobox in `DropdownMenu`.

## Multiple

Add `multiple` and render the selection with `ComboboxTagsValue`. `maxDisplayCount` collapses the rest into a `+N` chip.

```tsx
import {
  Combobox,
  ComboboxContent,
  ComboboxHeader,
  ComboboxItem,
  ComboboxItemCheckbox,
  ComboboxItemText,
  ComboboxList,
  ComboboxSearchBar,
  ComboboxTagsValue,
  ComboboxTrigger,
} from '@/components/ui/Combobox';
import { useState } from 'react';

type Option = {
  label: string;
  value: string;
};

const frameworks: Option[] = [
  { label: 'React', value: 'react' },
  { label: 'Vue', value: 'vue' },
  { label: 'Angular', value: 'angular' },
  { label: 'Svelte', value: 'svelte' },
  { label: 'Solid', value: 'solid' },
  { label: 'Preact', value: 'preact' },
  { label: 'Ember', value: 'ember' },
  { label: 'Backbone', value: 'backbone' },
];

export function ComboboxMultipleExample() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState<Option[]>(
    frameworks.slice(0, 4),
  );

  return (
    <Combobox
      autoHighlight
      multiple
      items={frameworks}
      itemToStringLabel={(item: Option | null) => item?.label ?? ''}
      itemToStringValue={(item: Option | null) => item?.value ?? ''}
      value={value}
      onValueChange={setValue}
    >
      <ComboboxTrigger
        nativeButton={false}
        render={<div />}
        className="w-72"
        aria-label="Open frameworks"
      >
        <ComboboxTagsValue
          maxDisplayCount={2}
          placeholder="Search frameworks"
        />
      </ComboboxTrigger>
      <ComboboxContent emptyText="No results">
        <ComboboxHeader>
          <ComboboxSearchBar placeholder="Search frameworks" />
        </ComboboxHeader>
        <ComboboxList>
          {(item: Option) => (
            <ComboboxItem key={item.value} value={item}>
              <ComboboxItemCheckbox />
              <ComboboxItemText>{item.label}</ComboboxItemText>
            </ComboboxItem>
          )}
        </ComboboxList>
      </ComboboxContent>
    </Combobox>
  );
}
```

## Tag Picker with Footer

A tag picker composed from existing parts: read-only pills and `ComboboxOverflowChip` in the trigger, removable `ComboboxChip`s with a `ComboboxInput` in the popup header, and a `Button` footer. The input lives inside the popup; the trigger stays the anchor.

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import {
  Combobox,
  ComboboxChip,
  ComboboxChipRemove,
  ComboboxChips,
  ComboboxContent,
  ComboboxEmpty,
  ComboboxHeader,
  ComboboxInput,
  ComboboxItem,
  ComboboxItemCheckbox,
  ComboboxItemText,
  ComboboxList,
  ComboboxOverflowChip,
  ComboboxTrigger,
} from '@/components/ui/Combobox';
import { GearIcon } from '@/components/icons/GearIcon';
import { useState } from 'react';

type Option = {
  label: string;
  value: string;
};

const tags: Option[] = Array.from({ length: 24 }, (_, index) => ({
  label: `Tag ${index + 1}`,
  value: `tag-${index + 1}`,
}));

export function ComboboxTagPickerWithFooterExample() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState<Option[]>(tags.slice(0, 12));
  const visibleChips = value.slice(0, 3);
  const overflowCount = value.length - visibleChips.length;

  return (
    <Combobox
      autoHighlight
      multiple
      items={tags}
      itemToStringLabel={(item: Option | null) => item?.label ?? ''}
      itemToStringValue={(item: Option | null) => item?.value ?? ''}
      value={value}
      onValueChange={setValue}
    >
      <ComboboxTrigger className="h-11 w-90" aria-label="Open tags">
        {value.length === 0 ? (
          <span className="min-w-0 flex-1 truncate text-grayscale-opacity-400">
            Select tags
          </span>
        ) : (
          <span className="flex min-w-0 flex-1 items-center gap-2 overflow-hidden">
            {visibleChips.map((item) => (
              <span
                key={item.value}
                className="inline-flex h-5 shrink-0 items-center rounded-full bg-grayscale-opacity-700 px-2.5 text-xs leading-5 text-background"
              >
                {item.label}
              </span>
            ))}
            {overflowCount > 0 ? (
              <ComboboxOverflowChip>
                +{overflowCount}
              </ComboboxOverflowChip>
            ) : null}
          </span>
        )}
      </ComboboxTrigger>
      <ComboboxContent className="max-h-120 py-0">
        <ComboboxHeader className="border-b border-grayscale-opacity-300 px-3 pt-3 pb-2">
          <ComboboxChips className="flex max-h-44 flex-wrap items-center gap-2 overflow-x-hidden overflow-y-auto">
            {value.map((item) => (
              <ComboboxChip key={item.value}>
                <span className="min-w-0 truncate">{item.label}</span>
                <ComboboxChipRemove
                  aria-label={`Remove ${item.label}`}
                />
              </ComboboxChip>
            ))}
            <ComboboxInput
              placeholder="Search tags"
              className="h-5 min-w-32 flex-1"
            />
          </ComboboxChips>
        </ComboboxHeader>
        <ComboboxList className="py-2">
          {(item: Option) => (
            <ComboboxItem
              key={item.value}
              value={item}
              className="pr-5"
            >
              <ComboboxItemCheckbox />
              <ComboboxItemText>{item.label}</ComboboxItemText>
            </ComboboxItem>
          )}
        </ComboboxList>
        <ComboboxEmpty>No matching tags</ComboboxEmpty>
        <div className="flex items-center justify-center border-t border-grayscale-opacity-300 pt-2 pb-3">
          <Button
            variant="ghost"
            theme="default"
            className="text-grayscale-opacity-600 [&_[data-icon]]:size-4.5"
          >
            <GearIcon data-icon="inline-start" />
            Manage tags
          </Button>
        </div>
      </ComboboxContent>
    </Combobox>
  );
}
```

## States

```tsx
import {
  Combobox,
  ComboboxContent,
  ComboboxHeader,
  ComboboxItem,
  ComboboxItemCheck,
  ComboboxItemText,
  ComboboxList,
  ComboboxSearchBar,
  ComboboxTrigger,
  ComboboxValue,
} from '@/components/ui/Combobox';

type Option = {
  label: string;
  value: string;
};

const countries: Option[] = [
  { label: 'Taiwan', value: 'tw' },
  { label: 'Japan', value: 'jp' },
  { label: 'Singapore', value: 'sg' },
];

const states = [
  { label: 'Placeholder', props: {} },
  { label: 'Selected', props: { defaultValue: countries[0] } },
  { label: 'Disabled', props: { disabled: true } },
  {
    label: 'Disabled, selected',
    props: { defaultValue: countries[0], disabled: true },
  },
];

export function ComboboxStatesExample() {
  return (
    <div className="grid w-fit grid-cols-[auto_15rem] items-center gap-x-6 gap-y-3 text-sm text-grayscale-opacity-700">
      {states.map(({ label, props }) => (
        <div key={label} className="contents">
```
