```tsx
          <span>{label}</span>
          <Combobox
            items={countries}
            itemToStringLabel={(item: Option | null) =>
              item?.label ?? ''
            }
            itemToStringValue={(item: Option | null) =>
              item?.value ?? ''
            }
            {...props}
          >
            <ComboboxTrigger aria-label={`${label} country`}>
              <ComboboxValue placeholder="Search countries" />
            </ComboboxTrigger>
            <ComboboxContent emptyText="No results">
              <ComboboxHeader>
                <ComboboxSearchBar placeholder="Search countries" />
              </ComboboxHeader>
              <ComboboxList>
                {(item: Option) => (
                  <ComboboxItem key={item.value} value={item}>
                    <ComboboxItemText>{item.label}</ComboboxItemText>
                    <ComboboxItemCheck />
                  </ComboboxItem>
                )}
              </ComboboxList>
            </ComboboxContent>
          </Combobox>
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## When to Choose What

| Need                                 | Use                   |
| ------------------------------------ | --------------------- |
| Flat single or multiple value picker | `Select`              |
| Searchable picker or tag picker      | `Combobox`            |
| Hierarchical path picker             | `Command` + `Popover` |
| Command menu with callbacks          | `DropdownMenu`        |

Use named exports for shadcn-style imports:

```tsx
import {
  Combobox,
  ComboboxChip,
  ComboboxChipRemove,
  ComboboxChips,
  ComboboxClear,
  ComboboxContent,
  ComboboxHeader,
  ComboboxInput,
  ComboboxInputGroup,
  ComboboxItem,
  ComboboxItemCheck,
  ComboboxItemCheckbox,
  ComboboxItemText,
  ComboboxOverflowChip,
  ComboboxSearchBar,
  ComboboxTagsValue,
  ComboboxTrigger,
  ComboboxValue,
} from '@/components/ui/Combobox';
```

## Props

### Combobox

`Combobox` is `BaseCombobox.Root`. Use the Base UI root props such as `items`, `value`, `onValueChange`, `multiple`, `disabled`, `itemToStringLabel`, and `itemToStringValue`.

### ComboboxTrigger

Styled shell for the selected value. Use `nativeButton={false}` with `render={<div />}` when rendering removable tags inside it.

### ComboboxSearchBar

Popup search input for the combobox list. It renders `BaseCombobox.Input`, so filtering remains owned by Base UI.

### ComboboxTagsValue

Preset value renderer for multiple comboboxes. It renders selected values as removable chips, supports `maxDisplayCount`, and shows the hidden count as `+N`.

### ComboboxContent

| Prop                    | Type                                                   | Default                        | Description                                           |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `emptyText`             | `ReactNode`                                            | —                              | Empty state content                                   |
| `listClassName`         | `string`                                               | —                              | Classes for the list element                          |
| `align`                 | `'start' \| 'center' \| 'end'`                         | `'start'`                      | Alignment relative to the anchor                      |
| `alignOffset`           | `number`                                               | `0`                            | Offset along the alignment axis                       |
| `side`                  | `'top' \| 'right' \| 'bottom' \| 'left' \| …`          | `'bottom'`                     | Preferred side of the anchor                          |
| `sideOffset`            | `number`                                               | `4`                            | Distance from the anchor                              |
| `anchor`                | `RefObject \| Element \| …`                            | —                              | Custom positioning anchor (defaults to the trigger)   |
| `arrowPadding`          | `number`                                               | `5`                            | Minimum space between the arrow and the popup's edges |
| `collisionAvoidance`    | `{ side?, align?, fallbackAxisSide? }`                 | `{ fallbackAxisSide: 'none' }` | How the popup flips or shifts to avoid collisions     |
| `collisionBoundary`     | `'clipping-ancestors' \| Element \| Element[] \| Rect` | `'clipping-ancestors'`         | Area the popup is kept inside                         |
| `collisionPadding`      | `number \| { top?, right?, bottom?, left? }`           | `5`                            | Space kept from the edge of the collision boundary    |
| `disableAnchorTracking` | `boolean`                                              | `false`                        | Stop following layout shifts of the anchor            |
| `positionMethod`        | `'absolute' \| 'fixed'`                                | `'absolute'`                   | CSS `position` of the positioner                      |
| `sticky`                | `boolean`                                              | `false`                        | Keep the popup in view after the anchor scrolls out   |
| `portalContainer`       | `HTMLElement \| ShadowRoot \| RefObject \| null`       | —                              | Custom portal container (defaults to `document.body`) |
| `keepMounted`           | `boolean`                                              | `false`                        | Keep the popup in the DOM while closed                |

### ComboboxItem

`ComboboxItem` is `BaseComboboxItem` with Vittal Design row styling. Compose it with `ComboboxItemText`, `ComboboxItemCheck`, or `ComboboxItemCheckbox`.

# Command

> A composable command palette primitive built on cmdk, with input, list, items, groups, and shortcut display.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/components/command

## Preview

```tsx
import {
  Command,
  CommandEmpty,
  CommandGroup,
  CommandInput,
  CommandItem,
  CommandList,
  CommandSeparator,
  CommandShortcut,
} from '@/components/ui/Command';

export function CommandExample() {
  return (
    <Command label="Command palette" className="h-[300px] w-[280px]">
      <CommandInput placeholder="Type a command or search" />
      <CommandList>
        <CommandEmpty>No results found.</CommandEmpty>
        <CommandGroup heading="Suggestions">
          <CommandItem>
            <span>New file</span>
            <CommandShortcut>⌘N</CommandShortcut>
          </CommandItem>
          <CommandItem>
            <span>Open file</span>
            <CommandShortcut>⌘O</CommandShortcut>
          </CommandItem>
          <CommandItem>
            <span>Save</span>
            <CommandShortcut>⌘S</CommandShortcut>
          </CommandItem>
        </CommandGroup>
        <CommandSeparator />
        <CommandGroup heading="Settings">
          <CommandItem>Preferences</CommandItem>
          <CommandItem>Keyboard shortcuts</CommandItem>
        </CommandGroup>
      </CommandList>
    </Command>
  );
}
```

## Usage

`Command` is a thin styled wrapper around [cmdk](https://github.com/pacocoursey/cmdk). Use it to build command palettes, custom searchable popups, paged hierarchical pickers, or any list UI with keyboard-driven filtering.

> Filtering is handled by cmdk based on the typed `CommandInput` value
> matching each `CommandItem`'s text content. Pass `shouldFilter={false}`
> on `Command` to opt out and run your own filter logic.

## When to Use

| Need                                     | Component             |
| ---------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| Flat value picker                        | `Select`              |
| Searchable value picker (input + popup)  | `Combobox`            |
| Hierarchical path picker                 | `Command` + `Popover` |
| Action menu                              | `DropdownMenu`        |
| Command palette / custom searchable list | `Command`             |

`Command` does not include a popover or trigger — pair it with `Popover` (or your own surface) when you need a floating panel. The [Tree Select](/docs/blocks/tree-select) block is a paged tree picker built from `Command` and `Popover`.

## States

Put `CommandLoading` in the list while items load. `CommandEmpty` shows when no item matches the search.

```tsx
import {
  Command,
  CommandEmpty,
  CommandGroup,
  CommandInput,
  CommandItem,
  CommandList,
  CommandLoading,
} from '@/components/ui/Command';

export function CommandStatesExample() {
  return (
    <div className="grid w-fit grid-cols-[auto_auto] items-start gap-x-6 gap-y-3 text-sm text-grayscale-opacity-700">
      <span>Loading</span>
      <Command label="Loading" className="max-h-[300px] w-[260px]">
        <CommandInput placeholder="Search" />
        <CommandList>
          <CommandLoading />
        </CommandList>
      </Command>
      <span>Empty</span>
      <Command label="Empty" className="max-h-[300px] w-[260px]">
        <CommandInput placeholder="Search" value="Durian" />
        <CommandList>
          <CommandEmpty>No results found.</CommandEmpty>
          <CommandGroup>
            <CommandItem>Apple</CommandItem>
            <CommandItem>Banana</CommandItem>
          </CommandGroup>
        </CommandList>
      </Command>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Exports

| Export              | Description                                                               |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Command`           | Root container; accepts cmdk props (`shouldFilter`, `filter`, `label`, …) |
| `CommandInput`      | Search input row with leading search icon                                 |
| `CommandList`       | Scrollable list primitive                                                 |
| `CommandEmpty`      | Empty state shown when no items match                                     |
| `CommandGroup`      | Grouped items with optional `heading`                                     |
| `CommandSeparator`  | Horizontal divider between groups                                         |
| `CommandItem`       | Selectable row; fires `onSelect`                                          |
| `CommandShortcut`   | Right-aligned keyboard hint inside an item                                |
| `CommandLoading`    | Loading row with default spinner                                          |
| `CommandHeader`     | Header slot above input (used for back button)                            |
| `CommandBackButton` | Styled back button for paged flows                                        |

# Dialog

> A modal surface for focused confirmations, decisions, and short forms.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/components/dialog

## Preview

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import {
  Dialog,
  DialogBackdrop,
  DialogBody,
  DialogClose,
  DialogDescription,
  DialogFooter,
  DialogHeader,
  DialogPopup,
  DialogPortal,
  DialogTitle,
  DialogTrigger,
  DialogViewport,
} from '@/components/ui/Dialog';

export function DialogExample() {
  return (
    <Dialog>
      <DialogTrigger render={<Button>Open dialog</Button>} />
      <DialogPortal>
        <DialogBackdrop />
        <DialogViewport>
          <DialogPopup>
            <DialogHeader>
              <div className="space-y-1">
                <DialogTitle>Submit request?</DialogTitle>
                <DialogDescription>
                  Review the details before sending this request for
                  approval.
                </DialogDescription>
              </div>
              <DialogClose />
            </DialogHeader>
            <DialogBody>
              This action will notify approvers and lock the current
              draft while it is being reviewed.
            </DialogBody>
            <DialogFooter>
              <DialogClose
                render={
                  <Button variant="text" theme="default">
                    Cancel
                  </Button>
                }
              />
              <DialogClose
                render={<Button theme="primary">Submit</Button>}
              />
            </DialogFooter>
          </DialogPopup>
        </DialogViewport>
      </DialogPortal>
    </Dialog>
  );
}
```

## Usage

`Dialog` is built on Base UI Dialog. Compose the named root, trigger, portal, backdrop, viewport, popup, and content parts together so the title and description remain accessible to assistive technology.

## Sizes

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import {
  Dialog,
  DialogBackdrop,
  DialogBody,
  DialogClose,
  DialogFooter,
  DialogHeader,
  DialogPopup,
  DialogPortal,
  DialogTitle,
  DialogTrigger,
  DialogViewport,
} from '@/components/ui/Dialog';

const sizes = ['small', 'medium', 'large'] as const;

export function DialogSizesExample() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-3">
      {sizes.map((size) => (
        <Dialog key={size}>
          <DialogTrigger
            render={<Button className="capitalize">{size}</Button>}
          />
          <DialogPortal>
            <DialogBackdrop />
            <DialogViewport>
              <DialogPopup size={size}>
                <DialogHeader>
                  <DialogTitle className="capitalize">
                    {size} dialog
                  </DialogTitle>
                  <DialogClose />
                </DialogHeader>
                <DialogBody>
                  Dialog popup width is controlled by the size prop.
                </DialogBody>
                <DialogFooter>
                  <DialogClose
                    render={
                      <Button variant="text" theme="default">
                        Close
                      </Button>
                    }
                  />
                </DialogFooter>
              </DialogPopup>
            </DialogViewport>
          </DialogPortal>
        </Dialog>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

Use `small` for brief confirmation copy, `medium` for common decision flows, and `large` when the dialog contains denser content.

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Dialog>
  <DialogTrigger />
  <DialogPortal>
    <DialogBackdrop />
    <DialogViewport>
      <DialogPopup>
        <DialogHeader>
          <DialogTitle />
          <DialogDescription />
          <DialogClose />
        </DialogHeader>
        <DialogBody />
        <DialogFooter />
      </DialogPopup>
    </DialogViewport>
  </DialogPortal>
</Dialog>
```

## Props

`Dialog` accepts Base UI `Dialog.Root` props, including `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange`, `modal`, and `disablePointerDismissal`.

### DialogPopup

| Prop        | Type                             | Default    | Description                  |
| ----------- | -------------------------------- | ---------- | ---------------------------- |
| `size`      | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | Controls the maximum width   |
| `className` | `string`                         | -          | Additional CSS classes       |
| `children`  | `ReactNode`                      | -          | Dialog content and sub-parts |

### DialogClose

| Prop         | Type        | Default   | Description                                  |
| ------------ | ----------- | --------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `children`   | `ReactNode` | -         | Optional custom close button content         |
| `render`     | `ReactNode` | -         | Renders a custom element as the close button |
| `aria-label` | `string`    | `'Close'` | Accessible label for the default icon button |

## Accessibility

Always include `DialogTitle` in the popup. Add `DialogDescription` when the dialog needs extra context, and keep destructive or irreversible actions explicit in the footer.

# DropdownMenu

> An action menu where each item fires a callback. Use this when items invoke actions rather than bind to a form value.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/components/dropdown-menu

## Preview

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import {
  DropdownMenu,
  DropdownMenuContent,
  DropdownMenuGroup,
  DropdownMenuItem,
  DropdownMenuLabel,
  DropdownMenuSeparator,
  DropdownMenuTrigger,
} from '@/components/ui/DropdownMenu';

export function DropdownMenuExample() {
  return (
    <DropdownMenu>
      <DropdownMenuTrigger render={<Button>Account</Button>} />
      <DropdownMenuContent>
        <DropdownMenuGroup>
          <DropdownMenuLabel>My account</DropdownMenuLabel>
          <DropdownMenuItem>Profile</DropdownMenuItem>
          <DropdownMenuItem>Billing</DropdownMenuItem>
          <DropdownMenuItem>Team</DropdownMenuItem>
        </DropdownMenuGroup>
        <DropdownMenuSeparator />
        <DropdownMenuGroup>
          <DropdownMenuLabel>Support</DropdownMenuLabel>
          <DropdownMenuItem>Documentation</DropdownMenuItem>
          <DropdownMenuItem disabled>Contact sales</DropdownMenuItem>
        </DropdownMenuGroup>
        <DropdownMenuSeparator />
        <DropdownMenuItem>Log out</DropdownMenuItem>
      </DropdownMenuContent>
    </DropdownMenu>
  );
}
```

## Usage

`DropdownMenu` is a thin styled wrapper around Base UI Menu. Use it for commands, not value picking. The trigger is render-prop based and trigger-agnostic — pass any element (a button, an icon-only button, anything) via `render`. For a `SplitButton`, see the [SplitButton recipe](#splitbutton-recipe).

Group related items in `DropdownMenuGroup` with a `DropdownMenuLabel`, and divide groups with `DropdownMenuSeparator`. Set `disabled` on an item that can't run right now.

## When to Use

| Need                                             | Use                   |
| ------------------------------------------------ | --------------------- |
| **Action menu** where each item fires a callback | **`DropdownMenu`**    |
| Flat value picker                                | `Select`              |
| Searchable value picker or tag picker            | `Combobox`            |
| Hierarchical path picker                         | `Command` + `Popover` |
| Floating panel with arbitrary content            | `Popover`             |

The key distinction: `DropdownMenu` items are **commands** (each triggers a side effect), not values. There is no value binding, no selected state on regular items, and selecting an item closes the menu by default.

Do not wrap `Select`, `Combobox`, or a custom `Command` picker inside `DropdownMenu` just to get a different trigger. Use the picker primitive directly and customize its own trigger.

## With Icons

Put an icon before the label with `data-icon="inline-start"`.

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import {
  DropdownMenu,
  DropdownMenuContent,
  DropdownMenuItem,
  DropdownMenuTrigger,
} from '@/components/ui/DropdownMenu';
import { CheckIcon } from '@/components/icons/CheckIcon';
import { MagnifyingGlassIcon } from '@/components/icons/MagnifyingGlassIcon';

export function DropdownMenuWithIconsExample() {
  return (
    <DropdownMenu>
      <DropdownMenuTrigger render={<Button>Quick actions</Button>} />
      <DropdownMenuContent>
        <DropdownMenuItem>
          <MagnifyingGlassIcon
            data-icon="inline-start"
            className="size-3.5"
          />
          <span>Search</span>
        </DropdownMenuItem>
        <DropdownMenuItem>
          <CheckIcon data-icon="inline-start" className="size-3.5" />
          <span>Mark complete</span>
        </DropdownMenuItem>
      </DropdownMenuContent>
    </DropdownMenu>
  );
}
```

## Checkbox and Radio Items

For toggle-style entries, use `DropdownMenuCheckboxItem` and `DropdownMenuRadioItem`. These render an indicator on the left and stay open after selection so users can flip multiple toggles.

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import {
  DropdownMenu,
  DropdownMenuCheckboxItem,
  DropdownMenuContent,
  DropdownMenuGroup,
  DropdownMenuLabel,
  DropdownMenuTrigger,
} from '@/components/ui/DropdownMenu';
import { useState } from 'react';

export function DropdownMenuWithCheckboxItemsExample() {
  const [showStatusBar, setShowStatusBar] = useState(true);
  const [showActivityBar, setShowActivityBar] = useState(false);

  return (
    <DropdownMenu>
      <DropdownMenuTrigger render={<Button>View</Button>} />
      <DropdownMenuContent>
        <DropdownMenuGroup>
          <DropdownMenuLabel>Appearance</DropdownMenuLabel>
          <DropdownMenuCheckboxItem
            checked={showStatusBar}
            onCheckedChange={setShowStatusBar}
          >
            Status bar
          </DropdownMenuCheckboxItem>
          <DropdownMenuCheckboxItem
            checked={showActivityBar}
            onCheckedChange={setShowActivityBar}
          >
            Activity bar
          </DropdownMenuCheckboxItem>
        </DropdownMenuGroup>
      </DropdownMenuContent>
    </DropdownMenu>
  );
}
```

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import {
  DropdownMenu,
  DropdownMenuContent,
  DropdownMenuGroup,
  DropdownMenuLabel,
  DropdownMenuRadioGroup,
  DropdownMenuRadioItem,
  DropdownMenuTrigger,
} from '@/components/ui/DropdownMenu';
import { useState } from 'react';

export function DropdownMenuWithRadioGroupExample() {
  const [position, setPosition] = useState('bottom');

  return (
    <DropdownMenu>
      <DropdownMenuTrigger render={<Button>Panel position</Button>} />
      <DropdownMenuContent>
        <DropdownMenuGroup>
          <DropdownMenuLabel>Position</DropdownMenuLabel>
          <DropdownMenuRadioGroup
            value={position}
            onValueChange={setPosition}
          >
            <DropdownMenuRadioItem value="top">
              Top
            </DropdownMenuRadioItem>
            <DropdownMenuRadioItem value="right">
              Right
            </DropdownMenuRadioItem>
            <DropdownMenuRadioItem value="bottom">
              Bottom
            </DropdownMenuRadioItem>
            <DropdownMenuRadioItem value="left">
              Left
            </DropdownMenuRadioItem>
          </DropdownMenuRadioGroup>
        </DropdownMenuGroup>
      </DropdownMenuContent>
    </DropdownMenu>
  );
}
```

## Submenus

Wrap nested items in `DropdownMenuSub` with a `DropdownMenuSubTrigger` and `DropdownMenuSubContent`. Submenus open on hover and right arrow key by default.

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import {
  DropdownMenu,
  DropdownMenuContent,
  DropdownMenuItem,
  DropdownMenuSeparator,
  DropdownMenuSub,
  DropdownMenuSubContent,
  DropdownMenuSubTrigger,
  DropdownMenuTrigger,
} from '@/components/ui/DropdownMenu';

export function DropdownMenuWithSubmenuExample() {
  return (
    <DropdownMenu>
      <DropdownMenuTrigger render={<Button>File</Button>} />
      <DropdownMenuContent>
        <DropdownMenuItem>New file</DropdownMenuItem>
        <DropdownMenuItem>Open…</DropdownMenuItem>
        <DropdownMenuSeparator />
        <DropdownMenuSub>
          <DropdownMenuSubTrigger>Open recent</DropdownMenuSubTrigger>
          <DropdownMenuSubContent>
            <DropdownMenuItem>project-a.tsx</DropdownMenuItem>
            <DropdownMenuItem>project-b.tsx</DropdownMenuItem>
            <DropdownMenuItem>notes.md</DropdownMenuItem>
          </DropdownMenuSubContent>
        </DropdownMenuSub>
        <DropdownMenuSeparator />
        <DropdownMenuItem>Settings</DropdownMenuItem>
      </DropdownMenuContent>
    </DropdownMenu>
  );
}
```

## SplitButton Recipe

Pass `<DropdownMenuTrigger />` to `SplitButton`'s `splitRender`. Only the chevron opens the menu; the main button keeps its own action. `align="end"` lines the menu up with the right edge of the SplitButton.

Do not pass the whole `SplitButton` to `DropdownMenuTrigger`'s `render`. The main button would also open the menu, and the menu would lose its position.

```tsx
import { SplitButton } from '@/components/ui/SplitButton';
import {
  DropdownMenu,
  DropdownMenuContent,
  DropdownMenuItem,
  DropdownMenuTrigger,
} from '@/components/ui/DropdownMenu';
import { useState } from 'react';

export function DropdownMenuWithSplitButtonTriggerExample() {
  const [lastAction, setLastAction] = useState('Nothing saved yet');

  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-4">
      <DropdownMenu>
        <SplitButton
          onClick={() => setLastAction('Saved')}
          splitRender={<DropdownMenuTrigger />}
        >
          Save
        </SplitButton>
        <DropdownMenuContent align="end">
          <DropdownMenuItem
            onClick={() => setLastAction('Saved as draft')}
          >
            Save as draft
          </DropdownMenuItem>
          <DropdownMenuItem
            onClick={() => setLastAction('Saved and published')}
          >
            Save and publish
          </DropdownMenuItem>
          <DropdownMenuItem
            onClick={() => setLastAction('Saved as template')}
          >
            Save as template
          </DropdownMenuItem>
        </DropdownMenuContent>
      </DropdownMenu>
      <p className="text-sm text-grayscale-opacity-700">
        {lastAction}
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

See [SplitButton](/docs/components/split-button) for its themes, sizes, and props.

## Props

### DropdownMenuContent

`DropdownMenuContent` (and `DropdownMenuSubContent`) is a composite of Portal + Positioner + Popup. Positioning props are forwarded to the Positioner; the popup accepts the usual Base UI Menu Popup props.

| Prop                    | Type                                                   | Default                               | Description                                           |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `align`                 | `'start' \| 'center' \| 'end'`                         | `'start'`                             | Alignment relative to the anchor                      |
| `alignOffset`           | `number`                                               | -                                     | Offset along the alignment axis                       |
| `side`                  | `'top' \| 'right' \| 'bottom' \| 'left' \| …`          | `'bottom'` (`'right'` for SubContent) | Preferred side of the anchor                          |
| `sideOffset`            | `number`                                               | `4`                                   | Distance from the anchor                              |
| `positionerClassName`   | `string`                                               | -                                     | Classes on the Positioner wrapper                     |
| `className`             | `string`                                               | -                                     | Additional classes on the popup                       |
| `anchor`                | `RefObject \| Element \| …`                            | -                                     | Custom positioning anchor (defaults to the trigger)   |
| `arrowPadding`          | `number`                                               | `5`                                   | Minimum space between the arrow and the popup's edges |
| `collisionAvoidance`    | `{ side?, align?, fallbackAxisSide? }`                 | `{ fallbackAxisSide: 'none' }`        | How the popup flips or shifts to avoid collisions     |
| `collisionBoundary`     | `'clipping-ancestors' \| Element \| Element[] \| Rect` | `'clipping-ancestors'`                | Area the popup is kept inside                         |
| `collisionPadding`      | `number \| { top?, right?, bottom?, left? }`           | `5`                                   | Space kept from the edge of the collision boundary    |
| `disableAnchorTracking` | `boolean`                                              | `false`                               | Stop following layout shifts of the anchor            |
| `positionMethod`        | `'absolute' \| 'fixed'`                                | `'absolute'`                          | CSS `position` of the positioner                      |
| `sticky`                | `boolean`                                              | `false`                               | Keep the popup in view after the anchor scrolls out   |
| `portalContainer`       | `HTMLElement \| ShadowRoot \| RefObject \| null`       | -                                     | Custom portal container (defaults to `document.body`) |
| `keepMounted`           | `boolean`                                              | `false`                               | Keep the popup in the DOM while closed                |

Use `portalContainer` when the menu must stay inside a CSS-scoped root — styles under a scope selector do not apply if the popup is portaled to `document.body`. It is also useful when body portaling breaks stacking or clipping (Dialog, transform, fullscreen, Shadow DOM).

When using submenus, pass the **same** container to both `DropdownMenuContent` and `DropdownMenuSubContent` so main and nested menus share one portal environment.

## Exports

| Export                     | Description                                                          |
| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `DropdownMenu`             | Root; manages open state                                             |
| `DropdownMenuTrigger`      | Render-prop trigger slot — accepts any element                       |
| `DropdownMenuContent`      | Composite of Portal + Positioner + Popup; supports `portalContainer` |
| `DropdownMenuItem`         | Action row; fires `onClick`, closes menu by default                  |
| `DropdownMenuCheckboxItem` | Toggleable item with built-in indicator                              |
| `DropdownMenuRadioGroup`   | Radio group container                                                |
| `DropdownMenuRadioItem`    | Mutually exclusive item with built-in indicator                      |
| `DropdownMenuLabel`        | Section label inside a group                                         |
| `DropdownMenuSeparator`    | Horizontal divider                                                   |
| `DropdownMenuGroup`        | Group container for related items                                    |
| `DropdownMenuSub`          | Submenu root                                                         |
| `DropdownMenuSubTrigger`   | Submenu trigger row with built-in angle-right indicator              |
| `DropdownMenuSubContent`   | Submenu content composite; supports `portalContainer`                |
| `DropdownMenuPortal`       | Portal target (rarely used directly)                                 |

# Editable

> Inline editable text field with display, input, and textarea parts.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/components/editable

## Preview

```tsx
import {
  Editable,
  EditableDisplay,
  EditableInput,
} from '@/components/ui/Editable';

export function EditableExample() {
  return (
    <div className="w-80">
      <Editable defaultValue="Click to edit" placeholder="Not set">
        <EditableDisplay />
        <EditableInput />
      </Editable>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Usage

`Editable` is a compound component for inline text editing. The
display surface looks like static text; clicking it swaps in an
`Input` (or `Textarea`) focused with the caret at the end. Pressing
`Enter` (or blurring) commits the value through `onCommit`; `Escape`
discards the staged edit.

## Textarea Variant

Swap `EditableInput` for `EditableTextarea` when the field should
accept multi-line content. `Enter` inserts a newline; click outside
to commit.

```tsx
import {
  Editable,
  EditableDisplay,
  EditableTextarea,
} from '@/components/ui/Editable';

export function EditableTextareaVariantExample() {
  return (
    <div className="w-80">
      <Editable
        defaultValue="A longer note. Click to edit."
        placeholder="Click to add a note"
      >
        <EditableDisplay />
        <EditableTextarea rows={3} />
      </Editable>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Controlled

Provide `value` together with `onCommit` to drive the field from
outside. The component still manages its own staged edit buffer
internally, so the parent only receives the committed value.

```tsx
import {
  Editable,
  EditableDisplay,
  EditableInput,
} from '@/components/ui/Editable';
import { useState } from 'react';

export function EditableControlledExample() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState('Alice');

  return (
    <div className="flex w-80 flex-col gap-2">
      <Editable
        value={value}
        onCommit={setValue}
        placeholder="Enter a name"
      >
        <EditableDisplay />
        <EditableInput />
      </Editable>
      <p className="font-sans text-xs text-grayscale-opacity-500">
        Current value: {value || '(empty)'}
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## States

When the value is empty, `EditableDisplay` renders the `placeholder`
text with a visible border so the affordance stays visible. Pass
`disabled` to block editing entirely, or `readOnly` to keep the
display interactive-looking but ignore enter-edit clicks.

```tsx
import {
  Editable,
  EditableDisplay,
  EditableInput,
} from '@/components/ui/Editable';

const states = [
  { label: 'Empty', props: { defaultValue: '' } },
  {
    label: 'Disabled',
    props: { defaultValue: 'Cannot edit', disabled: true },
  },
  {
    label: 'Read-only',
    props: { defaultValue: 'Read-only content', readOnly: true },
  },
];

export function EditableStatesExample() {
  return (
    <div className="grid w-fit grid-cols-[auto_20rem] items-center gap-x-6 gap-y-3 text-sm text-grayscale-opacity-700">
      {states.map(({ label, props }) => (
        <div key={label} className="contents">
          <span>{label}</span>
          <Editable placeholder="Click to add a note" {...props}>
            <EditableDisplay />
            <EditableInput />
          </Editable>
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Parts

| Part               | Description                                            |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Editable`         | Context provider that owns the value and editing state |
| `EditableDisplay`  | Static-looking button shown when not editing           |
| `EditableInput`    | Single-line `Input` shown while editing                |
| `EditableTextarea` | Multi-line `textarea` shown while editing              |

## Editable Props

| Prop           | Type                      | Default | Description                                        |
| -------------- | ------------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `value`        | `string`                  | —       | Controlled value                                   |
| `defaultValue` | `string`                  | `''`    | Uncontrolled initial value                         |
| `onCommit`     | `(value: string) => void` | —       | Called when the staged value is committed          |
| `placeholder`  | `string`                  | —       | Shown in display when empty and used by the input  |
| `disabled`     | `boolean`                 | `false` | Blocks entering edit mode                          |
| `readOnly`     | `boolean`                 | `false` | Display stays focusable but cannot enter edit mode |
| `className`    | `string`                  | —       | Additional CSS classes on the wrapper              |
| `...props`     | `ComponentProps<'div'>`   | —       | Native `div` props on the wrapper                  |

## Keyboard

| Key      | Behavior                                               |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Enter`  | (Input) commits the staged value and exits edit mode   |
| `Escape` | Discards the staged value and exits edit mode          |
| Blur     | Commits the staged value (both `Input` and `Textarea`) |

# Field

> Composable form field layout with labels, descriptions, errors, and groups.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/components/field

## Preview

```tsx
import {
  Field,
  FieldDescription,
  FieldLabel,
} from '@/components/ui/Field';
import { Input } from '@/components/ui/Input';

export function FieldExample() {
  return (
    <Field className="w-80">
      <FieldLabel htmlFor="field-email">Email</FieldLabel>
      <Input id="field-email" placeholder="name@example.com" />
      <FieldDescription>
        Used for notifications and account recovery.
      </FieldDescription>
    </Field>
  );
}
```

## Usage

`Field` provides a layout primitive that arranges a label, control,
description, and error message. Pair `FieldLabel` `htmlFor` with the
control's `id` for accessible focus and click behavior.

## Orientation

`Field` supports `vertical` (default), `horizontal`, and `responsive`
orientations. `responsive` switches from vertical to horizontal at
the `@md` container breakpoint defined on the parent `FieldGroup`.

```tsx
import {
  Field,
  FieldContent,
  FieldDescription,
  FieldLabel,
} from '@/components/ui/Field';
import { Input } from '@/components/ui/Input';

export function FieldHorizontalExample() {
  return (
    <Field orientation="horizontal" className="w-80">
      <FieldLabel
        htmlFor="field-horizontal-email"
        className="w-[100px]"
      >
        Email
      </FieldLabel>
      <FieldContent>
        <Input
          id="field-horizontal-email"
          placeholder="name@example.com"
        />
        <FieldDescription>Used for account alerts.</FieldDescription>
      </FieldContent>
    </Field>
  );
}
```

## With Checkbox

When a field wraps a control that already carries the label semantics
(checkbox, radio), use `FieldContent` with `FieldTitle` and
`FieldDescription` so the title is read alongside the control.

```tsx
import { Checkbox } from '@/components/ui/Checkbox';
import {
  Field,
  FieldContent,
  FieldDescription,
  FieldLabel,
} from '@/components/ui/Field';

export function FieldWithContentExample() {
  return (
    <Field orientation="horizontal" className="w-80">
      <Checkbox id="field-notifications" />
      <FieldContent>
        <FieldLabel htmlFor="field-notifications">
          Notifications
        </FieldLabel>
        <FieldDescription>
          Email, SMS, and push delivery options.
        </FieldDescription>
      </FieldContent>
    </Field>
  );
}
```

## Required

Pass `required` to `FieldLabel` to render the Vittal Design required
dot before the label text. Keep the actual `required` prop on the
control too so the form validates correctly.

```tsx
import { Field, FieldLabel } from '@/components/ui/Field';
import { Input } from '@/components/ui/Input';

export function FieldRequiredExample() {
  return (
    <Field className="w-80">
      <FieldLabel htmlFor="field-required-email" required>
        Email
      </FieldLabel>
      <Input
        id="field-required-email"
        placeholder="name@example.com"
        required
      />
    </Field>
  );
}
```

The dot is rendered as a `::before` pseudo positioned at `-left-2`,
so make sure the `Field` (or its parent) has enough left padding for
the dot to be visible.

## Invalid

Mark a field as invalid by setting `data-invalid="true"` on the
`Field` and `aria-invalid` on the input. Use `FieldError` to render
one or more validation messages.

```tsx
import {
  Field,
  FieldError,
  FieldLabel,
} from '@/components/ui/Field';
import { Input } from '@/components/ui/Input';

export function FieldInvalidExample() {
  return (
    <Field className="w-80" data-invalid="true">
      <FieldLabel htmlFor="field-invalid-email" required>
        Email
      </FieldLabel>
      <Input
        id="field-invalid-email"
        placeholder="name@example.com"
        required
        aria-invalid
      />
      <FieldError errors={[{ message: 'Enter a valid email.' }]} />
    </Field>
  );
}
```

## Grouped Fields

Use `FieldSet` + `FieldLegend` for grouped form sections, with
`FieldGroup` to control vertical spacing between fields and
`FieldSeparator` for inline section breaks.

```tsx
import { Checkbox } from '@/components/ui/Checkbox';
import {
  Field,
  FieldContent,
  FieldDescription,
  FieldGroup,
  FieldLabel,
  FieldLegend,
  FieldSeparator,
  FieldSet,
  FieldTitle,
} from '@/components/ui/Field';
import { Input } from '@/components/ui/Input';

export function FieldGroupedExample() {
  return (
    <FieldSet className="w-80">
      <FieldLegend>Profile</FieldLegend>
      <FieldGroup>
        <Field>
          <FieldLabel htmlFor="field-name">Name</FieldLabel>
          <Input id="field-name" placeholder="Ada Lovelace" />
        </Field>
        <Field>
          <FieldLabel htmlFor="field-role">Role</FieldLabel>
          <Input id="field-role" placeholder="Researcher" />
        </Field>
        <FieldSeparator>Optional</FieldSeparator>
        <Field orientation="horizontal">
          <Checkbox id="field-public" />
          <FieldContent>
            <FieldTitle>Public profile</FieldTitle>
            <FieldDescription>
              Show this profile in team directories.
            </FieldDescription>
          </FieldContent>
        </Field>
      </FieldGroup>
    </FieldSet>
  );
}
```

## Parts

| Part               | Description                                                       |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Field`            | Layout container for a single field; supports orientation variant |
| `FieldLabel`       | Wraps `Label`; ties to a control via `htmlFor`                    |
| `FieldTitle`       | Non-interactive label used inside `FieldContent`                  |
| `FieldDescription` | Helper text shown below or beside the control                     |
| `FieldError`       | Validation message — accepts `errors` array or children           |
| `FieldContent`     | Stacks label + description next to a checkbox/radio control       |
| `FieldGroup`       | Vertical stack of related fields                                  |
| `FieldSet`         | `<fieldset>` wrapper for grouped sections                         |
| `FieldLegend`      | `<legend>` heading for a `FieldSet`                               |
| `FieldSeparator`   | Inline divider with optional centered label                       |

## Field Props

| Prop            | Type                                         | Default      | Description                             |
| --------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------------ | --------------------------------------- |
| `orientation`   | `'vertical' \| 'horizontal' \| 'responsive'` | `'vertical'` | Controls layout direction               |
| `data-invalid`  | `boolean`                                    | —            | Marks the field as invalid for styling  |
| `data-disabled` | `boolean`                                    | —            | Marks the field as disabled for styling |
| `className`     | `string`                                     | —            | Additional CSS classes                  |
| `...props`      | `ComponentProps<'div'>`                      | —            | Native `div` props and events           |

## FieldLegend Props

| Prop        | Type                       | Default    | Description                         |
| ----------- | -------------------------- | ---------- | ----------------------------------- |
| `variant`   | `'legend' \| 'label'`      | `'legend'` | `legend` is larger; `label` is `sm` |
| `className` | `string`                   | —          | Additional CSS classes              |
| `...props`  | `ComponentProps<'legend'>` | —          | Native `legend` props               |

## FieldError Props

| Prop        | Type                                       | Default | Description                                      |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------ | ------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `errors`    | `Array<{ message?: string } \| undefined>` | —       | Renders deduped messages; multiple → bullet list |
| `children`  | `ReactNode`                                | —       | Override messages with custom content            |
| `className` | `string`                                   | —       | Additional CSS classes                           |

# Icons

> Built-in SVG icon set used across Vittal Design components.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/components/icons

## Gallery

All icons render as inline SVGs that inherit `currentColor`, so they
adapt to the text color of their container.

```tsx
import { AngleDownIcon } from '@/components/icons/AngleDownIcon';
import { AngleDownSolidIcon } from '@/components/icons/AngleDownSolidIcon';
import { AngleLeftIcon } from '@/components/icons/AngleLeftIcon';
import { AngleLeftSolidIcon } from '@/components/icons/AngleLeftSolidIcon';
import { AngleLeftToLineIcon } from '@/components/icons/AngleLeftToLineIcon';
import { AngleRightIcon } from '@/components/icons/AngleRightIcon';
import { AngleRightSolidIcon } from '@/components/icons/AngleRightSolidIcon';
import { AngleRightToLineIcon } from '@/components/icons/AngleRightToLineIcon';
import { AngleUpIcon } from '@/components/icons/AngleUpIcon';
import { AngleUpSolidIcon } from '@/components/icons/AngleUpSolidIcon';
import { AnglesLeftIcon } from '@/components/icons/AnglesLeftIcon';
import { AnglesRightIcon } from '@/components/icons/AnglesRightIcon';
import { ArrowRightLongIcon } from '@/components/icons/ArrowRightLongIcon';
import { ArrowUpRightFromSquareIcon } from '@/components/icons/ArrowUpRightFromSquareIcon';
import { ArrowUpRightFromSquareSolidIcon } from '@/components/icons/ArrowUpRightFromSquareSolidIcon';
import { BanIcon } from '@/components/icons/BanIcon';
import { BarsIcon } from '@/components/icons/BarsIcon';
import { BellIcon } from '@/components/icons/BellIcon';
import { BellSlashIcon } from '@/components/icons/BellSlashIcon';
import { CalendarDaysIcon } from '@/components/icons/CalendarDaysIcon';
import { CaretDownSolidIcon } from '@/components/icons/CaretDownSolidIcon';
import { CaretLeftSolidIcon } from '@/components/icons/CaretLeftSolidIcon';
import { CaretRightSolidIcon } from '@/components/icons/CaretRightSolidIcon';
import { CaretUpSolidIcon } from '@/components/icons/CaretUpSolidIcon';
import { CheckIcon } from '@/components/icons/CheckIcon';
import { CheckSolidIcon } from '@/components/icons/CheckSolidIcon';
import { CircleCheckIcon } from '@/components/icons/CircleCheckIcon';
import { CircleCheckSolidIcon } from '@/components/icons/CircleCheckSolidIcon';
import { CircleDashedIcon } from '@/components/icons/CircleDashedIcon';
import { CircleDotIcon } from '@/components/icons/CircleDotIcon';
import { CircleExclamationSolidIcon } from '@/components/icons/CircleExclamationSolidIcon';
import { CircleInfoIcon } from '@/components/icons/CircleInfoIcon';
import { CircleInfoSolidIcon } from '@/components/icons/CircleInfoSolidIcon';
import { CircleMinusSolidIcon } from '@/components/icons/CircleMinusSolidIcon';
import { CircleQuestionIcon } from '@/components/icons/CircleQuestionIcon';
import { CircleUserIcon } from '@/components/icons/CircleUserIcon';
import { CircleXmarkIcon } from '@/components/icons/CircleXmarkIcon';
import { CircleXmarkSolidIcon } from '@/components/icons/CircleXmarkSolidIcon';
import { ClearIcon } from '@/components/icons/ClearIcon';

export function IconsGalleryExample() {
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full grid-cols-[repeat(auto-fill,minmax(9rem,1fr))] gap-3">
      {icons.map(({ name, Icon }) => (
        <div
          key={name}
          className="flex min-w-0 flex-col items-center justify-center gap-2 rounded-md border border-grayscale-opacity-200 bg-background px-2 py-4 text-grayscale-opacity-800"
        >
          <Icon className="size-6" />
          {/* One line so the name copies cleanly. text-fit shrinks long
              names to fit (Chromium 150+). Chromium skips shrinks under
              ~2.5%, so the label may spill a few px into the tile padding
              there. Other browsers truncate with an ellipsis; title shows
              the full name. */}
          <span
            title={name}
            className="max-w-full truncate font-mono text-[11px] text-grayscale-opacity-600 [text-fit:shrink] supports-[text-fit:shrink]:overflow-visible"
          >
            {name}
          </span>
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Usage

Import each icon from its dedicated file. Barrel imports
(`@/icons`) are intentionally not allowed in component source so
that registry consumers only pull in the icons they actually use.

```tsx
import { MagnifyingGlassIcon } from '@/icons/MagnifyingGlassIcon';

<MagnifyingGlassIcon className="size-4 text-grayscale-opacity-700" />;
```

Available icons:

```ts
import { AngleDownIcon } from '@/icons/AngleDownIcon';
import { AngleDownSolidIcon } from '@/icons/AngleDownSolidIcon';
import { AngleLeftIcon } from '@/icons/AngleLeftIcon';
```

## Regular and Solid

Icons follow the Figma library's two weights. Regular icons have no suffix
and use a 1.3 stroke. Solid icons end in `Solid` and use a heavier 1.75
stroke or a filled shape, for example `AngleLeftIcon` and
`AngleLeftSolidIcon`. Pick the weight the Figma design names
(`Icons/Regular/…` or `Icons/Solid/…`); do not thicken a Regular icon with
`strokeWidth` instead.

## Sizes

Control the icon size with Tailwind's `size-*` utility — each icon
SVG fills the container set by width/height.

```tsx
import { MagnifyingGlassIcon } from '@/components/icons/MagnifyingGlassIcon';

export function IconsSizesExample() {
  return (
    <div className="flex items-end gap-4 text-grayscale-opacity-800">
      <MagnifyingGlassIcon className="size-3" />
      <MagnifyingGlassIcon className="size-4" />
      <MagnifyingGlassIcon className="size-5" />
      <MagnifyingGlassIcon className="size-6" />
      <MagnifyingGlassIcon className="size-8" />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Colors

Icons inherit `currentColor`, so any Tailwind text color utility
applies.

```tsx
import { FlagIcon } from '@/components/icons/FlagIcon';

export function IconsColorsExample() {
  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-4">
      <FlagIcon className="size-5 text-primary-500" />
      <FlagIcon className="size-5 text-success-500" />
      <FlagIcon className="size-5 text-warning-500" />
      <FlagIcon className="size-5 text-destructive-500" />
      <FlagIcon className="size-5 text-grayscale-opacity-700" />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## SpinnerIcon

`SpinnerIcon` renders the static glyph. Add Tailwind's `animate-spin`
utility when you need rotation, or use the `Spinner` component for
loading status UI.

```tsx
import { SpinnerIcon } from '@/components/icons/SpinnerIcon';

export function IconsSpinnerExample() {
  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-4">
      <SpinnerIcon className="size-6 animate-spin text-primary-500" />
      <SpinnerIcon className="size-6 text-grayscale-opacity-500" />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Props

All icons accept standard SVG props. Size and color should normally be
controlled with Tailwind classes.

| Prop          | Type                    | Default | Description                                     |
| ------------- | ----------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `className`   | `string`                | —       | Additional CSS classes                          |
| `width`       | `number \| string`      | `'1em'` | SVG width                                       |
| `height`      | `number \| string`      | `'1em'` | SVG height                                      |
| `aria-hidden` | `boolean`               | `true`  | Hide decorative icons from assistive technology |
| `...props`    | `ComponentProps<'svg'>` | —       | Native `svg` props and events                   |

# Input

> Text input components including Input, PasswordInput, and Textarea.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/components/input

## Input

The base single-line input primitive.

### Preview

```tsx
import { Input } from '@/components/ui/Input';
import { useState } from 'react';

export function InputExample() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState('');

  return (
    <Input
      className="w-112.5"
      placeholder="Enter text..."
      value={value}
      onValueChange={setValue}
    />
  );
}
```

### Usage

`Input` is built on Base UI's input primitive. Prefer `onValueChange`
for controlled value updates; native input props such as `onChange`,
`name`, `type`, `disabled`, and `aria-invalid` still pass through.

### Ghost

Set `appearance="ghost"` for a borderless input that shows its border on hover and focus, for example inline in a table or toolbar.

```tsx
import { Input } from '@/components/ui/Input';
import { useState } from 'react';

export function InputGhostExample() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState('');

  return (
    <Input
      appearance="ghost"
      className="w-112.5"
      placeholder="Borderless until hover or focus"
      value={value}
      onValueChange={setValue}
    />
  );
}
```

### States

Use `disabled` to disable the input, `aria-invalid` to mark an invalid value, and `readOnly` for a value that can be selected but not edited.

```tsx
import { Input } from '@/components/ui/Input';

const states = [
  { label: 'Placeholder', props: {} },
  { label: 'Filled', props: { defaultValue: 'Vital Design' } },
  { label: 'Disabled', props: { disabled: true } },
  { label: 'Invalid', props: { 'aria-invalid': true } },
  {
    label: 'Read-only',
    props: { defaultValue: 'Vital Design', readOnly: true },
  },
];

export function InputStatesExample() {
  return (
    <div className="grid w-fit grid-cols-[auto_18rem] items-center gap-x-6 gap-y-3 text-sm text-grayscale-opacity-700">
      {states.map(({ label, props }) => (
        <div key={label} className="contents">
          <span>{label}</span>
          <Input
            aria-label={label}
            placeholder="Enter text..."
            {...props}
          />
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Input Props

| Prop            | Type                                   | Default   | Description                      |
| --------------- | -------------------------------------- | --------- | -------------------------------- |
| `value`         | `string`                               | —         | Controlled value                 |
| `defaultValue`  | `string`                               | —         | Uncontrolled initial value       |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void`              | —         | Controlled value change callback |
| `onChange`      | `ChangeEventHandler<HTMLInputElement>` | —         | Native input change callback     |
| `placeholder`   | `string`                               | —         | Placeholder text                 |
| `appearance`    | `'solid' \| 'ghost'`                   | `'solid'` | Bordered or borderless style     |
| `disabled`      | `boolean`                              | `false`   | Disables the input               |
| `aria-invalid`  | `boolean`                              | —         | Applies invalid border styling   |
| `className`     | `string`                               | —         | Additional CSS classes           |
| `style`         | `CSSProperties`                        | —         | Inline styles                    |

## InputGroup

Need a prefix, suffix, inline text, or an action button inside the field? Compose it with [InputGroup](/docs/components/input-group).

## PasswordInput

A text input with a visibility toggle for password fields. It installs as its own registry item, `password-input`, and is built on `InputGroup`.

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @vital-design/password-input
```

### Preview

Set `id` to connect a label, and `autoComplete` so password managers can fill the field. The example uses `Field` and `FieldLabel` from the `field` registry item.

```tsx
import { Field, FieldLabel } from '@/components/ui/Field';
import { PasswordInput } from '@/components/ui/PasswordInput';
import { useState } from 'react';

export function PasswordInputExample() {
  const [password, setPassword] = useState('');

  return (
    <Field className="w-112.5">
      <FieldLabel htmlFor="current-password">Password</FieldLabel>
      <PasswordInput
        id="current-password"
        name="password"
        autoComplete="current-password"
        placeholder="Enter password"
        value={password}
        onChange={setPassword}
      />
    </Field>
  );
}
```

### PasswordInput Props

| Prop                | Type                      | Default           | Description                            |
| ------------------- | ------------------------- | ----------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `value`             | `string`                  | —                 | Controlled value                       |
| `defaultValue`      | `string`                  | —                 | Uncontrolled initial value             |
| `onChange`          | `(value: string) => void` | —                 | Value change callback                  |
| `placeholder`       | `string`                  | —                 | Placeholder text                       |
| `initiallyVisible`  | `boolean`                 | `false`           | Show password text initially           |
| `disabled`          | `boolean`                 | `false`           | Disables the input                     |
| `aria-invalid`      | `boolean`                 | —                 | Applies invalid border styling         |
| `prefix`            | `ReactNode`               | —                 | Element rendered inside the left side  |
| `onEnter`           | `(value: string) => void` | —                 | Called when Enter key is pressed       |
| `showPasswordLabel` | `string`                  | `'Show password'` | Toggle name while the text is hidden   |
| `hidePasswordLabel` | `string`                  | `'Hide password'` | Toggle name while the text is visible  |
| `className`         | `string`                  | —                 | Classes for the InputGroup shell       |
| `style`             | `CSSProperties`           | —                 | Inline styles for the InputGroup shell |

Every other `<input>` prop (`id`, `name`, `autoComplete`, `required`, `onBlur`, …) is forwarded to the inner input, and `ref` points at that input. `onChange` still receives a `string`, not an event.

---

## Textarea

A multi-line text field. See [Textarea](/docs/components/textarea) for its states.

### Preview

```tsx
import { Textarea } from '@/components/ui/Textarea';
import { useState } from 'react';

export function TextareaExample() {
  const [text, setText] = useState('');

  return (
    <Textarea
      aria-label="Feedback"
      className="w-112.5"
      placeholder="Tell us what you think..."
      value={text}
      onChange={(event) => setText(event.currentTarget.value)}
    />
  );
}
```

### Textarea Props

| Prop           | Type                                      | Default | Description                  |
| -------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ------- | ---------------------------- |
| `value`        | `string`                                  | —       | Controlled value             |
| `defaultValue` | `string`                                  | —       | Uncontrolled initial value   |
| `placeholder`  | `string`                                  | —       | Placeholder text             |
| `disabled`     | `boolean`                                 | `false` | Disables the textarea        |
| `aria-invalid` | `boolean`                                 | —       | Applies error border styling |
| `onChange`     | `ChangeEventHandler<HTMLTextAreaElement>` | —       | Native value change callback |
| `rows`         | `number`                                  | —       | Native visible row count     |
| `className`    | `string`                                  | —       | Additional CSS classes       |
| `style`        | `CSSProperties`                           | —       | Inline styles                |

# InputGroup

> A composable input shell for prefixes, suffixes, inline text, and actions around an input or textarea.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/components/input-group

## Preview

```tsx
import {
  InputGroup,
  InputGroupAddon,
  InputGroupButton,
  InputGroupInput,
} from '@/components/ui/InputGroup';
import { MagnifyingGlassIcon } from '@/components/icons/MagnifyingGlassIcon';
import { XmarkIcon } from '@/components/icons/XmarkIcon';
import { useState } from 'react';

export function InputGroupExample() {
  const [query, setQuery] = useState('');

  return (
    <InputGroup className="w-112.5">
      <InputGroupAddon>
        <MagnifyingGlassIcon className="size-4.5" />
      </InputGroupAddon>
      <InputGroupInput
        aria-label="Search"
        placeholder="Search..."
        value={query}
        onValueChange={setQuery}
      />
      <InputGroupAddon align="inline-end">
        <InputGroupButton
          aria-label="Clear"
          size="icon-xs"
          onClick={() => setQuery('')}
        >
          <XmarkIcon className="size-3.5" />
        </InputGroupButton>
      </InputGroupAddon>
    </InputGroup>
  );
}
```

## Installation

After [configuring the registry](/docs/getting-started/installation), install InputGroup:

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @vital-design/input-group
```

## Usage

`InputGroup` draws the border, focus, disabled, and invalid states around one control (`InputGroupInput` or `InputGroupTextarea`). Put icons, text, and buttons in `InputGroupAddon`; clicking an addon outside a button focuses the control.

Use it when you build your own input layout. [SearchBar](/docs/components/search-bar) and [PasswordInput](/docs/components/input#password-input) are preset wrappers built on `InputGroup`; use them when they fit.

## With Text

Use `InputGroupText` for static prefixes and suffixes such as a protocol, unit, or currency.

```tsx
import {
  InputGroup,
  InputGroupAddon,
  InputGroupInput,
  InputGroupText,
} from '@/components/ui/InputGroup';
import { useState } from 'react';

export function InputGroupWithTextExample() {
  const [domain, setDomain] = useState('vital.example.com');

  return (
    <InputGroup className="w-112.5">
      <InputGroupAddon>
        <InputGroupText>https://</InputGroupText>
      </InputGroupAddon>
      <InputGroupInput
        aria-label="Website"
        value={domain}
        onValueChange={setDomain}
      />
    </InputGroup>
  );
}
```

## Textarea

```tsx
import {
  InputGroup,
  InputGroupTextarea,
} from '@/components/ui/InputGroup';
import { useState } from 'react';

export function InputGroupTextareaExample() {
  const [message, setMessage] = useState('Multiline content');

  return (
    <InputGroup className="w-112.5">
      <InputGroupTextarea
        aria-label="Message"
        className="h-30"
        placeholder="Enter your message"
        value={message}
        onChange={(event) => setMessage(event.currentTarget.value)}
      />
    </InputGroup>
  );
}
```

## Block Addon

Set `align="block-start"` or `align="block-end"` to place an addon above or below the control.

```tsx
import {
  InputGroup,
  InputGroupAddon,
  InputGroupText,
  InputGroupTextarea,
} from '@/components/ui/InputGroup';
import { useState } from 'react';

export function InputGroupBlockAddonExample() {
  const [comment, setComment] = useState('Multiline content');

  return (
    <InputGroup className="w-112.5">
      <InputGroupAddon align="block-start" className="border-b">
        <InputGroupText>Comment</InputGroupText>
      </InputGroupAddon>
      <InputGroupTextarea
        aria-label="Comment"
        placeholder="Enter your message"
        value={comment}
        onChange={(event) => setComment(event.currentTarget.value)}
      />
    </InputGroup>
  );
}
```

## States

Disable the control with `disabled` on `InputGroupInput`; the group and its addons follow. Mark an invalid value with `aria-invalid` on the control.

```tsx
import {
  InputGroup,
  InputGroupAddon,
  InputGroupButton,
  InputGroupInput,
  InputGroupText,
} from '@/components/ui/InputGroup';
import { PlusIcon } from '@/components/icons/PlusIcon';

const states = [
  { label: 'Default', props: {} },
  { label: 'Disabled', props: { disabled: true } },
  { label: 'Invalid', props: { 'aria-invalid': true } },
];

export function InputGroupStatesExample() {
  return (
    <div className="grid w-fit grid-cols-[auto_18rem] items-center gap-x-6 gap-y-3 text-sm text-grayscale-opacity-700">
      {states.map(({ label, props }) => (
        <div key={label} className="contents">
          <span>{label}</span>
          <InputGroup>
            <InputGroupAddon>
              <InputGroupText>$</InputGroupText>
            </InputGroupAddon>
            <InputGroupInput
              aria-label={`${label} amount`}
              defaultValue="2000"
              {...props}
            />
            <InputGroupAddon align="inline-end">
              <InputGroupButton
                aria-label="Increase"
                size="icon-xs"
                disabled={props.disabled}
              >
                <PlusIcon className="size-3.5" />
              </InputGroupButton>
            </InputGroupAddon>
          </InputGroup>
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Parts

| Part                 | Description                                           |
| -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `InputGroup`         | Visual shell with focus, disabled, and invalid states |
| `InputGroupInput`    | Single-line input control                             |
| `InputGroupTextarea` | Multiline textarea control                            |
| `InputGroupAddon`    | Prefix or suffix slot                                 |
| `InputGroupButton`   | Small action button inside an addon                   |
| `InputGroupText`     | Static text inside an addon                           |

## Props

### InputGroupAddon

| Prop    | Type                                                             | Default          | Description                             |
| ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `align` | `'inline-start' \| 'inline-end' \| 'block-start' \| 'block-end'` | `'inline-start'` | Where the addon sits around the control |

### InputGroupButton

| Prop   | Type                                     | Default    | Description                         |
| ------ | ---------------------------------------- | ---------- | ----------------------------------- |
| `size` | `'xs' \| 'sm' \| 'icon-xs' \| 'icon-sm'` | `'xs'`     | Button size; `icon-*` for icon-only |
| `type` | `'button' \| 'submit' \| 'reset'`        | `'button'` | Native button type                  |

`InputGroupButton` also accepts `Button` props except `variant` and `size`; `theme` cannot be `dangerous`. `InputGroupInput` accepts `Input` props, and `InputGroupTextarea` accepts `Textarea` props.

# Item

> Content rows with media, title, description, and actions.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/components/item

## Preview

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import {
  Item,
  ItemActions,
  ItemContent,
  ItemDescription,
  ItemMedia,
  ItemTitle,
} from '@/components/ui/Item';
import { ShieldCheckIcon } from '@/components/icons/ShieldCheckIcon';

export function ItemExample() {
  return (
    <Item variant="outline" className="w-96 max-w-full">
      <ItemMedia variant="icon">
        <ShieldCheckIcon className="size-5" />
      </ItemMedia>
      <ItemContent>
        <ItemTitle>Profile verified</ItemTitle>
        <ItemDescription>
          Your profile has been verified.
        </ItemDescription>
      </ItemContent>
      <ItemActions>
        <Button size="md" theme="default">
          Review
        </Button>
      </ItemActions>
    </Item>
  );
}
```

## Composition

```txt
ItemGroup
`-- Item
    |-- ItemHeader
    |-- ItemMedia
    |-- ItemContent
    |   |-- ItemTitle
    |   `-- ItemDescription
    |-- ItemActions
    `-- ItemFooter
```

Use `Item` for display rows. Use `size="list"` when the row should match picker/list density. Use `Select` or `Combobox` for value picking, `DropdownMenu` for action menus, and `Command` with `Popover` for searchable or hierarchical command panels.

## Variants

```tsx
import {
  Item,
  ItemContent,
  ItemDescription,
  ItemTitle,
} from '@/components/ui/Item';

export function ItemVariantsExample() {
  return (
    <div className="flex w-96 max-w-full flex-col gap-3">
      <Item>
        <ItemContent>
          <ItemTitle>Default</ItemTitle>
          <ItemDescription>Transparent background.</ItemDescription>
        </ItemContent>
      </Item>
      <Item variant="outline">
        <ItemContent>
          <ItemTitle>Outline</ItemTitle>
          <ItemDescription>
            Bordered row for clear grouping.
          </ItemDescription>
        </ItemContent>
      </Item>
      <Item variant="muted">
        <ItemContent>
          <ItemTitle>Muted</ItemTitle>
          <ItemDescription>
            Soft background for secondary content.
          </ItemDescription>
        </ItemContent>
      </Item>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Sizes

```tsx
import {
  Item,
  ItemContent,
  ItemDescription,
  ItemTitle,
} from '@/components/ui/Item';

const sizes = [
  {
    size: 'default',
    title: 'Default',
    description: 'Standard spacing.',
  },
  { size: 'sm', title: 'Small', description: 'Compact spacing.' },
  {
    size: 'xs',
    title: 'Extra small',
    description: 'Dense row spacing.',
  },
  { size: 'list', title: 'List', description: 'Picker row spacing.' },
] as const;

export function ItemSizesExample() {
  return (
    <div className="flex w-96 max-w-full flex-col gap-3">
      {sizes.map(({ size, title, description }) => (
        <Item key={size} variant="outline" size={size}>
          <ItemContent>
            <ItemTitle>{title}</ItemTitle>
            <ItemDescription>{description}</ItemDescription>
          </ItemContent>
        </Item>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## List Rows

`size="list"` follows the select-option row pattern: text-sm, compact padding, hover, active, current, and disabled states. Picker and menu primitives set `data-highlighted`, `data-active`, `data-current`, and `data-disabled`; the examples set them directly to show each state.

```tsx
import {
  Item,
  ItemContent,
  ItemGroup,
  ItemTitle,
} from '@/components/ui/Item';

export function ItemTextRowsExample() {
  return (
    <ItemGroup className="w-96 max-w-full">
      <Item size="list">
        <ItemContent>
          <ItemTitle>Normal</ItemTitle>
        </ItemContent>
      </Item>
      <Item size="list" data-highlighted>
        <ItemContent>
          <ItemTitle>Hover</ItemTitle>
        </ItemContent>
      </Item>
      <Item size="list" data-active>
        <ItemContent>
          <ItemTitle>Active</ItemTitle>
        </ItemContent>
      </Item>
      <Item size="list" data-current>
        <ItemContent>
          <ItemTitle>Current</ItemTitle>
        </ItemContent>
      </Item>
      <Item size="list" data-disabled>
        <ItemContent>
          <ItemTitle>Disabled</ItemTitle>
        </ItemContent>
      </Item>
    </ItemGroup>
  );
}
```

### With Description

```tsx
import {

```

### With Icons

Use `ItemMedia variant="icon"` for a leading icon and `ItemActions` for a trailing one.

```tsx
import {

import { AngleRightIcon } from '@/components/icons/AngleRightIcon';

        </ItemMedia>

        </ItemActions>

```

### With Images

```tsx
import {
  Item,
  ItemActions,
  ItemContent,
  ItemDescription,
  ItemGroup,
  ItemMedia,
  ItemTitle,
} from '@/components/ui/Item';
import { AngleRightIcon } from '@/components/icons/AngleRightIcon';

const rows = [
  { label: 'Normal', description: true, action: true },
  {
    label: 'Hover',
    state: { 'data-highlighted': true },
    action: true,
  },
  { label: 'Active', state: { 'data-active': true }, action: true },
  {
    label: 'Current',
    state: { 'data-current': true },
    description: true,
  },
  { label: 'Disabled', state: { 'data-disabled': true } },
];

export function ItemImageRowsExample() {
  return (
    <ItemGroup className="w-96 max-w-full">
      {rows.map(({ label, state, description, action }) => (
        <Item key={label} size="list" {...state}>
          <ItemMedia variant="image">
            <span className="grid size-full place-content-center rounded-full border border-primary-200 bg-primary-50 text-sm text-primary-500">
              VD
            </span>
          </ItemMedia>
          <ItemContent>
            <ItemTitle>{label}</ItemTitle>
            {description && (
              <ItemDescription>Description text</ItemDescription>
            )}
          </ItemContent>
          {action && (
            <ItemActions>
              <AngleRightIcon className="size-[11px]" />
            </ItemActions>
          )}
        </Item>
      ))}
    </ItemGroup>
  );
}
```

## Group

Wrap rows in `ItemGroup` and divide them with `ItemSeparator`.

```tsx
import {
  Item,
  ItemContent,
  ItemDescription,
  ItemGroup,
  ItemMedia,
  ItemSeparator,
  ItemTitle,
} from '@/components/ui/Item';
import { Fragment } from 'react';

const people = [
  {
    name: 'Alex Lin',
    initials: 'AL',
    email: 'alex.lin@vikosmos.com',
  },
  {
    name: 'Jamie Chen',
    initials: 'JC',
    email: 'jamie.chen@vikosmos.com',
  },
  {
    name: 'Morgan Wu',
    initials: 'MW',
    email: 'morgan.wu@vikosmos.com',
  },
];

export function ItemGroupedRowsExample() {
  return (
    <ItemGroup className="w-96 max-w-full rounded border border-grayscale-opacity-300">
      {people.map(({ name, initials, email }, index) => (
        <Fragment key={name}>
          <Item size="list">
            <ItemMedia variant="image">
              <span className="grid size-full place-content-center rounded-full bg-grayscale-opacity-100 text-xs text-grayscale-opacity-700">
                {initials}
              </span>
            </ItemMedia>
            <ItemContent>
              <ItemTitle>{name}</ItemTitle>
              <ItemDescription>{email}</ItemDescription>
            </ItemContent>
          </Item>
          {index < people.length - 1 && <ItemSeparator />}
        </Fragment>
      ))}
    </ItemGroup>
  );
}
```

## Link

Pass `render={<a href="..." />}` to render the row as a link.

```tsx
import {
  Item,
  ItemActions,
  ItemContent,
  ItemDescription,
  ItemTitle,
} from '@/components/ui/Item';
import { AngleRightIcon } from '@/components/icons/AngleRightIcon';

export function ItemLinkExample() {
  return (
    <Item
      render={<a href="/docs" />}
      variant="outline"
      className="w-96 max-w-full"
    >
      <ItemContent>
        <ItemTitle>Documentation</ItemTitle>
        <ItemDescription>
          Learn how to install registry items.
        </ItemDescription>
      </ItemContent>
      <ItemActions>
        <AngleRightIcon className="size-[11px]" />
      </ItemActions>
    </Item>
  );
}
```

## Props

### Item

| Prop        | Type                                  | Default     | Description              |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------- | ----------- | ------------------------ |
| `variant`   | `'default' \| 'outline' \| 'muted'`   | `'default'` | Visual style             |
| `size`      | `'default' \| 'sm' \| 'xs' \| 'list'` | `'default'` | Row density              |
| `render`    | `ReactElement` or render function     | -           | Replace the root element |
| `className` | `string`                              | -           | Additional CSS classes   |

### ItemMedia

| Prop      | Type                             | Default     | Description     |
| --------- | -------------------------------- | ----------- | --------------- |
| `variant` | `'default' \| 'icon' \| 'image'` | `'default'` | Media treatment |

### Parts

`ItemGroup` renders `role="list"` by default. `ItemDescription` is clamped to two lines by default. `ItemSeparator` uses `Separator` props. `ItemContent`, `ItemTitle`, `ItemDescription`, `ItemActions`, `ItemHeader`, and `ItemFooter` accept native element props.

# Label

> Accessible label text associated with a form control.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/components/label

## Preview

```tsx
import { Input } from '@/components/ui/Input';
import { Label } from '@/components/ui/Label';

export function LabelWithInputExample() {
  return (
    <div className="flex w-80 flex-col gap-2">
      <Label htmlFor="email">Email</Label>
      <Input id="email" placeholder="name@example.com" />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Usage

Pair `htmlFor` with the control's `id` so clicking the label focuses the control. For a label with a description or error message, use [Field](/docs/components/field).

## Required

`required` adds the Vittal Design required dot to the label. Keep the actual required state on the control too.

```tsx
import { Input } from '@/components/ui/Input';
import { Label } from '@/components/ui/Label';

export function LabelRequiredExample() {
  return (
    <div className="flex w-80 flex-col gap-2">
      <Label htmlFor="required-email" required>
        Email
      </Label>
      <Input
        id="required-email"
        placeholder="name@example.com"
        required
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## With Disabled Input

Disabling the input doesn't change the label. To dim the label with the control, use [Field](/docs/components/field) with `data-disabled`.

```tsx
import { Input } from '@/components/ui/Input';
import { Label } from '@/components/ui/Label';

export function LabelWithDisabledInputExample() {
  return (
    <div className="flex w-80 flex-col gap-2">
      <Label htmlFor="disabled-email">Email</Label>
      <Input
        id="disabled-email"
        placeholder="name@example.com"
        disabled
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Props

| Prop        | Type                      | Default | Description                     |
| ----------- | ------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------- |
| `htmlFor`   | `string`                  | —       | Associated control id           |
| `required`  | `boolean`                 | `false` | Shows the required dot          |
| `className` | `string`                  | —       | Additional CSS classes          |
| `style`     | `CSSProperties`           | —       | Inline styles                   |
| `...props`  | `ComponentProps<'label'>` | —       | Native `label` props and events |

# NumberInput

> A numeric input with stepper buttons, locale-aware formatting, and clamped step interactions.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/components/number-input

## Preview

```tsx
import {
  NumberInput,
  NumberInputControl,
  NumberInputGroup,
  NumberInputSteppers,
} from '@/components/ui/NumberInput';

export function NumberInputExample() {
  return (
    <div className="w-60">
      <NumberInput defaultValue={0}>
        <NumberInputGroup>
          <NumberInputControl placeholder="0" />
          <NumberInputSteppers />
        </NumberInputGroup>
      </NumberInput>
```
