```tsx
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Usage

`NumberInput` is built on Base UI's
[Number Field](https://base-ui.com/react/components/number-field).
The root manages the numeric value, clamping, formatting, and the
disabled state of every part. Compose `NumberInputGroup`,
`NumberInputControl`, and `NumberInputSteppers` to render the field.

## Min, Max, And Step

`min` and `max` clamp values from the steppers, keyboard, and wheel.
`step` controls the increment per arrow press; `smallStep` and
`largeStep` are used when the meta or shift key is held.

```tsx
import {
  NumberInput,
  NumberInputControl,
  NumberInputGroup,
  NumberInputSteppers,
} from '@/components/ui/NumberInput';

export function NumberInputWithRangeExample() {
  return (
    <div className="w-60">
      <NumberInput defaultValue={5} min={0} max={10} step={1}>
        <NumberInputGroup>
          <NumberInputControl placeholder="0" />
          <NumberInputSteppers />
        </NumberInputGroup>
      </NumberInput>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## States

Disable every part with `disabled` on `NumberInput`, or keep the value focusable but unchangeable with `readOnly`. Set `aria-invalid` on `NumberInputControl` to apply the error border style.

```tsx
import {
  NumberInput,
  NumberInputControl,
  NumberInputGroup,
  NumberInputSteppers,
} from '@/components/ui/NumberInput';

const states = [
  { label: 'Empty', props: {} },
  { label: 'Disabled', props: { defaultValue: 12, disabled: true } },
  { label: 'Read-only', props: { defaultValue: 12, readOnly: true } },
  { label: 'Invalid', props: { defaultValue: 99 }, invalid: true },
];

export function NumberInputStatesExample() {
  return (
    <div className="grid w-fit grid-cols-[auto_15rem] items-center gap-x-6 gap-y-3 text-sm text-grayscale-opacity-700">
      {states.map(({ label, props, invalid }) => (
        <div key={label} className="contents">
          <span>{label}</span>
          <NumberInput {...props}>
            <NumberInputGroup>
              <NumberInputControl
                aria-invalid={invalid}
                placeholder="0"
              />
              <NumberInputSteppers />
            </NumberInputGroup>
          </NumberInput>
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Decimals

```tsx
import {
  NumberInput,
  NumberInputControl,
  NumberInputGroup,
  NumberInputSteppers,
} from '@/components/ui/NumberInput';

export function NumberInputDecimalsExample() {
  return (
    <div className="w-60">
      <NumberInput
        defaultValue={1.5}
        step={0.1}
        smallStep={0.01}
        largeStep={1}
      >
        <NumberInputGroup>
          <NumberInputControl placeholder="0.0" />
          <NumberInputSteppers />
        </NumberInputGroup>
      </NumberInput>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Currency Formatting

Pass `Intl.NumberFormatOptions` via `format` to render the value in any
locale-aware shape.

```tsx
import {
  NumberInput,
  NumberInputControl,
  NumberInputGroup,
  NumberInputSteppers,
} from '@/components/ui/NumberInput';

export function NumberInputFormattedCurrencyExample() {
  return (
    <div className="w-60">
      <NumberInput
        defaultValue={1234}
        format={{
          style: 'currency',
          currency: 'TWD',
          maximumFractionDigits: 0,
        }}
      >
        <NumberInputGroup>
          <NumberInputControl placeholder="NT$0" />
          <NumberInputSteppers />
        </NumberInputGroup>
      </NumberInput>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Controlled

Use `value` and `onValueChange` to drive the field from state. The
callback emits `null` when the input is empty.
Wrap a label in `NumberInputScrubArea` to let users drag it to change
the value.

```tsx
import {
  NumberInput,
  NumberInputControl,
  NumberInputGroup,
  NumberInputScrubArea,
  NumberInputScrubAreaCursor,
  NumberInputSteppers,
} from '@/components/ui/NumberInput';
import { Label } from '@/components/ui/Label';
import { useId, useState } from 'react';

export function NumberInputControlledExample() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState<number | null>(0);
  const id = useId();

  return (
    <div className="w-60">
      <NumberInput
        id={id}
        className="flex flex-col gap-2"
        value={value}
        onValueChange={setValue}
        min={-50}
        max={50}
        step={5}
      >
        <NumberInputGroup>
          <NumberInputControl placeholder="0" />
          <NumberInputSteppers />
        </NumberInputGroup>
        <NumberInputScrubArea>
          <Label htmlFor={id}>
            Current value: {value ?? 'empty'}
          </Label>
          <NumberInputScrubAreaCursor />
        </NumberInputScrubArea>
      </NumberInput>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Props

### NumberInput

`NumberInput` is the root component and accepts every Base UI
[`NumberField.Root`](https://base-ui.com/react/components/number-field#api-reference-numberfieldroot)
prop.

| Prop               | Type                                       | Default | Description                             |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------ | ------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `value`            | `number \| null`                           | —       | Controlled numeric value                |
| `defaultValue`     | `number`                                   | —       | Uncontrolled initial value              |
| `onValueChange`    | `(value, eventDetails) => void`            | —       | Called when the value changes           |
| `onValueCommitted` | `(value, eventDetails) => void`            | —       | Called when the value is committed      |
| `min`              | `number`                                   | —       | Minimum allowed value                   |
| `max`              | `number`                                   | —       | Maximum allowed value                   |
| `step`             | `number \| 'any'`                          | `1`     | Step for buttons, arrow keys, and wheel |
| `smallStep`        | `number`                                   | `0.1`   | Step when the meta key is held          |
| `largeStep`        | `number`                                   | `10`    | Step when the shift key is held         |
| `snapOnStep`       | `boolean`                                  | `false` | Snap to the nearest step when stepping  |
| `allowOutOfRange`  | `boolean`                                  | `false` | Allow typed values outside the min/max  |
| `allowWheelScrub`  | `boolean`                                  | `false` | Increment with the mouse wheel on focus |
| `format`           | `Intl.NumberFormatOptions`                 | —       | Locale-aware formatting options         |
| `locale`           | `Intl.LocalesArgument`                     | —       | Locale to format the value with         |
| `disabled`         | `boolean`                                  | `false` | Disables every part                     |
| `readOnly`         | `boolean`                                  | `false` | Prevents user-driven value changes      |
| `required`         | `boolean`                                  | `false` | Requires a value before form submit     |
| `name`             | `string`                                   | —       | Form field name                         |
| `id`               | `string`                                   | —       | Hidden input id                         |
| `inputRef`         | `Ref<HTMLInputElement>`                    | —       | Ref forwarded to the hidden input       |
| `className`        | `string \| (state) => string \| undefined` | —       | Additional classes for the root element |

### NumberInput Parts

| Part                         | Description                                                                     |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `NumberInputGroup`           | Visual shell with focus, disabled, and `aria-invalid` states                    |
| `NumberInputControl`         | The native input that displays and parses the formatted value                   |
| `NumberInputSteppers`        | Convenience layout that stacks the increment and decrement buttons on the right |
| `NumberInputIncrement`       | Stepper button that adds `step` to the value                                    |
| `NumberInputDecrement`       | Stepper button that subtracts `step` from the value                             |
| `NumberInputScrubArea`       | Optional region that scrubs the value with pointer drags                        |
| `NumberInputScrubAreaCursor` | Cursor element rendered while scrubbing                                         |

All parts forward refs to their underlying DOM elements and accept Base
UI `className` state functions.

# Pagination

> Composable page navigation with page links, first and last controls, and ellipsis.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/components/pagination

## Preview

```tsx
import {
  Pagination,
  PaginationContent,
  PaginationFirst,
  PaginationItem,
  PaginationLast,
  PaginationLink,
  PaginationNext,
  PaginationPrevious,
} from '@/components/ui/Pagination';
import { useState } from 'react';

const totalPages = 5;

export function PaginationExample() {
  const [page, setPage] = useState(2);

  return (
    <Pagination>
      <PaginationContent>
        <PaginationItem>
          <PaginationFirst
            render={<button type="button" />}
            disabled={page === 1}
            onClick={() => setPage(1)}
          />
        </PaginationItem>
        <PaginationItem>
          <PaginationPrevious
            render={<button type="button" />}
            disabled={page === 1}
            onClick={() => setPage(page - 1)}
          />
        </PaginationItem>
        {[1, 2, 3, 4, 5].map((value) => (
          <PaginationItem key={value}>
            <PaginationLink
              render={<button type="button" />}
              aria-label={`Page ${value}`}
              isActive={page === value}
              onClick={() => setPage(value)}
            >
              {value}
            </PaginationLink>
          </PaginationItem>
        ))}
        <PaginationItem>
          <PaginationNext
            render={<button type="button" />}
            disabled={page === totalPages}
            onClick={() => setPage(page + 1)}
          />
        </PaginationItem>
        <PaginationItem>
          <PaginationLast
            render={<button type="button" />}
            disabled={page === totalPages}
            onClick={() => setPage(totalPages)}
          />
        </PaginationItem>
      </PaginationContent>
    </Pagination>
  );
}
```

## Installation

After [configuring the registry](/docs/getting-started/installation), install Pagination:

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @vital-design/pagination
```

The registry also installs the theme, utilities, and the five icons used by Pagination. You do not need to install the full icon set.

## Usage

Compose a navigation landmark, a list, and a list item for each control. `PaginationLink` renders an anchor by default. Set `isActive` on the current page to add `aria-current="page"`.

```tsx
import {
  Pagination,
  PaginationContent,
  PaginationItem,
  PaginationLink,
  PaginationNext,
  PaginationPrevious,
} from '@/components/ui/Pagination';

export function PaginationLinksExample() {
  return (
    <Pagination>
      <PaginationContent>
        <PaginationItem>
          <PaginationPrevious href="?page=1">
            Previous
          </PaginationPrevious>
        </PaginationItem>
        {[1, 2, 3].map((page) => (
          <PaginationItem key={page}>
            <PaginationLink
              href={`?page=${page}`}
              isActive={page === 2}
            >
              {page}
            </PaginationLink>
          </PaginationItem>
        ))}
        <PaginationItem>
          <PaginationNext href="?page=3">Next</PaginationNext>
        </PaginationItem>
      </PaginationContent>
    </Pagination>
  );
}
```

## Client-side Pagination

For in-place updates, use `render` to compose a native button and keep the current page in your own state. Buttons retain their native Enter and Space behaviour. The preview at the top uses this pattern; its Code tab shows the full example.

Pagination does not calculate page ranges, load data, or own a current-page state. Keep the page count, visible page numbers, and data updates together in the consuming screen.

## More Pages

Use `PaginationEllipsis` for gaps in the visible range. Pass the hidden page numbers and `onPageSelect`. It renders the same button as the other page controls and opens a menu of those pages. This example keeps the current group of five pages visible. Choosing a page inside that group does not move the group. When ellipses appear on both sides, the first and last page numbers stay in those menus; the icon buttons still jump to those pages. Three-digit page numbers expand to fit.

```tsx
import {
  Pagination,
  PaginationContent,
  PaginationEllipsis,
  PaginationFirst,
  PaginationItem,
  PaginationLast,
  PaginationLink,
  PaginationNext,
  PaginationPrevious,
} from '@/components/ui/Pagination';
import { useState } from 'react';

const totalPages = 200;

export function PaginationMorePagesExample() {
  const [page, setPage] = useState(121);
  const current = Math.min(Math.max(page, 1), totalPages);
  const groupStart = Math.floor((current - 1) / 5) * 5 + 1;
  const groupEnd = Math.min(totalPages, groupStart + 4);
  const hasLeftGap = groupStart > 1;
  const hasRightGap = groupEnd < totalPages;
  const bothGaps = hasLeftGap && hasRightGap;
  const pages = Array.from(
    { length: groupEnd - groupStart + 1 },
    (_, index) => groupStart + index,
  );
  const leadingPage = hasLeftGap && !bothGaps ? 1 : undefined;
  const trailingPage =
    hasRightGap && !bothGaps ? totalPages : undefined;
  const leftHidden = hasLeftGap
    ? Array.from(
        { length: groupStart - (bothGaps ? 1 : 2) },
        (_, index) => (bothGaps ? 1 : 2) + index,
      )
    : [];
  const rightHidden = hasRightGap
    ? Array.from(
        {
          length: (bothGaps ? totalPages : totalPages - 1) - groupEnd,
        },
        (_, index) => groupEnd + 1 + index,
      )
    : [];

  return (
    <Pagination>
      <PaginationContent>
        <PaginationItem>
          <PaginationFirst
            render={<button type="button" />}
            disabled={page === 1}
            onClick={() => setPage(1)}
          />
        </PaginationItem>
        <PaginationItem>
          <PaginationPrevious
            render={<button type="button" />}
            disabled={page === 1}
            onClick={() => setPage(page - 1)}
          />
        </PaginationItem>
        {leadingPage !== undefined && (
          <PaginationItem>
            <PaginationLink
              render={<button type="button" />}
              aria-label={`Page ${leadingPage}`}
              isActive={page === leadingPage}
              onClick={() => setPage(leadingPage)}
            >
              {leadingPage}
            </PaginationLink>
          </PaginationItem>
        )}
        {leftHidden.length > 0 && (
          <PaginationItem>
            <PaginationEllipsis
              pages={leftHidden}
              onPageSelect={setPage}
            />
          </PaginationItem>
        )}
        {pages.map((value) => (
          <PaginationItem key={value}>
            <PaginationLink
              render={<button type="button" />}
              aria-label={`Page ${value}`}
              isActive={page === value}
              onClick={() => setPage(value)}
            >
              {value}
            </PaginationLink>
          </PaginationItem>
        ))}
        {rightHidden.length > 0 && (
          <PaginationItem>
            <PaginationEllipsis
              pages={rightHidden}
              onPageSelect={setPage}
            />
          </PaginationItem>
        )}
        {trailingPage !== undefined && (
          <PaginationItem>
            <PaginationLink
              render={<button type="button" />}
              aria-label={`Page ${trailingPage}`}
              isActive={page === trailingPage}
              onClick={() => setPage(trailingPage)}
            >
              {trailingPage}
            </PaginationLink>
          </PaginationItem>
        )}
        <PaginationItem>
          <PaginationNext
            render={<button type="button" />}
            disabled={page === totalPages}
            onClick={() => setPage(page + 1)}
          />
        </PaginationItem>
        <PaginationItem>
          <PaginationLast
            render={<button type="button" />}
            disabled={page === totalPages}
            onClick={() => setPage(totalPages)}
          />
        </PaginationItem>
      </PaginationContent>
    </Pagination>
  );
}
```

The preview's Code tab includes its page-range calculation. The calculation stays outside the Pagination primitive.

## First, Last, and Disabled Controls

`PaginationFirst` and `PaginationLast` follow the same API as `PaginationPrevious` and `PaginationNext`. Place each in a `PaginationItem`.

```tsx
<PaginationItem>
  <PaginationFirst
    render={<button type="button" />}
    disabled={page === 1}
    onClick={() => setPage(1)}
  />
</PaginationItem>
<PaginationItem>
  <PaginationLast
    render={<button type="button" />}
    disabled={page === totalPages}
    onClick={() => setPage(totalPages)}
  />
</PaginationItem>
```

Use `disabled` to block click and middle-click activation and remove a control from the tab order. A disabled default anchor also loses its `href` and retains its link semantics with `aria-disabled`. Setting only `aria-disabled` forwards that attribute without blocking activation.

## States

With a single page, every directional control is disabled. In a right-to-left layout, the directional icons mirror.

```tsx
import {
  Pagination,
  PaginationContent,
  PaginationFirst,
  PaginationItem,
  PaginationLast,
  PaginationLink,
  PaginationNext,
  PaginationPrevious,
} from '@/components/ui/Pagination';

const states = [
  { label: 'Single page', page: 1, totalPages: 1 },
  { label: 'Right to left', page: 2, totalPages: 5, dir: 'rtl' },
] as const;

export function PaginationStatesExample() {
  return (
    <div className="grid w-fit grid-cols-[auto_auto] items-center gap-x-6 gap-y-3 text-sm text-grayscale-opacity-700">
      {states.map((state) => (
        <div key={state.label} className="contents">
          <span>{state.label}</span>
          <div dir={'dir' in state ? state.dir : undefined}>
            <Pagination aria-label={state.label}>
              <PaginationContent>
                <PaginationItem>
                  <PaginationFirst
                    render={<button type="button" />}
                    disabled={state.page === 1}
                  />
                </PaginationItem>
                <PaginationItem>
                  <PaginationPrevious
                    render={<button type="button" />}
                    disabled={state.page === 1}
                  />
                </PaginationItem>
                {Array.from(
                  { length: state.totalPages },
                  (_, index) => index + 1,
                ).map((value) => (
                  <PaginationItem key={value}>
                    <PaginationLink
                      render={<button type="button" />}
                      aria-label={`Page ${value}`}
                      isActive={state.page === value}
                    >
                      {value}
                    </PaginationLink>
                  </PaginationItem>
                ))}
                <PaginationItem>
                  <PaginationNext
                    render={<button type="button" />}
                    disabled={state.page === state.totalPages}
                  />
                </PaginationItem>
                <PaginationItem>
                  <PaginationLast
                    render={<button type="button" />}
                    disabled={state.page === state.totalPages}
                  />
                </PaginationItem>
              </PaginationContent>
            </Pagination>
          </div>
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Labels and Router Links

Directional controls show icons by default. Supply children for a visible label and `aria-label` to localise the accessible name.

```tsx
<PaginationPrevious href="?page=1" aria-label="上一頁">
  上一頁
</PaginationPrevious>
<PaginationNext href="?page=3" aria-label="下一頁">
  下一頁
</PaginationNext>
```

Compose a router link through `render`; Pagination keeps link semantics. For example, with Next.js:

```tsx
import { PaginationLink } from '@/components/ui/Pagination';
import Link from 'next/link';

<PaginationLink render={<Link href="/products?page=2" />} isActive>
  2
</PaginationLink>;
```

The single-row table footer is the [Table Pagination](/docs/blocks/table-pagination) block. It places these page controls beside a page jump and a rows-per-page select. When the row is too narrow, the jump field and the page-size select hide.

To build a different footer, combine these parts with [Input](/docs/components/input) and [Select](/docs/components/select). Validate page bounds, and update the page when the page size or result count changes in your screen's state.

## Props

### Pagination, PaginationContent, and PaginationItem

These render `nav`, `ul`, and `li` respectively, forward native props and refs, and accept `className`. `Pagination` defaults to `aria-label="pagination"`; give each navigation landmark a distinct label when a page contains multiple paginators.

### PaginationLink

| Prop        | Type                              | Default | Description                                                                              |
| ----------- | --------------------------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `href`      | `string`                          | —       | Destination for the default anchor                                                       |
| `isActive`  | `boolean`                         | `false` | Highlights the page and sets `aria-current="page"`                                       |
| `disabled`  | `boolean`                         | `false` | Blocks clicks, removes the control from tab order, and omits the default anchor's `href` |
| `render`    | `ReactElement \| render function` | —       | Composes a router link or native button                                                  |
| `children`  | `ReactNode`                       | —       | Page number or custom content                                                            |
| `className` | `string`                          | —       | Additional CSS classes                                                                   |
| `...props`  | Anchor props                      | —       | Native attributes, events, and ref                                                       |

### Directional Controls

`PaginationFirst`, `PaginationPrevious`, `PaginationNext`, and `PaginationLast` accept `PaginationLink` props. Each provides an icon and a default accessible name such as “Go to next page”. Use `children` for an optional visible label and `aria-label` to override the accessible name. Directional icons mirror in RTL layouts.

### PaginationEllipsis

Renders a button that opens a menu of the omitted pages. `pages` is the list of page numbers in that gap. `onPageSelect` runs when a menu item is chosen. A string `children` replaces the accessible name, which defaults to “More pages”. The visible control stays the ellipsis icon.

### Data Slots

Each public part has a stable slot: `pagination`, `pagination-content`, `pagination-item`, `pagination-link`, `pagination-first`, `pagination-previous`, `pagination-next`, `pagination-last`, and `pagination-ellipsis`.

# Popover

> A floating panel anchored to a trigger element, used for tooltips with rich content, profile cards, and contextual overlays.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/components/popover

## Preview

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import {
  Popover,
  PopoverContent,
  PopoverDescription,
  PopoverTitle,
  PopoverTrigger,
} from '@/components/ui/Popover';

export function PopoverExample() {
  return (
    <Popover>
      <PopoverTrigger render={<Button>Open</Button>} />
      <PopoverContent className="w-72">
        <PopoverTitle>Popover title</PopoverTitle>
        <PopoverDescription className="mt-1">
          Popovers are floating panels that appear when triggered. Use
          them for short bits of information, action menus, or rich
          content overlays.
        </PopoverDescription>
      </PopoverContent>
    </Popover>
  );
}
```

## Usage

`Popover` is a thin styled wrapper around Base UI Popover. The trigger is render-prop based — pass any element via `render` and the popover wires up open state, focus, and ARIA attributes automatically.

## Placement

`PopoverContent` accepts `side` (`top` | `right` | `bottom` | `left`), `align` (`start` | `center` | `end`), and `sideOffset` props for positioning. Defaults are `align='start'`, `sideOffset=4`.

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import {
  Popover,
  PopoverContent,
  PopoverTrigger,
} from '@/components/ui/Popover';

const sides = ['top', 'right', 'bottom', 'left'] as const;

export function PopoverSidePlacementExample() {
  return (
    <div className="flex gap-4">
      {sides.map((side) => (
        <Popover key={side}>
          <PopoverTrigger
            render={<Button size="md">{side}</Button>}
          />
          <PopoverContent side={side} className="w-48">
            Anchored on the {side} side.
          </PopoverContent>
        </Popover>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

```tsx
<PopoverContent side="top" align="center" sideOffset={8}>
  …
</PopoverContent>
```

## Rich Content

The popup takes any content. Combine `PopoverTitle` and `PopoverDescription` with your own markup for profile cards and similar summaries.

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import {
  Popover,
  PopoverContent,
  PopoverDescription,
  PopoverTitle,
  PopoverTrigger,
} from '@/components/ui/Popover';

export function PopoverRichContentExample() {
  return (
    <Popover>
      <PopoverTrigger render={<Button>View profile</Button>} />
      <PopoverContent className="w-72">
        <PopoverTitle>Yuki Tanaka</PopoverTitle>
        <PopoverDescription className="mt-1">
          Senior Engineer · Tokyo
        </PopoverDescription>
        <p className="mt-3 text-sm text-grayscale-opacity-600">
          Joined the platform team in 2021. Owns the registry pipeline
          and the docs site deployment.
        </p>
      </PopoverContent>
    </Popover>
  );
}
```

## Multiple Triggers

One `Popover` root can serve several triggers. Give each `PopoverTrigger` a `payload`, and render the content from the `payload` the root passes to its function child. The popup moves to whichever trigger opened it.

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import {
  Popover,
  PopoverContent,
  PopoverDescription,
  PopoverTitle,
  PopoverTrigger,
} from '@/components/ui/Popover';

type Field = {
  label: string;
  description: string;
};

const fields = {
  assignee: {
    label: 'Alex Lin',
    description: 'Assigned owner for this editable cell.',
  },
  status: {
    label: 'In review',
    description: 'Shared content updates from the active trigger.',
  },
  date: {
    label: '2026/05/29',
    description: 'One popover root can serve many triggers.',
  },
} satisfies Record<string, Field>;

export function PopoverMultipleTriggersExample() {
  return (
    <Popover<Field>>
      {({ payload }) => (
        <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
          <PopoverTrigger
            payload={fields.assignee}
            render={<Button variant="ghost">Assignee</Button>}
          />
          <PopoverTrigger
            payload={fields.status}
            render={<Button variant="ghost">Status</Button>}
          />
          <PopoverTrigger
            payload={fields.date}
            render={<Button variant="ghost">Date</Button>}
          />
          <PopoverContent className="w-72">
            {payload && (
              <div className="space-y-1">
                <PopoverTitle>{payload.label}</PopoverTitle>
                <PopoverDescription>
                  {payload.description}
                </PopoverDescription>
              </div>
            )}
          </PopoverContent>
        </div>
      )}
    </Popover>
  );
}
```

## Custom Anchor

Pass `anchor` to position the popup against an element other than the trigger. A popover without a trigger, such as one opened from a menu item or a row action, needs it: control `open` yourself and point `anchor` at the element to align to. `anchor` accepts an element, a ref, a virtual element, or a function returning one.

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import {
  Item,
  ItemActions,
  ItemContent,
  ItemGroup,
  ItemSeparator,
  ItemTitle,
} from '@/components/ui/Item';
import {
  Popover,
  PopoverContent,
  PopoverDescription,
  PopoverTitle,
} from '@/components/ui/Popover';
import { Fragment, useState } from 'react';

type Person = {
  name: string;
  email: string;
};

const people: Person[] = [
  { name: 'Alex Lin', email: 'alex.lin@vikosmos.com' },
  { name: 'Jamie Chen', email: 'jamie.chen@vikosmos.com' },
  { name: 'Morgan Wu', email: 'morgan.wu@vikosmos.com' },
];

export function PopoverAnchorExample() {
  const [active, setActive] = useState<Person | null>(null);
  const [anchor, setAnchor] = useState<Element | null>(null);

  return (
    <>
      <ItemGroup className="w-80 max-w-full rounded border border-grayscale-opacity-300">
        {people.map((person, index) => (
          <Fragment key={person.name}>
            <Item size="list">
              <ItemContent>
                <ItemTitle>{person.name}</ItemTitle>
              </ItemContent>
              <ItemActions>
                <Button
                  variant="ghost"
                  size="md"
                  onClick={(event) => {
                    setAnchor(
                      event.currentTarget.closest(
                        '[data-slot="item"]',
                      ),
                    );
                    setActive(person);
                  }}
                >
                  Details
                </Button>
              </ItemActions>
            </Item>
            {index < people.length - 1 && <ItemSeparator />}
          </Fragment>
        ))}
      </ItemGroup>
      <Popover
        open={active !== null}
        onOpenChange={(open) => {
          if (!open) setActive(null);
        }}
      >
        <PopoverContent anchor={anchor} side="right" className="w-64">
          {active && (
            <div className="space-y-1">
              <PopoverTitle>{active.name}</PopoverTitle>
              <PopoverDescription>{active.email}</PopoverDescription>
            </div>
          )}
        </PopoverContent>
      </Popover>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Portal Container

`PopoverContent` portals to `document.body` by default. Pass `portalContainer` (an element or a ref) to render the popup inside another node instead.

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import {
  Popover,
  PopoverContent,
  PopoverDescription,
  PopoverTitle,
  PopoverTrigger,
} from '@/components/ui/Popover';
import { useRef } from 'react';

export function PopoverPortalContainerExample() {
  const scope = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);

  return (
    <div
      ref={scope}
      className="rounded border border-dashed border-grayscale-opacity-300 p-4"
    >
      <Popover>
        <PopoverTrigger
          render={<Button size="md">Open in scope</Button>}
        />
        <PopoverContent portalContainer={scope} className="w-64">
          <div className="space-y-1">
            <PopoverTitle>Scoped popup</PopoverTitle>
            <PopoverDescription>
              Rendered inside the dashed region, so styles scoped to
              it still apply.
            </PopoverDescription>
          </div>
        </PopoverContent>
      </Popover>
    </div>
  );
}
```

Use it when the popover must stay inside a CSS-scoped root — styles under a scope selector do not apply if the popup is portaled to `document.body`. It is also useful when body portaling breaks stacking or clipping (Dialog, transform, fullscreen, Shadow DOM).

## When to Use

| Need                                      | Component             |
| ----------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| Short overlay with rich content           | `Popover`             |
| Action menu (each item fires a callback)  | `DropdownMenu`        |
| Value picker (selection bound to a value) | `Select` / `Combobox` |
| Hierarchical path picker                  | `Command` + `Popover` |
| Searchable command palette                | `Command`             |

`Popover` is the bare floating panel — pair it with your own content. For action menus, prefer `DropdownMenu`; for value pickers, prefer the matched component.

## Props

### PopoverContent

`PopoverContent` is a composite of Portal + Positioner + Popup. Positioning props are forwarded to the Positioner; the popup accepts the usual Base UI Popover Popup props.

| Prop                    | Type                                                   | Default                       | Description                                           |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `align`                 | `'start' \| 'center' \| 'end'`                         | `'start'`                     | Alignment relative to the anchor                      |
| `alignOffset`           | `number`                                               | -                             | Offset along the alignment axis                       |
| `side`                  | `'top' \| 'right' \| 'bottom' \| 'left' \| …`          | `'bottom'`                    | Preferred side of the anchor                          |
| `sideOffset`            | `number`                                               | `4`                           | Distance from the anchor                              |
| `positionerClassName`   | `string`                                               | -                             | Classes on the Positioner wrapper                     |
| `className`             | `string`                                               | -                             | Additional classes on the popup                       |
| `anchor`                | `RefObject \| Element \| …`                            | -                             | Custom positioning anchor (defaults to the trigger)   |
| `arrowPadding`          | `number`                                               | `5`                           | Minimum space between the arrow and the popup's edges |
| `collisionAvoidance`    | `{ side?, align?, fallbackAxisSide? }`                 | `{ fallbackAxisSide: 'end' }` | How the popup flips or shifts to avoid collisions     |
| `collisionBoundary`     | `'clipping-ancestors' \| Element \| Element[] \| Rect` | `'clipping-ancestors'`        | Area the popup is kept inside                         |
| `collisionPadding`      | `number \| { top?, right?, bottom?, left? }`           | `5`                           | Space kept from the edge of the collision boundary    |
| `disableAnchorTracking` | `boolean`                                              | `false`                       | Stop following layout shifts of the anchor            |
| `positionMethod`        | `'absolute' \| 'fixed'`                                | `'absolute'`                  | CSS `position` of the positioner                      |
| `sticky`                | `boolean`                                              | `false`                       | Keep the popup in view after the anchor scrolls out   |
| `portalContainer`       | `HTMLElement \| ShadowRoot \| RefObject \| null`       | -                             | Custom portal container (defaults to `document.body`) |
| `keepMounted`           | `boolean`                                              | `false`                       | Keep the popup in the DOM while closed                |

## Exports

| Export               | Description                                                                       |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Popover`            | Root; manages open state                                                          |
| `PopoverTrigger`     | Render-prop trigger                                                               |
| `PopoverContent`     | Composite of Portal + Positioner + Popup; supports `anchor` and `portalContainer` |
| `PopoverPortal`      | Portal target (rarely used directly)                                              |
| `PopoverArrow`       | Optional pointer arrow                                                            |
| `PopoverClose`       | Close button slot                                                                 |
| `PopoverTitle`       | Accessible title styled for popups                                                |
| `PopoverDescription` | Accessible description styled for popups                                          |

# Progress

> Progress primitives and segmented status indicators.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/components/progress

## Preview

```tsx
import { Progress } from '@/components/ui/Progress';

export function ProgressExample() {
  return <Progress aria-label="Upload progress" value={64} />;
}
```

## With Label

```tsx
import {
  ProgressIndicator,
  ProgressLabel,
  ProgressRoot,
  ProgressTrack,
  ProgressValue,
} from '@/components/ui/Progress';

export function ProgressWithLabelExample() {
  return (
    <ProgressRoot value={42} className="w-80">
      <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
        <ProgressLabel>Export data</ProgressLabel>
        <ProgressValue />
      </div>
      <ProgressTrack>
        <ProgressIndicator />
      </ProgressTrack>
    </ProgressRoot>
  );
}
```

## Segments

```tsx
import {
  ProgressSegment,
  ProgressSegments,
} from '@/components/ui/Progress';

export function ProgressSegmentsExample() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-6">
      <ProgressSegments
        aria-label="Monthly status"
        className="w-[118px] gap-0.5"
      >
        <ProgressSegment className="w-2 bg-success-500" />
        <ProgressSegment className="w-2 bg-warning-500" />
        <ProgressSegment className="w-2 bg-grayscale-opacity-600" />
        <ProgressSegment className="w-2 bg-destructive-500" />
        {Array.from({ length: 8 }, (_, index) => (
          <ProgressSegment
            key={index}
            className="w-2"
            data-state="inactive"
          />
        ))}
      </ProgressSegments>
      <ProgressSegments
        aria-label="Quarterly status"
        className="w-[118px] gap-[3px]"
      >
        <ProgressSegment className="flex-1 bg-success-500" />
        <ProgressSegment className="flex-1 bg-warning-500" />
        <ProgressSegment className="flex-1 bg-grayscale-opacity-600" />
        <ProgressSegment className="flex-1" data-state="inactive" />
      </ProgressSegments>
      <ProgressSegments
        aria-label="Yearly status"
        className="w-[118px]"
      >
        <ProgressSegment className="flex-1 bg-success-500" />
      </ProgressSegments>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Connected Segments

```tsx
import {
  ProgressSegment,
  ProgressSegments,
} from '@/components/ui/Progress';

export function ProgressCustomSegmentsExample() {
  return (
    <ProgressSegments
      aria-label="Review status"
      className="w-[118px] gap-0"
      joint="connected"
    >
      <ProgressSegment
        aria-label="Complete"
        className="flex-1 bg-success-500"
      />
      <ProgressSegment
        aria-label="Pending review"
        className="flex-1 bg-warning-500"
      />
      <ProgressSegment
        aria-label="Waiting"
        className="flex-1 bg-grayscale-opacity-600"
      />
      <ProgressSegment
        aria-label="Not started"
        className="flex-1"
        data-state="inactive"
      />
    </ProgressSegments>
  );
}
```

## Parts

| Part                | Element  | Notes                                                                        |
| ------------------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Progress`          | `<div>`  | Shorthand root with track and indicator.                                     |
| `ProgressRoot`      | `<div>`  | Base UI progress root.                                                       |
| `ProgressTrack`     | `<div>`  | Visual track.                                                                |
| `ProgressIndicator` | `<div>`  | Filled progress indicator.                                                   |
| `ProgressLabel`     | `<span>` | Label linked to the progress root.                                           |
| `ProgressValue`     | `<span>` | Formatted value from the progress context.                                   |
| `ProgressSegments`  | `<div>`  | Compact segmented status display. Caller owns width, gap, count, and colors. |
| `ProgressSegment`   | `<span>` | Individual status segment.                                                   |

## Props

| Prop        | Type                      | Default    | Description                                            |
| ----------- | ------------------------- | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`     | `number` or `null`        | —          | Current progress value.                                |
| `min`       | `number`                  | `0`        | Minimum value.                                         |
| `max`       | `number`                  | `100`      | Maximum value.                                         |
| `className` | `string`                  | —          | Additional CSS classes.                                |
| `joint`     | `separate` or `connected` | `separate` | Segment edge behavior. Use `connected` for gap-0 bars. |

## Segment Layout

`ProgressSegments` only provides shared anatomy. Set segment width and gap at the call site.

```tsx
// Fixed ticks
<ProgressSegments className="gap-0.5">
  <ProgressSegment className="w-2 bg-success-500" />
</ProgressSegments>

// Fill available width
<ProgressSegments className="w-[118px] gap-[3px]">
  <ProgressSegment className="flex-1 bg-success-500" />
</ProgressSegments>

// Connected stacked bar
<ProgressSegments className="w-[118px] gap-0" joint="connected">
  <ProgressSegment className="flex-1 bg-grayscale-opacity-600" />
  <ProgressSegment className="flex-1 bg-warning-500" />
</ProgressSegments>
```

# RadioGroup

> A single-selection group of radio buttons.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/components/radio-group

## Preview

```tsx
import { Field, FieldLabel } from '@/components/ui/Field';
import {
  RadioGroup,
  RadioGroupItem,
} from '@/components/ui/RadioGroup';
import { useState } from 'react';

const options = [
  { label: 'Option A', value: 'a' },
  { label: 'Option B', value: 'b' },
  { label: 'Option C', value: 'c' },
];

export function RadioGroupExample() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState('a');

  return (
    <RadioGroup
      className="flex w-auto flex-wrap gap-4"
      value={value}
      onValueChange={setValue}
    >
      {options.map((option) => (
        <Field
          key={option.value}
          orientation="horizontal"
          className="w-auto"
        >
          <RadioGroupItem
            id={`radio-${option.value}`}
            value={option.value}
          />
          <FieldLabel htmlFor={`radio-${option.value}`}>
            {option.label}
          </FieldLabel>
        </Field>
      ))}
    </RadioGroup>
  );
}
```

## Usage

Wrap each `RadioGroupItem` and its `FieldLabel` in a horizontal `Field`, and pair the label's `htmlFor` with the item `id`. `RadioGroup` stacks items vertically by default; pass layout classes such as `flex flex-wrap gap-4` to put them in a row.

## Compound Items

Use `FieldContent` with a `FieldLabel` and `FieldDescription` when an option needs extra text.

```tsx
import {
  Field,
  FieldContent,
  FieldDescription,
  FieldLabel,
} from '@/components/ui/Field';
import {
  RadioGroup,
  RadioGroupItem,
} from '@/components/ui/RadioGroup';
import { useState } from 'react';

const plans = [
  {
    description: 'Good for individual use',
    label: 'Basic',
    value: 'basic',
  },
  {
    description: 'Recommended for teams',
    label: 'Pro',
    value: 'pro',
  },
];

export function RadioGroupCompoundItemsExample() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState('basic');

  return (
    <RadioGroup
      className="flex w-auto flex-wrap gap-4"
      value={value}
      onValueChange={setValue}
    >
      {plans.map((plan) => (
        <Field
          key={plan.value}
          orientation="horizontal"
          className="w-auto"
        >
          <RadioGroupItem
            id={`plan-${plan.value}`}
            value={plan.value}
          />
          <FieldContent>
            <FieldLabel htmlFor={`plan-${plan.value}`}>
              {plan.label}
            </FieldLabel>
            <FieldDescription>{plan.description}</FieldDescription>
          </FieldContent>
        </Field>
      ))}
    </RadioGroup>
  );
}
```

## Vertical Layout

```tsx
import { Field, FieldLabel } from '@/components/ui/Field';
import {
  RadioGroup,
  RadioGroupItem,
} from '@/components/ui/RadioGroup';
import { useState } from 'react';

const options = [
  { label: 'Option A', value: 'a' },
  { label: 'Option B', value: 'b' },
  { label: 'Option C', value: 'c' },
];

export function RadioGroupVerticalExample() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState('a');

  return (
    <RadioGroup
      className="w-auto gap-4"
      value={value}
      onValueChange={setValue}
    >
      {options.map((option) => (
        <Field key={option.value} orientation="horizontal">
          <RadioGroupItem
            id={`radio-vertical-${option.value}`}
            value={option.value}
          />
          <FieldLabel htmlFor={`radio-vertical-${option.value}`}>
            {option.label}
          </FieldLabel>
        </Field>
      ))}
    </RadioGroup>
  );
}
```

## States

Disable an item with `disabled` on `RadioGroupItem` and put `data-disabled` on its `Field` so the label dims too. Mark an invalid item with `aria-invalid`. Long labels wrap and stay aligned with the radio button.

```tsx
import { Field, FieldLabel } from '@/components/ui/Field';
import {
  RadioGroup,
  RadioGroupItem,
} from '@/components/ui/RadioGroup';

const states = [
  { label: 'Unchecked' },
  { label: 'Checked', checked: true },
  { label: 'Invalid', invalid: true },
  { label: 'Disabled', disabled: true },
  { label: 'Checked & disabled', checked: true, disabled: true },
  {
    label: 'Long label',
    checked: true,
    text: 'A long option label that wraps onto the next line and stays aligned with the radio button',
  },
];

export function RadioGroupStatesExample() {
  return (
    <div className="grid w-fit grid-cols-[auto_15rem] items-start gap-x-6 gap-y-3 text-sm text-grayscale-opacity-700">
      {states.map(({ label, checked, invalid, disabled, text }) => {
        const id = `radio-state-${label.toLowerCase().replace(/\W+/g, '-')}`;

        return (
          <div key={label} className="contents">
            <span className="leading-5">{label}</span>
            <RadioGroup
              aria-label={label}
              defaultValue={checked ? 'option' : undefined}
            >
              <Field
                orientation="horizontal"
                data-disabled={disabled}
              >
                <RadioGroupItem
                  aria-invalid={invalid}
                  disabled={disabled}
                  id={id}
                  value="option"
                />
                <FieldLabel htmlFor={id}>
                  {text ?? 'Option'}
                </FieldLabel>
              </Field>
            </RadioGroup>
          </div>
        );
      })}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Props

### RadioGroup

| Prop            | Type             | Default | Description                          |
| --------------- | ---------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `value`         | `string`         | —       | Currently selected value             |
| `defaultValue`  | `string`         | —       | Initial value for uncontrolled usage |
| `onValueChange` | Base UI callback | —       | Called when selection changes        |
| `className`     | `string`         | —       | Additional CSS classes               |

### RadioGroupItem

| Prop       | Type      | Default | Description                 |
| ---------- | --------- | ------- | --------------------------- |
| `value`    | `string`  | —       | **Required.** Option value  |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables this specific item |

# Resizable

> Accessible resizable panels backed by react-resizable-panels.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/components/resizable

## Preview

```tsx
import {
  ResizableHandle,
  ResizablePanel,
  ResizablePanelGroup,
} from '@/components/ui/Resizable';

function PanelContent({ children }: { children: string }) {
  return (
    <div className="flex h-full items-center justify-center p-6 font-sans text-sm font-medium text-grayscale-opacity-800">
      {children}
    </div>
  );
}

export function ResizableExample() {
  return (
    <ResizablePanelGroup
      orientation="horizontal"
      className="min-h-[200px] max-w-md rounded-md border border-grayscale-opacity-300"
    >
      <ResizablePanel defaultSize="50%">
        <PanelContent>One</PanelContent>
      </ResizablePanel>
      <ResizableHandle />
      <ResizablePanel defaultSize="50%">
        <ResizablePanelGroup orientation="vertical">
          <ResizablePanel defaultSize="35%">
            <PanelContent>Two</PanelContent>
          </ResizablePanel>
          <ResizableHandle />
          <ResizablePanel defaultSize="65%">
            <PanelContent>Three</PanelContent>
          </ResizablePanel>
        </ResizablePanelGroup>
      </ResizablePanel>
    </ResizablePanelGroup>
  );
}
```

## Usage

`Resizable` wraps
[`react-resizable-panels`](https://github.com/bvaughn/react-resizable-panels).
Compose `ResizablePanelGroup` with `ResizablePanel` children separated
by `ResizableHandle`. Nest groups to build mixed horizontal/vertical
layouts.

## Vertical

```tsx
import {
  ResizableHandle,
  ResizablePanel,
  ResizablePanelGroup,
} from '@/components/ui/Resizable';

function PanelContent({ children }: { children: string }) {
  return (
    <div className="flex h-full items-center justify-center p-6 font-sans text-sm font-medium text-grayscale-opacity-800">
      {children}
    </div>
  );
}

export function ResizableVerticalExample() {
  return (
    <ResizablePanelGroup
      orientation="vertical"
      className="min-h-[240px] max-w-md rounded-md border border-grayscale-opacity-300"
    >
      <ResizablePanel defaultSize="30%">
        <PanelContent>Header</PanelContent>
      </ResizablePanel>
      <ResizableHandle />
      <ResizablePanel defaultSize="70%">
        <PanelContent>Content</PanelContent>
      </ResizablePanel>
    </ResizablePanelGroup>
  );
}
```

## With Handle

Pass `withHandle` to `ResizableHandle` to render a visible drag
indicator. Use a `minSize` on a panel to prevent it from collapsing.

```tsx
import {
  ResizableHandle,
  ResizablePanel,
  ResizablePanelGroup,
} from '@/components/ui/Resizable';

function PanelContent({ children }: { children: string }) {
  return (
    <div className="flex h-full items-center justify-center p-6 font-sans text-sm font-medium text-grayscale-opacity-800">
      {children}
    </div>
  );
}

export function ResizableWithHandleExample() {
  return (
    <ResizablePanelGroup
      orientation="horizontal"
      className="min-h-[200px] max-w-md rounded-md border border-grayscale-opacity-300"
    >
      <ResizablePanel defaultSize="30%" minSize="20%">
        <PanelContent>Sidebar</PanelContent>
      </ResizablePanel>
      <ResizableHandle withHandle />
      <ResizablePanel defaultSize="70%">
        <PanelContent>Content</PanelContent>
      </ResizablePanel>
    </ResizablePanelGroup>
  );
}
```

## Parts

| Part                  | Description                                                 |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ResizablePanelGroup` | Layout container; sets `horizontal` or `vertical` direction |
| `ResizablePanel`      | Resizable region inside a group                             |
| `ResizableHandle`     | Drag handle separator between two panels                    |

## ResizablePanelGroup Props

Accepts every prop from `react-resizable-panels`'s
[`PanelGroup`](https://github.com/bvaughn/react-resizable-panels#panelgroup).

| Prop          | Type                         | Default        | Description                     |
| ------------- | ---------------------------- | -------------- | ------------------------------- |
| `orientation` | `'horizontal' \| 'vertical'` | `'horizontal'` | Layout direction                |
| `autoSaveId`  | `string`                     | —              | Persist sizes in `localStorage` |
| `className`   | `string`                     | —              | Additional CSS classes          |

## ResizablePanel Props

Accepts every prop from `react-resizable-panels`'s
[`Panel`](https://github.com/bvaughn/react-resizable-panels#panel).

| Prop          | Type               | Default | Description                              |
| ------------- | ------------------ | ------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `defaultSize` | `number \| string` | —       | Initial size as percentage               |
| `minSize`     | `number \| string` | —       | Minimum size before collapse             |
| `maxSize`     | `number \| string` | —       | Maximum size                             |
| `collapsible` | `boolean`          | `false` | Allow collapsing past `collapsedSize`    |
| `id`          | `string`           | —       | Required if `autoSaveId` is set on group |

## ResizableHandle Props

| Prop         | Type      | Default | Description                      |
| ------------ | --------- | ------- | -------------------------------- |
| `withHandle` | `boolean` | `false` | Renders a visible grip indicator |
| `disabled`   | `boolean` | `false` | Disables dragging                |
| `className`  | `string`  | —       | Additional CSS classes           |

# Scroll Area

> Scrollable viewport with optional edge fade.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/components/scroll-area

## Preview

```tsx
import {
  ScrollArea,
  ScrollAreaScrollbar,
  ScrollAreaThumb,
  ScrollAreaViewport,
} from '@/components/ui/ScrollArea';

const items = Array.from({ length: 24 }, (_, index) => ({
  label: `Activity ${index + 1}`,
  description:
    index % 3 === 0
      ? 'Needs review before publish'
      : 'Synced with the workspace',
}));

export function ScrollAreaVerticalExample() {
  return (
    <ScrollArea className="h-64 w-80 rounded border border-grayscale-opacity-200 bg-background">
      <ScrollAreaViewport className="h-full">
        <div className="flex flex-col py-2">
          {items.map((item) => (
            <div key={item.label} className="px-4 py-2">
              <div className="text-sm leading-5 font-medium text-grayscale-opacity-800">
                {item.label}
              </div>
              <div className="text-xs leading-4 text-grayscale-opacity-500">
                {item.description}
              </div>
            </div>
          ))}
        </div>
      </ScrollAreaViewport>
      <ScrollAreaScrollbar>
        <ScrollAreaThumb />
      </ScrollAreaScrollbar>
    </ScrollArea>
  );
}
```

## Edge Fade

Use `fadeEdges` on the viewport when the edge fade should be CSS-driven.
Set `overflowEdgeThreshold` on `ScrollArea` to tune when Base UI exposes
the overflow CSS variables.

```tsx
import {
  ScrollArea,
  ScrollAreaViewport,
} from '@/components/ui/ScrollArea';

const items = Array.from({ length: 24 }, (_, index) => ({
  label: `Activity ${index + 1}`,
  description:
    index % 3 === 0
      ? 'Needs review before publish'
      : 'Synced with the workspace',
}));

export function ScrollAreaFadeEdgesExample() {
  return (
    <ScrollArea
      className="h-64 w-80 rounded border border-grayscale-opacity-200 bg-background"
      overflowEdgeThreshold={1}
    >
      <ScrollAreaViewport className="h-full" fadeEdges>
        <div className="flex flex-col py-2">
          {items.map((item) => (
            <div key={item.label} className="px-4 py-2">
              <div className="text-sm leading-5 font-medium text-grayscale-opacity-800">
                {item.label}
              </div>
              <div className="text-xs leading-4 text-grayscale-opacity-500">
                {item.description}
              </div>
            </div>
          ))}
        </div>
      </ScrollAreaViewport>
    </ScrollArea>
  );
}
```

## Select Composition

`ScrollArea` is not built into picker primitives. Compose it when a
specific surface needs fade edges or custom scrollbars.

```tsx
<SelectContent
  className="h-75 py-0"
  listRender={
    <ScrollAreaViewport className="h-full py-2" fadeEdges />
  }
  listWrapper={(list) => (
    <ScrollArea className="h-full min-h-0" overflowEdgeThreshold={1}>
      {list}
    </ScrollArea>
  )}
  showScrollButtons={false}
>
  {items.map((item) => (
    <SelectItem key={item.value} value={item.value}>
      <SelectItemText>{item.label}</SelectItemText>
      <SelectItemCheck />
    </SelectItem>
  ))}
</SelectContent>
```

## Exports

| Export                | Description                         |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| `ScrollArea`          | Root scroll area container          |
| `ScrollAreaViewport`  | Scrollable viewport; supports fade  |
| `ScrollAreaContent`   | Optional content wrapper            |
| `ScrollAreaScrollbar` | Custom scrollbar track              |
| `ScrollAreaThumb`     | Custom scrollbar thumb              |
| `ScrollAreaCorner`    | Corner slot for two-axis scrollbars |

## Props

| Prop        | Type                          | Default | Description                |
| ----------- | ----------------------------- | ------- | -------------------------- |
| `fadeEdges` | `boolean`                     | `false` | Applies CSS edge fade mask |
| `fadeSize`  | `number \| string`            | `40`    | Fade size for each edge    |
| `className` | `string`                      | —       | Additional CSS classes     |
| `style`     | `CSSProperties`               | —       | Inline styles              |
| `...props`  | `ComponentProps<typeof Base>` | —       | Base UI scroll area props  |

# SearchBar

> A search input with an icon. Supports instant onChange and explicit onSearch (Enter / icon click).

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/components/search-bar

## Preview

```tsx
import { SearchBar } from '@/components/ui/SearchBar';
import { useState } from 'react';

export function SearchBarExample() {
  const [lastSearch, setLastSearch] = useState('');

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col items-center gap-2">
      <SearchBar
        aria-label="Search"
        isSearchIconClickable
        placeholder="Search..."
        width="280px"
        onSearch={setLastSearch}
      />
      {lastSearch && (
        <p className="text-sm text-grayscale-opacity-500">
          Searched: <strong>{lastSearch}</strong>
        </p>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Usage

`onChange` fires on every keystroke with the current value. `onSearch` fires when the user presses Enter, or clicks the search icon when `isSearchIconClickable` is set. The example above shows the last submitted query.

## States

Use `disabled` to disable the search bar. Long values truncate with an ellipsis.

```tsx
import { SearchBar } from '@/components/ui/SearchBar';

const states = [
  { label: 'Placeholder', props: {} },
  { label: 'Filled', props: { defaultValue: 'Vital Design' } },
  {
    label: 'Long value',
    props: {
      defaultValue: 'A long search query that does not fit the field',
    },
  },
  { label: 'Disabled', props: { disabled: true } },
];

export function SearchBarStatesExample() {
  return (
    <div className="grid w-fit grid-cols-[auto_17.5rem] items-center gap-x-6 gap-y-3 text-sm text-grayscale-opacity-700">
      {states.map(({ label, props }) => (
        <div key={label} className="contents">
          <span>{label}</span>
          <SearchBar
            aria-label={label}
            placeholder="Search..."
            {...props}
          />
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Props

| Prop                    | Type                      | Default | Description                                       |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `value`                 | `string`                  | —       | Controlled value                                  |
| `defaultValue`          | `string`                  | —       | Uncontrolled initial value                        |
| `placeholder`           | `string`                  | —       | Placeholder text                                  |
| `onChange`              | `(value: string) => void` | —       | Called on every keystroke                         |
| `onSearch`              | `(value: string) => void` | —       | Called when Enter is pressed or icon is clicked   |
| `isSearchIconClickable` | `boolean`                 | `false` | Makes the search icon trigger `onSearch` on click |
| `disabled`              | `boolean`                 | `false` | Disables the input                                |
| `width`                 | `string`                  | —       | Custom width (e.g., `'300px'`)                    |
| `className`             | `string`                  | —       | Classes for the InputGroup shell                  |
| `style`                 | `CSSProperties`           | —       | Inline styles for the InputGroup shell            |

Every other `<input>` prop (`id`, `name`, `aria-label`, `autoFocus`,
`inputMode`, `enterKeyHint`, `onBlur`, …) is forwarded to the inner input, and
`ref` points at that input.

## Controlled vs uncontrolled

Pass `value` when something outside the component owns the query — a URL search
param, a "clear all filters" button, or a suggestion chip that fills the field.
Pass `defaultValue` instead when the input itself is the only source of truth
and `onChange` just feeds a request. Setting both makes `defaultValue` inert.

```tsx
// Controlled: the query string owns the value, so clearing it clears the input
<SearchBar
  value={query}
  onChange={setQuery}
  onSearch={(value) => router.push(`?q=${value}`)}
/>
```

# Select

> A dropdown for choosing one or many options from a flat list.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/components/select

## Preview

```tsx
import {
  Select,
  SelectContent,
  SelectItem,
  SelectItemCheck,
  SelectItemText,
  SelectTrigger,
} from '@/components/ui/Select';
import { useState } from 'react';

const items = [
  { label: 'Option 1', value: '1' },
  { label: 'Option 2', value: '2' },
  { label: 'Option 3', value: '3' },
];

export function SelectExample() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState<string | null>(null);

  return (
    <div className="w-50">
      <Select items={items} value={value} onValueChange={setValue}>
        <SelectTrigger placeholder="Select an option" />
        <SelectContent>
          {items.map((item) => (
            <SelectItem key={item.value} value={item.value}>
              <SelectItemText>{item.label}</SelectItemText>
              <SelectItemCheck />
            </SelectItem>
          ))}
        </SelectContent>
      </Select>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Usage

`Select` is a thin styled wrapper around Base UI Select. The root is `BaseSelect.Root`; layout belongs to the parent wrapper.

Use `Select` for flat value picking. If the trigger needs custom visuals, keep `Select` as the root and customize `SelectTrigger`; do not move the picker into `DropdownMenu`.

## Multiple

```tsx
import {
  Select,
  SelectContent,
  SelectItem,
  SelectItemCheckbox,
  SelectItemText,
  SelectTrigger,
} from '@/components/ui/Select';
import { useState } from 'react';

const frameworks = [
  { label: 'React', value: 'react' },
  { label: 'Vue', value: 'vue' },
  { label: 'Angular', value: 'angular' },
];

export function SelectMultipleExample() {
  const [values, setValues] = useState<string[]>([]);

  return (
    <div className="w-60">
      <Select
        multiple
        items={frameworks}
        value={values}
        onValueChange={setValues}
      >
        <SelectTrigger placeholder="Select options" />
        <SelectContent>
          {frameworks.map((item) => (
            <SelectItem key={item.value} value={item.value}>
              <SelectItemCheckbox />
              <SelectItemText>{item.label}</SelectItemText>
            </SelectItem>
          ))}
        </SelectContent>
      </Select>
    </div>
  );
}
```

Use `Combobox` for searchable pickers, autocomplete, or removable chip values.

## When to Choose What

| Need                                 | Use                   |
| ------------------------------------ | --------------------- |
| Flat single or multiple value picker | `Select`              |
| Searchable picker or tag picker      | `Combobox`            |
| Hierarchical path picker             | `Command` + `Popover` |
| Command menu with callbacks          | `DropdownMenu`        |

## Exports

```tsx
import {
  Select,
  SelectContent,
  SelectGroup,
  SelectItem,
  SelectItemCheck,
  SelectItemCheckbox,
  SelectItemText,
  SelectLabel,
  SelectScrollDownButton,
  SelectScrollUpButton,
  SelectSeparator,
  SelectTrigger,
  SelectValue,
} from '@/components/ui/Select';
```

## With Grouped Items

```tsx
import {
  Select,
  SelectContent,
  SelectGroup,
  SelectItem,
  SelectItemCheck,
  SelectItemText,
  SelectLabel,
  SelectSeparator,
  SelectTrigger,
} from '@/components/ui/Select';
import { useState } from 'react';

const fruits = [
  { label: 'Apple', value: 'apple' },
  { label: 'Banana', value: 'banana' },
];

const vegetables = [
  { label: 'Carrot', value: 'carrot' },
  { label: 'Broccoli', value: 'broccoli' },
];

export function SelectGroupedExample() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState<string | null>(null);

  return (
    <div className="w-50">
      <Select
        items={[...fruits, ...vegetables]}
        value={value}
        onValueChange={setValue}
      >
        <SelectTrigger placeholder="Select food" />
        <SelectContent>
          <SelectGroup>
            <SelectLabel>Fruits</SelectLabel>
            {fruits.map((item) => (
              <SelectItem key={item.value} value={item.value}>
                <SelectItemText>{item.label}</SelectItemText>
                <SelectItemCheck />
              </SelectItem>
            ))}
          </SelectGroup>
          <SelectSeparator />
          <SelectGroup>
            <SelectLabel>Vegetables</SelectLabel>
            {vegetables.map((item) => (
              <SelectItem key={item.value} value={item.value}>
                <SelectItemText>{item.label}</SelectItemText>
                <SelectItemCheck />
              </SelectItem>
            ))}
          </SelectGroup>
        </SelectContent>
      </Select>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## With Icons

Put an icon before `SelectItemText` in each item.

```tsx
import {
  Select,
  SelectContent,
  SelectItem,
  SelectItemCheck,
  SelectItemText,
  SelectTrigger,
} from '@/components/ui/Select';
import { BellIcon } from '@/components/icons/BellIcon';
import { InboxIcon } from '@/components/icons/InboxIcon';
import { UserIcon } from '@/components/icons/UserIcon';
import { useState } from 'react';

const channels = [
  { label: 'Notifications', value: 'notifications', Icon: BellIcon },
  { label: 'Inbox', value: 'inbox', Icon: InboxIcon },
  { label: 'Profile', value: 'profile', Icon: UserIcon },
];

export function SelectIconExample() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState<string | null>(null);

  return (
    <div className="w-50">
      <Select items={channels} value={value} onValueChange={setValue}>
        <SelectTrigger placeholder="Select a page" />
        <SelectContent>
          {channels.map((item) => (
            <SelectItem key={item.value} value={item.value}>
              <item.Icon className="size-4 shrink-0 text-grayscale-opacity-700" />
              <SelectItemText>{item.label}</SelectItemText>
              <SelectItemCheck />
            </SelectItem>
          ))}
        </SelectContent>
      </Select>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## States

Disable the whole select with `disabled` on `Select`, and mark an invalid value with `aria-invalid` on `SelectTrigger`. Long values truncate with an ellipsis.

```tsx
import {
  Select,
  SelectContent,
  SelectItem,
  SelectItemCheck,
  SelectItemText,
  SelectTrigger,
} from '@/components/ui/Select';

const items = [
  { label: 'Option 1', value: '1' },
  { label: 'Option 2', value: '2' },
  {
    label: 'A long option label that does not fit the trigger',
    value: 'long',
  },
];

const states = [
  { label: 'Placeholder', props: {} },
  { label: 'Selected', props: { defaultValue: '1' } },
  { label: 'Long value', props: { defaultValue: 'long' } },
  { label: 'Disabled', props: { disabled: true } },
  { label: 'Invalid', props: {}, invalid: true },
];

export function SelectStatesExample() {
  return (
    <div className="grid grid-cols-[auto_12.5rem] items-center gap-x-6 gap-y-3 text-sm text-grayscale-opacity-700">
      {states.map(({ label, props, invalid }) => (
        <div key={label} className="contents">
          <span>{label}</span>
          <Select items={items} {...props}>
            <SelectTrigger
              aria-invalid={invalid}
              placeholder="Select an option"
            />
            <SelectContent>
              {items.map((item) => (
                <SelectItem key={item.value} value={item.value}>
                  <SelectItemText>{item.label}</SelectItemText>
                  <SelectItemCheck />
                </SelectItem>
              ))}
            </SelectContent>
          </Select>
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Props

`Select` accepts Base UI `Select.Root` props. Pass `items` when you want `SelectValue` to render labels instead of raw values.

### SelectContent

`SelectContent` is a composite of Portal + Positioner + Popup. Positioning props go to the Positioner; `portalContainer` goes to the Portal.

| Prop                    | Type                                                   | Default                        | Description                                               |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `align`                 | `'start' \| 'center' \| 'end'`                         | `'start'`                      | Alignment relative to the anchor                          |
| `alignItemWithTrigger`  | `boolean`                                              | `false`                        | Overlap the trigger so the selected item lines up with it |
| `alignOffset`           | `number`                                               | `0`                            | Offset along the alignment axis                           |
| `side`                  | `'top' \| 'right' \| 'bottom' \| 'left' \| …`          | `'bottom'`                     | Preferred side of the anchor                              |
| `sideOffset`            | `number`                                               | `4`                            | Distance from the anchor                                  |
| `anchor`                | `RefObject \| Element \| …`                            | —                              | Custom positioning anchor (defaults to the trigger)       |
| `arrowPadding`          | `number`                                               | `5`                            | Minimum space between the arrow and the popup's edges     |
| `collisionAvoidance`    | `{ side?, align?, fallbackAxisSide? }`                 | `{ fallbackAxisSide: 'none' }` | How the popup flips or shifts to avoid collisions         |
| `collisionBoundary`     | `'clipping-ancestors' \| Element \| Element[] \| Rect` | `'clipping-ancestors'`         | Area the popup is kept inside                             |
| `collisionPadding`      | `number \| { top?, right?, bottom?, left? }`           | `5`                            | Space kept from the edge of the collision boundary        |
| `disableAnchorTracking` | `boolean`                                              | `false`                        | Stop following layout shifts of the anchor                |
| `positionMethod`        | `'absolute' \| 'fixed'`                                | `'absolute'`                   | CSS `position` of the positioner                          |
| `sticky`                | `boolean`                                              | `false`                        | Keep the popup in view after the anchor scrolls out       |
| `portalContainer`       | `HTMLElement \| ShadowRoot \| RefObject \| null`       | —                              | Custom portal container (defaults to `document.body`)     |

### SelectTrigger

| Prop          | Type        | Default | Description                               |
| ------------- | ----------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `placeholder` | `ReactNode` | `''`    | Placeholder text when nothing is selected |

### SelectItem

| Prop       | Type               | Default | Description        |
| ---------- | ------------------ | ------- | ------------------ |
| `value`    | `string \| number` | —       | Item value         |
| `children` | `ReactNode`        | —       | Item content       |
| `disabled` | `boolean`          | `false` | Disables this item |

Use `<SelectItemText>`, `<SelectItemCheck>`, and `<SelectItemCheckbox>` inside items for the visual affordance you need.

```tsx
import { Separator } from '@/components/ui/Separator';
```

```tsx
import { Separator } from '@/components/ui/Separator';
```

```tsx
  return (
    <div className="flex w-80 flex-col">
      <span className="px-5 py-1.5 text-sm leading-5 text-grayscale-opacity-800">
        First row
      </span>

      </span>
```
