## Selected row state

Apply `data-state="selected"` to a row to highlight it.

```tsx
<TableRow data-state="selected">…</TableRow>
```

```tsx
import {
  Table,
  TableBody,
  TableCell,
  TableHead,
  TableHeader,
  TableRow,
} from '@/components/ui/Table';

export function TableSelectedRowExample() {
  return (
    <Table>
      <TableHeader>
        <TableRow>
          <TableHead>Invoice</TableHead>
          <TableHead>Status</TableHead>
          <TableHead className="text-right">Amount</TableHead>
        </TableRow>
      </TableHeader>
      <TableBody>
        <TableRow data-state="selected">
          <TableCell className="font-medium">INV001</TableCell>
          <TableCell>Paid</TableCell>
          <TableCell className="text-right">$250.00</TableCell>
        </TableRow>
        <TableRow>
          <TableCell className="font-medium">INV002</TableCell>
          <TableCell>Pending</TableCell>
          <TableCell className="text-right">$150.00</TableCell>
        </TableRow>
      </TableBody>
    </Table>
  );
}
```

# Table of Contents

> A compact rail of section ticks that expands into the full list of headings on hover or focus.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/components/table-of-contents

## Preview

```tsx
import {
  TableOfContents,
  type TableOfContentsItem,
} from '@/components/ui/TableOfContents';

const items: TableOfContentsItem[] = [
  { id: 'introduction', label: 'Introduction', level: 1 },
  { id: 'getting-started', label: 'Getting started', level: 2 },
  { id: 'install', label: 'Install', level: 3 },
  { id: 'configure', label: 'Configure', level: 3 },
  { id: 'theme', label: 'Theme', level: 3 },
  { id: 'tokens', label: 'Tokens', level: 3 },
  { id: 'icons', label: 'Icons', level: 3 },
  { id: 'fonts', label: 'Fonts', level: 3 },
  { id: 'dark-mode', label: 'Dark mode', level: 3 },
  { id: 'components', label: 'Components', level: 1 },
  { id: 'inputs', label: 'Inputs', level: 2 },
  { id: 'button', label: 'Button', level: 3 },
  { id: 'checkbox', label: 'Checkbox', level: 3 },
  { id: 'select', label: 'Select', level: 3 },
  { id: 'switch', label: 'Switch', level: 3 },
];

export function TableOfContentsExample() {
  return (
    <div className="flex min-h-100 w-full items-start justify-between gap-8">
      <div className="max-w-sm space-y-2 text-sm leading-5 text-grayscale-opacity-600">
        <p className="font-medium text-grayscale-opacity-800">
          Hover the rail on the right →
        </p>
        <p>
          The rail expands into the full list on hover or keyboard
          focus, and collapses when the pointer or focus leaves.
        </p>
      </div>
      <TableOfContents items={items} defaultValue="install" />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Installation

After [configuring the registry](/docs/getting-started/installation), install Table of Contents:

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @vital-design/table-of-contents
```

## Usage

Pass the page's headings as `items`. Each item renders a tick on the rail: level 1 is the longest, level 3 the shortest. The active item's tick turns primary.

At rest only the rail shows. Hovering it, or moving keyboard focus into it, opens a panel with every label; the panel closes when the pointer or focus leaves. You don't need to pass `expanded` for this.

Each item links to `#<id>` unless you give it an `href`. Clicking an item makes it active; set the starting one with `defaultValue`.

## Left Side

Set `side="left"` when the rail sits on the left of the content. The ticks align left and the panel opens to the right.

```tsx
import {
  TableOfContents,
  type TableOfContentsItem,
} from '@/components/ui/TableOfContents';

const items: TableOfContentsItem[] = [
  { id: 'introduction', label: 'Introduction', level: 1 },
  { id: 'getting-started', label: 'Getting started', level: 2 },
  { id: 'install', label: 'Install', level: 3 },
  { id: 'configure', label: 'Configure', level: 3 },
  { id: 'theme', label: 'Theme', level: 3 },
  { id: 'tokens', label: 'Tokens', level: 3 },
  { id: 'icons', label: 'Icons', level: 3 },
  { id: 'fonts', label: 'Fonts', level: 3 },
  { id: 'dark-mode', label: 'Dark mode', level: 3 },
  { id: 'components', label: 'Components', level: 1 },
  { id: 'inputs', label: 'Inputs', level: 2 },
  { id: 'button', label: 'Button', level: 3 },
  { id: 'checkbox', label: 'Checkbox', level: 3 },
  { id: 'select', label: 'Select', level: 3 },
  { id: 'switch', label: 'Switch', level: 3 },
];

export function TableOfContentsLeftExample() {
  return (
    <div className="min-h-100">
      <TableOfContents
        items={items}
        defaultValue="install"
        side="left"
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Controlled

Pass `value` and `onValueChange` to own the active item, for example to follow the section in view as the page scrolls. Clicking an item calls `onValueChange`; the active item only moves when you update `value`.

```tsx
import {
  TableOfContents,
  type TableOfContentsItem,
} from '@/components/ui/TableOfContents';
import { useState } from 'react';

const items: TableOfContentsItem[] = [
  { id: 'introduction', label: 'Introduction', level: 1 },
  { id: 'getting-started', label: 'Getting started', level: 2 },
  { id: 'install', label: 'Install', level: 3 },
  { id: 'configure', label: 'Configure', level: 3 },
  { id: 'theme', label: 'Theme', level: 3 },
  { id: 'tokens', label: 'Tokens', level: 3 },
  { id: 'icons', label: 'Icons', level: 3 },
  { id: 'fonts', label: 'Fonts', level: 3 },
  { id: 'dark-mode', label: 'Dark mode', level: 3 },
  { id: 'components', label: 'Components', level: 1 },
  { id: 'inputs', label: 'Inputs', level: 2 },
  { id: 'button', label: 'Button', level: 3 },
  { id: 'checkbox', label: 'Checkbox', level: 3 },
  { id: 'select', label: 'Select', level: 3 },
  { id: 'switch', label: 'Switch', level: 3 },
];

export function TableOfContentsControlledExample() {
  const [active, setActive] = useState('introduction');

  return (
    <div className="flex min-h-100 items-start gap-8">
      <ul className="space-y-2 text-sm text-grayscale-opacity-700">
        {items
          .filter((item) => item.level !== 3)
          .map((item) => (
            <li key={item.id}>
              <button
                type="button"
                onClick={() => setActive(item.id)}
                className={
                  item.id === active ? 'text-primary-500' : undefined
                }
              >
                Go to {item.label}
              </button>
            </li>
          ))}
      </ul>
      <TableOfContents
        items={items}
        value={active}
        onValueChange={setActive}
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Always Open or Closed

`expanded` overrides hover and focus: `expanded` keeps the panel open, `expanded={false}` keeps it closed. Leave it unset for the default behavior.

## Props

`TableOfContents` renders a `<nav>` and accepts its props.

| Prop            | Type                    | Default               | Description                                                    |
| --------------- | ----------------------- | --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `items`         | `TableOfContentsItem[]` | -                     | Headings to list, in page order                                |
| `value`         | `string`                | -                     | Controlled active item id                                      |
| `defaultValue`  | `string`                | -                     | Initial active item id when uncontrolled                       |
| `onValueChange` | `(id: string) => void`  | -                     | Called when an item is clicked                                 |
| `side`          | `'left' \| 'right'`     | `'right'`             | Which side of the content the rail sits on                     |
| `expanded`      | `boolean`               | -                     | Forces the panel open or closed; unset follows hover and focus |
| `aria-label`    | `string`                | `'Table of contents'` | Name of the navigation landmark                                |

### TableOfContentsItem

| Field   | Type          | Default | Description                               |
| ------- | ------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `id`    | `string`      | -       | Unique id, and the default link target    |
| `label` | `string`      | -       | Text in the panel and the link name       |
| `level` | `1 \| 2 \| 3` | `1`     | Heading depth; sets tick width and indent |
| `href`  | `string`      | `#<id>` | Link target                               |

## Accessibility

The component is a `navigation` landmark named by `aria-label`. The rail links are the accessible surface: each is named by its item's label, and the active one has `aria-current="location"`. The expanded panel is visual only and hidden from assistive technology, so screen reader and keyboard users get one link per heading.

# Tabs

> Switch between related panels with underline or pill tab styles.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/components/tabs

## Preview

```tsx
import {
  Tabs,
  TabsContent,
  TabsList,
  TabsTrigger,
} from '@/components/ui/Tabs';
import { useState } from 'react';

const tabs = [
  { label: 'Overview', value: 'overview' },
  { label: 'Activity', value: 'activity' },
  { label: 'Members', value: 'members' },
  { label: 'Settings', value: 'settings' },
];

export function TabsExample() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState('overview');

  return (
    <Tabs
      value={value}
      onValueChange={setValue}
      className="w-full max-w-120"
    >
      <TabsList>
        {tabs.map((tab) => (
          <TabsTrigger key={tab.value} value={tab.value}>
            {tab.label}
          </TabsTrigger>
        ))}
      </TabsList>
      {tabs.map((tab) => (
        <TabsContent key={tab.value} value={tab.value}>
          {tab.label} content
        </TabsContent>
      ))}
    </Tabs>
  );
}
```

## Usage

The active underline renders per trigger and grows from width 0, so no
extra element is needed.

## Bordered

Use `bordered` on `TabsList` when the underline tabs need a rail border.

```tsx
import { Tabs, TabsList, TabsTrigger } from '@/components/ui/Tabs';
import { useState } from 'react';

const tabs = Array.from({ length: 6 }, (_, index) => ({
  label: `Tab ${index + 1}`,
  value: `tab-${index + 1}`,
}));

export function TabsBorderedExample() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState('tab-1');

  return (
    <Tabs
      value={value}
      onValueChange={setValue}
      className="w-full max-w-200"
    >
      <TabsList bordered>
        {tabs.map((tab) => (
          <TabsTrigger key={tab.value} value={tab.value}>
            {tab.label}
          </TabsTrigger>
        ))}
      </TabsList>
    </Tabs>
  );
}
```

## Sliding indicator

By default the active underline grows from width 0 under each tab. Render
`TabsIndicator` inside `TabsList` to opt into a single bar that slides between
tabs instead — adding it disables the per-tab grow highlight.

```tsx
import {
  Tabs,
  TabsIndicator,
  TabsList,
  TabsTrigger,
} from '@/components/ui/Tabs';
import { useState } from 'react';

const tabs = Array.from({ length: 6 }, (_, index) => ({
  label: `Tab ${index + 1}`,
  value: `tab-${index + 1}`,
}));

export function TabsSlidingIndicatorExample() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState('tab-1');

  return (
    <Tabs
      value={value}
      onValueChange={setValue}
      className="w-full max-w-200"
    >
      <TabsList bordered>
        {tabs.map((tab) => (
          <TabsTrigger key={tab.value} value={tab.value}>
            {tab.label}
          </TabsTrigger>
        ))}
        {/* Rendering TabsIndicator swaps the per-tab grow highlight for a
            single bar that slides between tabs. */}
        <TabsIndicator />
      </TabsList>
    </Tabs>
  );
}
```

## With Badges

Put a `Badge` after the label to show a count or a status dot.

```tsx
import { Badge } from '@/components/ui/Badge';
import { Tabs, TabsList, TabsTrigger } from '@/components/ui/Tabs';
import { useState } from 'react';

export function TabsWithBadgesExample() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState('all');

  return (
    <Tabs
      value={value}
      onValueChange={setValue}
      className="w-full max-w-140"
    >
      <TabsList bordered>
        <TabsTrigger value="all">All</TabsTrigger>
        <TabsTrigger value="messages">
          Messages
          <Badge size="md">4</Badge>
        </TabsTrigger>
        <TabsTrigger value="errors">
          Errors
          <Badge size="sm" variant="destructive" />
        </TabsTrigger>
        <TabsTrigger value="more">More</TabsTrigger>
      </TabsList>
    </Tabs>
  );
}
```

## Pill

```tsx
import { Badge } from '@/components/ui/Badge';
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import { Tabs, TabsList, TabsTrigger } from '@/components/ui/Tabs';
import { FlagIcon } from '@/components/icons/FlagIcon';
import { PlusIcon } from '@/components/icons/PlusIcon';
import { useState } from 'react';

export function TabsPillExample() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState('overview');

  return (
    <Tabs variant="pill" value={value} onValueChange={setValue}>
      <TabsList>
        <TabsTrigger value="overview">Overview</TabsTrigger>
        <TabsTrigger value="messages">
          Messages
          <Badge size="md">4</Badge>
        </TabsTrigger>
        <TabsTrigger value="files">Files</TabsTrigger>
        <TabsTrigger value="flagged">
          <FlagIcon className="size-4" data-icon="inline-start" />
          Flagged
        </TabsTrigger>
        <Button
          variant="text"
          theme="default"
          size="icon-md"
          aria-label="Add tab"
        >
          <PlusIcon data-icon="inline-start" />
        </Button>
      </TabsList>
    </Tabs>
  );
}
```

## Vertical

```tsx
import {
  Tabs,
  TabsContent,
  TabsList,
  TabsTrigger,
} from '@/components/ui/Tabs';
import { useState } from 'react';

const tabs = [
  { label: 'Overview', value: 'overview' },
  { label: 'Activity', value: 'activity' },
  { label: 'Members', value: 'members' },
  { label: 'Settings', value: 'settings' },
];

export function TabsVerticalBorderedExample() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState('overview');

  return (
    <Tabs
      value={value}
      onValueChange={setValue}
      orientation="vertical"
      className="min-h-90 w-full max-w-140"
    >
      <TabsList bordered>
        {tabs.map((tab) => (
          <TabsTrigger key={tab.value} value={tab.value}>
            {tab.label}
          </TabsTrigger>
        ))}
      </TabsList>
      {tabs.map((tab) => (
        <TabsContent key={tab.value} value={tab.value}>
          {tab.label} content
        </TabsContent>
      ))}
    </Tabs>
  );
}
```

## Props

| Part            | Prop          | Type                         | Default        | Description                                                     |
| --------------- | ------------- | ---------------------------- | -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Tabs`          | `variant`     | `'underline' \| 'pill'`      | `'underline'`  | Visual style for the tab triggers                               |
| `Tabs`          | `orientation` | `'horizontal' \| 'vertical'` | `'horizontal'` | Layout direction from Base UI Tabs                              |
| `TabsList`      | `bordered`    | `boolean`                    | `false`        | Adds the underline rail border                                  |
| `TabsTrigger`   | `value`       | `string`                     | —              | Value connected to a tab panel                                  |
| `TabsContent`   | `value`       | `string`                     | —              | Panel value connected to a tab trigger                          |
| `TabsIndicator` | —             | —                            | —              | Optional sliding underline; disables the per-tab grow highlight |

# Tag

> A label component for categorization, status, and filtering. Supports 12 colors, two variants, and optional remove action.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/components/tag

## Preview

```tsx
import { Tag } from '@/components/ui/Tag';

export function TagExample() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
      <Tag color="blue" colorVariant="tint">
        Design
      </Tag>
      <Tag color="green" colorVariant="tint">
        Development
      </Tag>
      <Tag color="gold" colorVariant="tint">
        Marketing
      </Tag>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Colors

All 12 colors in the `tint` variant (first row) and the default `solid` variant (second row):

```tsx
import { Tag } from '@/components/ui/Tag';

const colors = [
  'default',
  'teal',
  'olive',
  'brown',
  'rose',
  'indigo',
  'blue',
  'green',
  'gold',
  'red',
  'purple',
  'navy',
] as const;

export function TagColorsExample() {
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-3">
      {(['tint', 'solid'] as const).map((colorVariant) => (
        <div key={colorVariant} className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
          {colors.map((color) => (
            <Tag
              key={color}
              color={color}
              colorVariant={colorVariant}
            >
              {color}
            </Tag>
          ))}
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Clickable

With `onClick`, the tag label renders as a button with a hover overlay.

```tsx
import { Tag } from '@/components/ui/Tag';
import { FlagIcon } from '@/components/icons/FlagIcon';
import { useState } from 'react';

export function TagClickableExample() {
  const [lastClicked, setLastClicked] = useState<string>();

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2">
      <Tag onClick={() => setLastClicked('Design')}>Design</Tag>
      <Tag
        icon={<FlagIcon />}
        onClick={() => setLastClicked('Urgent')}
      >
        Urgent
      </Tag>
      {lastClicked && (
        <span className="text-sm text-grayscale-opacity-600">
          Clicked: {lastClicked}
        </span>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Removable

Tags can include a remove button via `removable` + `onRemove`:

```tsx
import { Tag } from '@/components/ui/Tag';
import { FlagIcon } from '@/components/icons/FlagIcon';
import { useState } from 'react';

export function TagRemovableExample() {
  const [tags, setTags] = useState(['Design', 'Urgent']);
  const remove = (tag: string) =>
    setTags((current) => current.filter((item) => item !== tag));

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
      {tags.map((tag) => (
        <Tag
          key={tag}
          removable
          icon={tag === 'Urgent' ? <FlagIcon /> : undefined}
          onRemove={() => remove(tag)}
        >
          {tag}
        </Tag>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Clickable and Removable

`onClick` and `onRemove` can be combined. Clicking the remove button does not trigger `onClick`.

```tsx
import { Tag } from '@/components/ui/Tag';
import { FlagIcon } from '@/components/icons/FlagIcon';
import { useState } from 'react';

export function TagClickableAndRemovableExample() {
  const [tags, setTags] = useState(['Design', 'Urgent']);
  const [lastClicked, setLastClicked] = useState<string>();
  const remove = (tag: string) =>
    setTags((current) => current.filter((item) => item !== tag));

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2">
      {tags.map((tag) => (
        <Tag
          key={tag}
          removable
          icon={tag === 'Urgent' ? <FlagIcon /> : undefined}
          onClick={() => setLastClicked(tag)}
          onRemove={() => remove(tag)}
        >
          {tag}
        </Tag>
      ))}
      {lastClicked && (
        <span className="text-sm text-grayscale-opacity-600">
          Clicked: {lastClicked}
        </span>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Selected

`selected` draws a focus-colored outline. With `onClick`, it also sets `aria-pressed`, so the tag works as a toggle.

```tsx
import { Tag } from '@/components/ui/Tag';
import { FlagIcon } from '@/components/icons/FlagIcon';
import { useState } from 'react';

const tags = [
  { label: 'Design', icon: undefined },
  { label: 'Urgent', icon: <FlagIcon /> },
];

export function TagSelectedExample() {
  const [selected, setSelected] = useState<string | undefined>(
    'Design',
  );

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
      {tags.map(({ label, icon }) => (
        <Tag
          key={label}
          icon={icon}
          selected={selected === label}
          onClick={() =>
            setSelected((current) =>
              current === label ? undefined : label,
            )
          }
        >
          {label}
        </Tag>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Props

| Prop           | Type                                                                                                                            | Default     | Description                                                        |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `children`     | `ReactNode`                                                                                                                     | —           | **Required.** Tag content                                          |
| `color`        | `'default' \| 'teal' \| 'olive' \| 'brown' \| 'rose' \| 'indigo' \| 'blue' \| 'green' \| 'gold' \| 'red' \| 'purple' \| 'navy'` | `'default'` | Tag color                                                          |
| `colorVariant` | `'solid' \| 'tint'`                                                                                                             | `'solid'`   | Color style variant                                                |
| `icon`         | `ReactNode`                                                                                                                     | —           | Icon rendered before the label                                     |
| `removable`    | `boolean`                                                                                                                       | `false`     | Shows a remove (×) button                                          |
| `selected`     | `boolean`                                                                                                                       | `false`     | Applies selected styling. With `onClick`, also sets `aria-pressed` |
| `onClick`      | `() => void`                                                                                                                    | —           | Click handler                                                      |
| `onRemove`     | `() => void`                                                                                                                    | —           | Called when the remove button is clicked                           |
| `className`    | `string`                                                                                                                        | —           | Additional CSS classes                                             |
| `style`        | `CSSProperties`                                                                                                                 | —           | Inline styles                                                      |

# Textarea

> Multi-line text input with consistent border, focus, and disabled states.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/components/textarea

## Preview

```tsx
import { Textarea } from '@/components/ui/Textarea';
import { useState } from 'react';

export function TextareaExample() {
  const [text, setText] = useState('');

  return (
    <Textarea
      aria-label="Feedback"
      className="w-112.5"
      placeholder="Tell us what you think..."
      value={text}
      onChange={(event) => setText(event.currentTarget.value)}
    />
  );
}
```

## Usage

`Textarea` renders a native `<textarea>`; read the value from `event.currentTarget.value` in `onChange`. Set `rows` for a taller default height.

## States

Use `disabled` to disable the textarea, `aria-invalid` to apply the destructive border treatment, and `readOnly` for text that can be selected but not edited.

```tsx
import { Textarea } from '@/components/ui/Textarea';

const states = [
  { label: 'Placeholder', props: {} },
  {
    label: 'Filled',
    props: { defaultValue: 'The new dashboard loads much faster.' },
  },
  { label: 'Disabled', props: { disabled: true } },
  { label: 'Invalid', props: { 'aria-invalid': true } },
  {
    label: 'Read-only',
    props: {
      defaultValue: 'The new dashboard loads much faster.',
      readOnly: true,
    },
  },
];

export function TextareaStatesExample() {
  return (
    <div className="grid w-fit grid-cols-[auto_18rem] items-start gap-x-6 gap-y-3 text-sm text-grayscale-opacity-700">
      {states.map(({ label, props }) => (
        <div key={label} className="contents">
          <span className="py-1.5">{label}</span>
          <Textarea
            aria-label={label}
            placeholder="Tell us what you think..."
            {...props}
          />
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Props

| Prop           | Type                                   | Default | Description                       |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------- | ------- | --------------------------------- |
| `disabled`     | `boolean`                              | `false` | Disables the textarea             |
| `aria-invalid` | `boolean`                              | —       | Applies destructive border styles |
| `className`    | `string`                               | —       | Additional CSS classes            |
| `...props`     | `ComponentPropsWithoutRef<'textarea'>` | —       | Native textarea props forwarded   |

# Time Picker

> Three-column time picker (hours, minutes, seconds) with click-to-select and CSS scroll-snap.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/components/time-picker

## Preview

```tsx
import { TimePicker } from '@/components/ui/TimePicker';
import { format } from 'date-fns';
import { useState } from 'react';

export function TimePickerExample() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState(new Date(2026, 0, 1, 9, 30));

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col items-center gap-4">
      <TimePicker value={value} onValueChange={setValue} />
      <code className="text-sm text-grayscale-opacity-600">
        {format(value, 'HH:mm:ss')}
      </code>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Usage

`TimePicker` accepts a `Date` and emits a `Date`. Only the hours, minutes, and seconds portion is mutated — the date portion of `value` is preserved.

## Hours and Minutes Only

```tsx
import { TimePicker } from '@/components/ui/TimePicker';
import { useState } from 'react';

export function TimePickerHoursMinutesOnlyExample() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState(new Date(2026, 0, 1, 14, 0));

  return (
    <TimePicker
      value={value}
      onValueChange={setValue}
      showSeconds={false}
    />
  );
}
```

Hidden seconds don't disappear from the underlying `Date` — they keep whatever was on `value` (or `0` if `value` was undefined). Toggle `showSeconds` freely without losing data.

## Custom Steps

```tsx
import { TimePicker } from '@/components/ui/TimePicker';
import { useState } from 'react';

export function TimePickerStepsExample() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState(new Date(2026, 0, 1, 9, 0));

  return (
    <TimePicker
      value={value}
      onValueChange={setValue}
      minuteStep={15}
      showSeconds={false}
    />
  );
}
```

Use `hourStep`, `minuteStep`, `secondStep` to render fewer rows per column. This example uses `minuteStep={15}`.

## Custom Height

```tsx
import { TimePicker } from '@/components/ui/TimePicker';
import { useState } from 'react';

export function TimePickerCustomHeightExample() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState(new Date(2026, 0, 1, 9, 30));

  return (
    <TimePicker
      value={value}
      onValueChange={setValue}
      className="h-60"
    />
  );
}
```

The default column height is 300px. Override it with `className`, here `h-60`.

## Time Picker (Popover + TimePicker)

There is no separate root component — compose `Popover`, `TimePicker`, and an input-style trigger:

```tsx
import {
  InputGroup,
  InputGroupAddon,
  InputGroupInput,
} from '@/components/ui/InputGroup';
import {
  Popover,
  PopoverContent,
  PopoverTrigger,
} from '@/components/ui/Popover';
import { TimePicker } from '@/components/ui/TimePicker';
import { ClockIcon } from '@/components/icons/ClockIcon';
import { format } from 'date-fns';
import { useState } from 'react';

export function TimePickerInsideTimePickerExample() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState<Date | undefined>();
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);

  return (
    <div className="w-96">
      <Popover open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
        <PopoverTrigger
          nativeButton={false}
          render={
            <InputGroup className="cursor-pointer">
              <InputGroupInput
                readOnly
                value={value ? format(value, 'HH:mm:ss') : ''}
                placeholder="Pick a time"
                className="cursor-pointer"
              />
              <InputGroupAddon align="inline-end">
                <ClockIcon className="text-grayscale-opacity-500" />
              </InputGroupAddon>
            </InputGroup>
          }
        />
        <PopoverContent className="p-0" sideOffset={8}>
          <TimePicker value={value} onValueChange={setValue} />
        </PopoverContent>
      </Popover>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Behavior

- **Click selects.** Clicking an item calls `onValueChange` and smooth-scrolls that item to the top of its column.
- **Scrolling does not select.** Drag or wheel scrolls the column freely; the selection only changes when the user explicitly clicks.
- **`scroll-snap-type: y proximity`.** When motion settles, the column snaps so an item sits flush at the top — no per-frame snap fighting during fast scroll.
- **Initial position.** On mount, the selected item is placed at the top instantly (no animation). Subsequent value changes animate.
- **Date portion preserved.** If `value` is provided, its year/month/day are preserved in the emitted `Date`. If `undefined`, the emit anchors to today.

## Pairing with Calendar

Because both `Calendar` and `TimePicker` work with `Date`, composing a date-time input is straightforward — pass the same `Date` through both:

```tsx
const [value, setValue] = useState<Date>();

<Calendar mode="single" selected={value} onSelect={setValue} />
<TimePicker value={value} onValueChange={setValue} />
```

`Calendar.onSelect` updates the year/month/day; `TimePicker.onValueChange` updates the hours/minutes/seconds. Both write back to the same `Date`.

## Props

| Prop            | Type                    | Default | Description                                                                                                 |
| --------------- | ----------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `value`         | `Date`                  | —       | Current time. Only the hours/minutes/seconds portion is rendered; date portion is preserved on emit.        |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: Date) => void` | —       | Called with a new `Date` carrying the chosen time. Date portion is preserved from `value`, or set to today. |
| `showSeconds`   | `boolean`               | `true`  | When `false`, hides the seconds column.                                                                     |
| `hourStep`      | `number`                | `1`     | Step between hour values (e.g. `2` → `0, 2, 4, …, 22`).                                                     |
| `minuteStep`    | `number`                | `1`     | Step between minute values.                                                                                 |
| `secondStep`    | `number`                | `1`     | Step between second values.                                                                                 |
| `disabled`      | `boolean`               | `false` | Disables all interaction.                                                                                   |
| `className`     | `string`                | —       | Additional classes on root. Use to override height (e.g. `h-60`).                                           |

# Toast

> Status-coloured notifications dispatched imperatively from anywhere in the app.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/components/toast

## Preview

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import {
  ToastProvider,
  type ToastStatus,
  type ToasterToastData,
  createToastManager,
} from '@/components/ui/Toast';

// In an app, mount one `ToastProvider` at the root and call the exported
// `toastManager`. Each example here has its own manager so its toasts stay
// in its own viewport.
const toast = createToastManager<ToasterToastData>();

const toasts: { type: ToastStatus; title: string }[] = [
  { type: 'success', title: 'Changes saved' },
  { type: 'warning', title: 'Storage almost full' },
  { type: 'error', title: 'Upload failed' },
  { type: 'info', title: 'New version available' },
];

export function ToastSolidBottomRightExample() {
  return (
    <ToastProvider toastManager={toast}>
      <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
        {toasts.map(({ type, title }) => (
          <Button
            key={type}
            theme="primary"
            onClick={() => toast.add({ type, title })}
          >
            {type}
          </Button>
        ))}
      </div>
    </ToastProvider>
  );
}
```

## Usage

`Toast` is built on Base UI's
[Toast](https://base-ui.com/react/components/toast). The package
exports a module-level singleton `toastManager` and a `ToastProvider`
that auto-mounts the viewport — drop `<ToastProvider>` once at the app
root and call `toastManager.add(...)` from anywhere (event handlers,
fetch interceptors, zustand actions, …). No hook required at the call
site.

Each example on this page creates its own manager so its toasts stay in
its own viewport. In an app, use the exported `toastManager` as below.

```tsx
// app root
import {
  toastManager,
  ToastProvider,
} from '@/components/ui/Toast';

function App() {
  return (
    <ToastProvider>
      <Page />
    </ToastProvider>
  );
}

// anywhere
import { toastManager } from '@/components/ui/Toast';

function SaveButton() {
  return (
    <Button
      onClick={() =>
        toastManager.add({ type: 'success', title: '已成功儲存' })
      }
    >
      Save
    </Button>
  );
}
```

## Status

`type` accepts `success`, `warning`, `error`, `info`, or `loading`.
The toast applies the matching colour but does not pick an icon —
icons are opt-in via `data.icon`. The `loading` status swaps the
close X for a cancel button when `data.cancelProps` is supplied.

## Position

`ToastProvider` accepts a `position` prop with six anchors:
`top-left`, `top-center`, `top-right`, `bottom-left`, `bottom-center`,
`bottom-right`. One provider serves one position — toasts dispatched
through its manager render at that anchor.

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import {
  type ToastPosition,
  ToastProvider,
  type ToasterToastData,
  createToastManager,
} from '@/components/ui/Toast';
import { useState } from 'react';

const positions: ToastPosition[] = [
  'top-left',
  'top-center',
  'top-right',
  'bottom-left',
  'bottom-center',
  'bottom-right',
];

// One provider serves one position, so each position gets its own manager.
function PositionScene({ position }: { position: ToastPosition }) {
  const [toast] = useState(() =>
    createToastManager<ToasterToastData>(),
  );

  return (
    <ToastProvider toastManager={toast} position={position}>
      <div className="flex min-h-35 flex-col gap-3 rounded border border-grayscale-opacity-200 bg-background p-4">
        <p className="font-sans text-xs text-grayscale-opacity-600">
          position: {position}
        </p>
        <Button
          onClick={() =>
            toast.add({ type: 'info', title: `Shown at ${position}` })
          }
        >
          {position}
        </Button>
      </div>
    </ToastProvider>
  );
}

export function ToastPositionsExample() {
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full grid-cols-1 gap-3 p-4 md:grid-cols-3">
      {positions.map((position) => (
        <PositionScene key={position} position={position} />
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Multiple positions (two channels)

To send some toasts to one corner and others to a different corner,
create a second manager with `createToastManager` and nest a second
`ToastProvider` for it. Each provider/manager pair is a separate
channel — pick whichever you want at the call site.

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import {
  ToastProvider,
  type ToasterToastData,
  createToastManager,
} from '@/components/ui/Toast';
import { XmarkIcon } from '@/components/icons/XmarkIcon';

// In an app, the outer provider would use the exported `toastManager`.
const toast = createToastManager<ToasterToastData>();
const errorToast = createToastManager<ToasterToastData>();

export function ToastTwoChannelsExample() {
  return (
    <ToastProvider toastManager={toast} position="bottom-right">
      <ToastProvider
        toastManager={errorToast}
        position="top-center"
        variant="subtle"
      >
        <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
          <Button
            onClick={() =>
              toast.add({ type: 'success', title: 'Saved to draft' })
            }
          >
            Bottom-right success
          </Button>
          <Button
            onClick={() =>
              errorToast.add({
                type: 'error',
                title: 'Connection lost',
                data: { icon: <XmarkIcon className="size-5" /> },
              })
            }
          >
            Top-center error
          </Button>
        </div>
      </ToastProvider>
    </ToastProvider>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// toast-managers.ts
import {
  type ToasterToastData,
  createToastManager,
} from '@/components/ui/Toast';

export const errorToast = createToastManager<ToasterToastData>();
```

```tsx
// app root
import { ToastProvider, toastManager } from '@/components/ui/Toast';
import { errorToast } from './toast-managers';

<ToastProvider position="bottom-right">
  <ToastProvider
    toastManager={errorToast}
    position="top-center"
    variant="subtle"
  >
    {children}
  </ToastProvider>
</ToastProvider>;
```

```tsx
// anywhere
import { toastManager } from '@/components/ui/Toast';
import { errorToast } from './toast-managers';

toastManager.add({ type: 'success', title: 'Saved' });
errorToast.add({ type: 'error', title: 'Connection lost' });
```

## Variants

The `solid` variant (default) fills the toast with the status colour
on a white-on-coloured layout. The `subtle` variant flips to a white
surface with a tinted icon — matches the "notification" pattern in the
design system.

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import {
  ToastProvider,
  type ToastStatus,
  type ToasterToastData,
  createToastManager,
} from '@/components/ui/Toast';
import { CheckIcon } from '@/components/icons/CheckIcon';
import { FlagIcon } from '@/components/icons/FlagIcon';
import { XmarkIcon } from '@/components/icons/XmarkIcon';
import type { ReactNode } from 'react';

const toast = createToastManager<ToasterToastData>();

const toasts: {
  type: ToastStatus;
  title: string;
  icon: ReactNode;
}[] = [
  {
    type: 'success',
    title: 'Changes saved',
    icon: <CheckIcon className="size-5" />,
  },
  {
    type: 'warning',
    title: 'Storage almost full',
    icon: <FlagIcon className="size-5" />,
  },
  {
    type: 'error',
    title: 'Upload failed',
    icon: <XmarkIcon className="size-5" />,
  },
  {
    type: 'info',
    title: 'New version available',
    icon: <FlagIcon className="size-5" />,
  },
];

export function ToastSubtleTopRightExample() {
  return (
    <ToastProvider
      toastManager={toast}
      position="top-right"
      variant="subtle"
    >
      <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
        {toasts.map(({ type, title, icon }) => (
          <Button
            key={type}
            theme="primary"
            onClick={() => toast.add({ type, title, data: { icon } })}
          >
            {type}
          </Button>
        ))}
      </div>
    </ToastProvider>
  );
}
```

## Loading

For long-running operations, dispatch a toast with `type: 'loading'`
and `timeout: 0`. Give it a `data.cancelProps` button, which replaces
the close X, so the user can cancel the operation, then `update` the
toast on completion.

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import { Spinner } from '@/components/ui/Spinner';
import {
  ToastProvider,
  type ToasterToastData,
  createToastManager,
} from '@/components/ui/Toast';
import { CheckIcon } from '@/components/icons/CheckIcon';

const toast = createToastManager<ToasterToastData>();

export function ToastLoadingExample() {
  return (
    <ToastProvider
      toastManager={toast}
      position="top-right"
      variant="subtle"
    >
      <Button
        onClick={() => {
          // Stands in for a real upload that finishes after 2.5 seconds.
          const upload = setTimeout(() => {
            toast.update('upload', {
              type: 'success',
              title: 'Upload complete',
              timeout: 4000,
              data: { icon: <CheckIcon className="size-5" /> },
            });
          }, 2500);
          toast.add({
            id: 'upload',
            type: 'loading',
            title: 'Uploading…',
            timeout: 0,
            data: {
              icon: <Spinner className="size-5" />,
              cancelProps: {
                children: 'Cancel',
                onClick: () => clearTimeout(upload),
              },
            },
          });
        }}
      >
        Loading toast
      </Button>
    </ToastProvider>
  );
}
```

## With Icon

Pass any icon node through `data.icon`; the renderer drops it into
the icon slot before the title.

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import {
  ToastProvider,
  type ToasterToastData,
  createToastManager,
} from '@/components/ui/Toast';
import { FlagIcon } from '@/components/icons/FlagIcon';

const toast = createToastManager<ToasterToastData>();

export function ToastWithIconExample() {
  return (
    <ToastProvider toastManager={toast}>
      <Button
        onClick={() =>
          toast.add({
            type: 'warning',
            title: 'Maintenance starts at 22:00',
            data: { icon: <FlagIcon className="size-5" /> },
          })
        }
      >
        Toast with icon
      </Button>
    </ToastProvider>
  );
}
```

## With Description

Add a second line of context with `description`.

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import {
  ToastProvider,
  type ToasterToastData,
  createToastManager,
} from '@/components/ui/Toast';

const toast = createToastManager<ToasterToastData>();

export function ToastWithDescriptionExample() {
  return (
    <ToastProvider toastManager={toast}>
      <Button
        onClick={() =>
          toast.add({
            type: 'success',
            title: 'Changes saved',
            description: 'All changes were applied to the project.',
          })
        }
      >
        Toast with description
      </Button>
    </ToastProvider>
  );
}
```

## With Action

`actionProps` is forwarded to the action button. Use it for an "Undo"
or other recovery affordance.

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import {
  ToastProvider,
  type ToasterToastData,
  createToastManager,
} from '@/components/ui/Toast';

const toast = createToastManager<ToasterToastData>();

export function ToastWithActionExample() {
  return (
    <ToastProvider toastManager={toast}>
      <Button
        onClick={() =>
          toast.add({
            type: 'info',
            title: 'Item archived',
            actionProps: {
              children: 'Undo',
              onClick: () =>
                toast.add({
                  type: 'success',
                  title: 'Item restored',
                }),
            },
          })
        }
      >
        Toast with action
      </Button>
    </ToastProvider>
  );
}
```

## Promise

`promise` swaps a single toast through loading, success, and error
states based on a promise.

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import {
  ToastProvider,
  type ToasterToastData,
  createToastManager,
} from '@/components/ui/Toast';

const toast = createToastManager<ToasterToastData>();

// Stands in for a request that resolves after 1.5 seconds.
function saveDraft() {
  return new Promise<string>((resolve) =>
    setTimeout(() => resolve('Draft saved'), 1500),
  );
}

export function ToastPromiseFlowExample() {
  return (
    <ToastProvider toastManager={toast}>
      <Button
        onClick={() => {
          void toast.promise(saveDraft(), {
            loading: { type: 'info', title: 'Saving…' },
            success: (result) => ({ type: 'success', title: result }),
            error: {
              type: 'error',
              title: 'Failed, try again later',
            },
          });
        }}
      >
        Promise toast
      </Button>
    </ToastProvider>
  );
}
```

## Stacking

Toasts in one viewport stack. Hover or focus the stack to expand it.
When more than `limit` toasts (default `3`) are open, the oldest one is
removed.

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import {
  ToastProvider,
  type ToasterToastData,
  createToastManager,
} from '@/components/ui/Toast';

const toast = createToastManager<ToasterToastData>();

export function ToastStackedExample() {
  return (
    <ToastProvider toastManager={toast}>
      <Button
        onClick={() => {
          toast.add({ type: 'success', title: 'File uploaded' });
          toast.add({
            type: 'warning',
            title: 'Storage almost full',
          });
          toast.add({ type: 'error', title: 'Sync failed' });
        }}
      >
        Stack three toasts
      </Button>
    </ToastProvider>
  );
}
```

## Anchored toasts

For tooltip-style feedback anchored to a specific element (e.g.,
"Copied!" near a button), use `anchoredToastManager` and wrap with
`AnchoredToastProvider`. Pass `positionerProps.anchor` per call.

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import {
  AnchoredToastProvider,
  type ToasterToastData,
  createToastManager,
} from '@/components/ui/Toast';
import { useRef, useState } from 'react';

// In an app, use the exported `anchoredToastManager`.
const toast = createToastManager<ToasterToastData>();

export function ToastAnchoredExample() {
  const ref = useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null);
  const [count, setCount] = useState(0);

  return (
    <AnchoredToastProvider toastManager={toast} variant="subtle">
      <Button
        ref={ref}
        theme="primary"
        onClick={() => {
          const next = count + 1;
          setCount(next);
          toast.add({
            type: 'success',
            title: `Copied! (${next})`,
            positionerProps: {
              anchor: ref.current,
              side: 'top',
              sideOffset: 8,
            },
          });
        }}
      >
        Copy
      </Button>
    </AnchoredToastProvider>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// app root
import {
  AnchoredToastProvider,
  ToastProvider,
} from '@/components/ui/Toast';

<ToastProvider>
  <AnchoredToastProvider variant="subtle">
    {children}
  </AnchoredToastProvider>
</ToastProvider>;
```

```tsx
// anywhere
import { anchoredToastManager } from '@/components/ui/Toast';

function CopyButton() {
  const ref = useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null);
  return (
    <Button
      ref={ref}
      onClick={() => {
        navigator.clipboard.writeText(value);
        anchoredToastManager.add({
          type: 'success',
          title: 'Copied!',
          positionerProps: {
            anchor: ref.current,
            side: 'top',
            sideOffset: 8,
          },
        });
      }}
    >
      Copy
    </Button>
  );
}
```

## Props

### ToastProvider

| Prop           | Type                                                                                              | Default          | Description                                                                                           |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `position`     | `'top-left' \| 'top-center' \| 'top-right' \| 'bottom-left' \| 'bottom-center' \| 'bottom-right'` | `'bottom-right'` | Anchor for the toast viewport                                                                         |
| `variant`      | `'solid' \| 'subtle'`                                                                             | `'solid'`        | Solid status-coloured surface or subtle white bg                                                      |
| `closable`     | `boolean`                                                                                         | `true`           | Render the close X button                                                                             |
| `className`    | `string`                                                                                          | —                | Additional classes for the viewport                                                                   |
| `toastManager` | `ToastManager`                                                                                    | `toastManager`   | Override the default singleton — pass a custom manager from `createToastManager` for a second channel |
| `timeout`      | `number`                                                                                          | `5000`           | Default auto-dismiss in ms (`0` keeps it open)                                                        |
| `limit`        | `number`                                                                                          | `3`              | Max toasts shown at once                                                                              |

### AnchoredToastProvider

Same as `ToastProvider` but without `position` — anchored toasts
position themselves against `positionerProps.anchor` on each call.
Defaults to the `anchoredToastManager` singleton.

### Manager methods

`toastManager`, `anchoredToastManager`, and any manager from
`createToastManager()` expose the same imperative API.

| Method    | Signature                                                  | Description                                                 |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `add`     | `(options) => string`                                      | Adds a toast and returns its id                             |
| `update`  | `(id, options) => void`                                    | Updates an existing toast (or upserts by id via `add`)      |
| `close`   | `(id?) => void`                                            | Closes a toast (or all toasts when no id)                   |
| `promise` | `(promise, { loading, success, error }) => Promise<Value>` | Threads loading/success/error states through a single toast |

### Add options

| Option             | Type                                                       | Description                                                                    |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `id`               | `string`                                                   | Stable id — calling `add` again with the same id updates in place              |
| `type`             | `'success' \| 'warning' \| 'error' \| 'info' \| 'loading'` | Status colour                                                                  |
| `title`            | `ReactNode`                                                | Main message                                                                   |
| `description`      | `ReactNode`                                                | Secondary text shown after the title                                           |
| `timeout`          | `number`                                                   | Override provider timeout (`0` keeps it open)                                  |
| `priority`         | `'low' \| 'high'`                                          | ARIA live region politeness                                                    |
| `actionProps`      | `ButtonHTMLAttributes`                                     | Props for the action button                                                    |
| `positionerProps`  | `{ anchor, side, ... }`                                    | For anchored toasts — element to anchor against (passed to `Toast.Positioner`) |
| `data.icon`        | `ReactNode`                                                | Icon rendered before the title                                                 |
| `data.cancelProps` | `ButtonHTMLAttributes`                                     | Cancel button — replaces the close X when set or on loading toasts             |
| `onClose`          | `() => void`                                               | Called when the toast closes                                                   |

### createToastManager

```tsx
import {
  type ToasterToastData,
  createToastManager,
} from '@/components/ui/Toast';

const errorToast = createToastManager<ToasterToastData>();
```

Pass the returned manager to a `ToastProvider`'s `toastManager` prop
to create a separate channel with its own state, position, and variant.

### Exports

| Export                                                                                                                                                                | Description                                                                             |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `toastManager`                                                                                                                                                        | Default module-level singleton manager — wired to `ToastProvider`                       |
| `anchoredToastManager`                                                                                                                                                | Singleton for anchored/tooltip-style toasts — wired to `AnchoredToastProvider`          |
| `createToastManager`                                                                                                                                                  | Factory for additional manager channels                                                 |
| `ToastProvider`                                                                                                                                                       | Mounts a viewport at a position and pre-wires `toastManager` (override via prop)        |
| `AnchoredToastProvider`                                                                                                                                               | Same idea for anchored toasts                                                           |
| `useToast`                                                                                                                                                            | Hook reading the manager from context — for advanced custom rendering inside primitives |
| `Toast`, `ToastViewport`, `ToastPortal`, `ToastPositioner`, `ToastContent`, `ToastTitle`, `ToastDescription`, `ToastIcon`, `ToastAction`, `ToastClose`, `ToastCancel` | Lower-level parts for custom rendering                                                  |

# Toolbar

> Flex layout primitive with role="toolbar". Lays out actions, separators, and spacers above tables, editors, or panels.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/components/toolbar

## Preview

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import {
  Toolbar,
  ToolbarGroup,
  ToolbarSpacer,
} from '@/components/ui/Toolbar';

export function ToolbarExample() {
  return (
    <Toolbar>
      <ToolbarGroup>
        <Button size="md" theme="default" variant="text">
          File
        </Button>
        <Button size="md" theme="default" variant="text">
          Edit
        </Button>
      </ToolbarGroup>
      <ToolbarSpacer />
      <ToolbarGroup>
        <Button size="md" theme="primary" variant="text">
          Save
        </Button>
      </ToolbarGroup>
    </Toolbar>
  );
}
```

## Usage

Put related actions in a `ToolbarGroup`. `ToolbarSpacer` pushes the groups after
it to the trailing edge.

## With Separator

Use `ToolbarSeparator` between groups of related actions.

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import {
  Toolbar,
  ToolbarGroup,
  ToolbarSeparator,
} from '@/components/ui/Toolbar';

export function ToolbarWithSeparatorExample() {
  return (
    <Toolbar variant="outline">
      <ToolbarGroup>
        <Button size="md" theme="default" variant="text">
          Cut
        </Button>
        <Button size="md" theme="default" variant="text">
          Copy
        </Button>
        <Button size="md" theme="default" variant="text">
          Paste
        </Button>
      </ToolbarGroup>
      <ToolbarSeparator />
      <ToolbarGroup>
        <Button size="md" theme="default" variant="text">
          Undo
        </Button>
        <Button size="md" theme="default" variant="text">
          Redo
        </Button>
      </ToolbarGroup>
    </Toolbar>
  );
}
```

## Variants

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import {
  Toolbar,
  ToolbarGroup,
  ToolbarSpacer,
} from '@/components/ui/Toolbar';

const variants = ['default', 'bar', 'outline'] as const;

export function ToolbarVariantsExample() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-4">
      {variants.map((variant) => (
        <div key={variant} className="flex flex-col gap-1">
          <span className="font-sans text-xs text-grayscale-opacity-600">
            variant=&quot;{variant}&quot;
          </span>
          <Toolbar variant={variant}>
            <ToolbarGroup>
              <Button size="md" theme="default" variant="text">
                File
              </Button>
              <Button size="md" theme="default" variant="text">
                Edit
              </Button>
            </ToolbarGroup>
            <ToolbarSpacer />
            <ToolbarGroup>
              <Button size="md" theme="primary" variant="text">
                Save
              </Button>
            </ToolbarGroup>
          </Toolbar>
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

| Variant   | Use                                                         |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `default` | Transparent background. Drop into existing surfaces.        |
| `bar`     | Subtle gray-50 background. Standalone toolbar above panels. |
| `outline` | White background with bottom border. Sits above tables.     |

## Sizes

| Size      | Padding     | Use                                    |
| --------- | ----------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `default` | `px-4 py-3` | Top-of-page toolbars.                  |
| `sm`      | `px-3 py-2` | Compact toolbars above data tables.    |
| `none`    | `p-0`       | When wrapping content with own layout. |

## Parts

| Part               | Notes                                                         |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Toolbar`          | `role="toolbar"`, `aria-orientation="horizontal"` by default. |
| `ToolbarGroup`     | `role="group"`, flex with gap for clustered actions.          |
| `ToolbarSeparator` | Vertical separator (uses `Separator` primitive).              |
| `ToolbarSpacer`    | `flex-1` to push subsequent items to the trailing edge.       |

# Tooltip

> A short, transient hint anchored to a trigger element with arrow and side controls.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/components/tooltip

## Preview

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import {
  Tooltip,
  TooltipContent,
  TooltipProvider,
  TooltipTrigger,
} from '@/components/ui/Tooltip';

export function TooltipExample() {
  return (
    <TooltipProvider>
      <Tooltip>
        <TooltipTrigger render={<Button>Hover me</Button>} />
        <TooltipContent>Tooltip text</TooltipContent>
      </Tooltip>
    </TooltipProvider>
  );
}
```

## Usage

`Tooltip` is built on Base UI's
[Tooltip](https://base-ui.com/react/components/tooltip).
Wrap a region of triggers in `TooltipProvider` to share open and close
delays, then compose `Tooltip`, `TooltipTrigger`, and `TooltipContent`.
The default offset matches the design (8 px from the anchor).

## With Icon

The content is a flex row, so add an icon next to the message to mark
warnings or status hints.

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import {
  Tooltip,
  TooltipContent,
  TooltipProvider,
  TooltipTrigger,
} from '@/components/ui/Tooltip';
import { FlagIcon } from '@/components/icons/FlagIcon';

export function TooltipWithIconExample() {
  return (
    <TooltipProvider>
      <Tooltip>
        <TooltipTrigger render={<Button>Help</Button>} />
        <TooltipContent>
          <FlagIcon className="size-5 shrink-0 text-warning-500" />
          <span>Save your changes before leaving this page</span>
        </TooltipContent>
      </Tooltip>
    </TooltipProvider>
  );
}
```

## Side

`side` selects which edge of the trigger the tooltip anchors to. Base UI
will flip the side automatically to avoid clipping.

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import {
  Tooltip,
  TooltipContent,
  TooltipProvider,
  TooltipTrigger,
} from '@/components/ui/Tooltip';

const sides = ['top', 'right', 'bottom', 'left'] as const;

export function TooltipSidePlacementExample() {
  return (
    <TooltipProvider>
      <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3">
        {sides.map((side) => (
          <Tooltip key={side}>
            <TooltipTrigger
              render={<Button size="md">{side}</Button>}
            />
            <TooltipContent side={side}>
              Shown on the {side}
            </TooltipContent>
          </Tooltip>
        ))}
      </div>
    </TooltipProvider>
  );
}
```

## Align

`align` shifts the tooltip along the chosen side.

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import {
  Tooltip,
  TooltipContent,
  TooltipProvider,
  TooltipTrigger,
} from '@/components/ui/Tooltip';

const aligns = ['start', 'center', 'end'] as const;

export function TooltipAlignmentsExample() {
  return (
    <TooltipProvider>
      <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3">
        {aligns.map((align) => (
          <Tooltip key={align}>
            <TooltipTrigger
              render={<Button size="md">{align}</Button>}
            />
            <TooltipContent align={align}>
              align: {align}
            </TooltipContent>
          </Tooltip>
        ))}
      </div>
    </TooltipProvider>
  );
}
```

## Long Content

The popup wraps at the configured `400px` max width.

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import {
  Tooltip,
  TooltipContent,
  TooltipProvider,
  TooltipTrigger,
} from '@/components/ui/Tooltip';

export function TooltipLongContentExample() {
  return (
    <TooltipProvider>
      <Tooltip>
        <TooltipTrigger render={<Button>Long content</Button>} />
        <TooltipContent>
          Tooltip text is capped at 400px wide. Longer content wraps
          onto new lines instead of stretching across the screen.
        </TooltipContent>
      </Tooltip>
    </TooltipProvider>
  );
}
```

## Without Arrow

Pass `arrow={false}` to drop the pointer when the tooltip is anchored to
custom layouts that don't need a beak.

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import {
  Tooltip,
  TooltipContent,
  TooltipProvider,
  TooltipTrigger,
} from '@/components/ui/Tooltip';

export function TooltipWithoutArrowExample() {
  return (
    <TooltipProvider>
      <Tooltip>
        <TooltipTrigger render={<Button>No arrow</Button>} />
        <TooltipContent arrow={false}>Tooltip text</TooltipContent>
      </Tooltip>
    </TooltipProvider>
  );
}
```

## Props

### Tooltip

`Tooltip` is the root and accepts every Base UI
[`Tooltip.Root`](https://base-ui.com/react/components/tooltip#api-reference-tooltiproot)
prop.

| Prop                    | Type                             | Default  | Description                             |
| ----------------------- | -------------------------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `defaultOpen`           | `boolean`                        | `false`  | Whether the tooltip is initially open   |
| `open`                  | `boolean`                        | —        | Controlled open state                   |
| `onOpenChange`          | `(open, eventDetails) => void`   | —        | Called when the open state changes      |
| `disabled`              | `boolean`                        | `false`  | Disables the tooltip                    |
| `disableHoverablePopup` | `boolean`                        | `false`  | Whether the popup itself can be hovered |
| `trackCursorAxis`       | `'none' \| 'x' \| 'y' \| 'both'` | `'none'` | Track the cursor along the given axis   |

### TooltipProvider

| Prop         | Type     | Default | Description                                          |
| ------------ | -------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `delay`      | `number` | `200`   | Open delay in ms                                     |
| `closeDelay` | `number` | `100`   | Close delay in ms                                    |
| `timeout`    | `number` | `400`   | Window during which adjacent tooltips open instantly |

### TooltipContent

`TooltipContent` portals its children, positions them with Base UI, and
adds the styled popup with an optional arrow.

| Prop                    | Type                                                                       | Default                       | Description                                           |
| ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `side`                  | `'top' \| 'right' \| 'bottom' \| 'left' \| 'inline-start' \| 'inline-end'` | `'top'`                       | Side relative to the trigger                          |
| `sideOffset`            | `number`                                                                   | `8`                           | Distance from the trigger in px                       |
| `align`                 | `'start' \| 'center' \| 'end'`                                             | `'center'`                    | Alignment along the side                              |
| `alignOffset`           | `number`                                                                   | `0`                           | Offset along the alignment axis                       |
| `arrow`                 | `boolean`                                                                  | `true`                        | Whether to render the arrow                           |
| `positionerClassName`   | `string`                                                                   | —                             | Classes for the inner positioner element              |
| `anchor`                | `RefObject \| Element \| …`                                                | —                             | Custom positioning anchor (defaults to the trigger)   |
| `arrowPadding`          | `number`                                                                   | `5`                           | Minimum space between the arrow and the popup's edges |
| `collisionAvoidance`    | `{ side?, align?, fallbackAxisSide? }`                                     | `{ fallbackAxisSide: 'end' }` | How the popup flips or shifts to avoid collisions     |
| `collisionBoundary`     | `'clipping-ancestors' \| Element \| Element[] \| Rect`                     | `'clipping-ancestors'`        | Area the popup is kept inside                         |
| `collisionPadding`      | `number \| { top?, right?, bottom?, left? }`                               | `5`                           | Space kept from the edge of the collision boundary    |
| `disableAnchorTracking` | `boolean`                                                                  | `false`                       | Stop following layout shifts of the anchor            |
| `positionMethod`        | `'absolute' \| 'fixed'`                                                    | `'absolute'`                  | CSS `position` of the positioner                      |
| `sticky`                | `boolean`                                                                  | `false`                       | Keep the popup in view after the anchor scrolls out   |
| `portalContainer`       | `HTMLElement \| ShadowRoot \| RefObject \| null`                           | —                             | Custom portal container (defaults to `document.body`) |
| `keepMounted`           | `boolean`                                                                  | `false`                       | Keep the popup in the DOM while closed                |

### Tooltip Parts

| Part                | Description                                                         |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `TooltipProvider`   | Shares delays for grouped tooltips                                  |
| `Tooltip`           | Root that controls a single tooltip's open state                    |
| `TooltipTrigger`    | Element that opens the tooltip on hover or focus                    |
| `TooltipContent`    | Portal + positioner + popup with the styled body and optional arrow |
| `TooltipPortal`     | Lower-level portal exposed for advanced composition                 |
| `TooltipPositioner` | Lower-level positioner exposed for advanced composition             |
| `TooltipArrow`      | Standalone arrow element when composing the content manually        |

# Flat

> Base cloud sidebar. Frosted glass skin, flat nav with no submenus, no account footer.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/blocks/sidebar/cloud/flat

## Preview

```tsx
import { CloudSidebar } from '@/blocks/sidebar-cloud-01/app-sidebar';
import {
  SidebarInset,
  SidebarProvider,
  SidebarTrigger,
} from '@/components/ui/Sidebar';
import { Skeleton } from '@/components/ui/Skeleton';
import { type CSSProperties } from 'react';

// Keeps the fixed sidebar inside this demo box. In an app, drop the frame:
// the sidebar is fixed to the viewport.
const DEMO_FRAME =
  'relative h-160 w-full overflow-hidden ' +
  '[&_[data-slot=sidebar-container]]:!absolute ' +
  '[&_[data-slot=sidebar-container]]:!h-full';

const providerStyle = {
  '--sidebar-width': '180px',
  '--sidebar-width-icon': '56px',
} as CSSProperties;

export function SidebarCloud01Example() {
  return (
    <div className={DEMO_FRAME}>
      <SidebarProvider
        defaultOpen
        enableKeyboardShortcut={false}
        className="h-full min-h-0"
        style={providerStyle}
      >
        <CloudSidebar collapsible="icon" />
        <SidebarInset>
          <header className="flex h-12 shrink-0 items-center gap-2 border-b border-sidebar-border px-3 md:hidden">
            <SidebarTrigger />
          </header>
          <div className="flex flex-col gap-4 p-6">
            <Skeleton className="h-4 w-1/3" />
            <Skeleton className="h-4 w-1/2" />
            <Skeleton className="h-36 w-full rounded-lg" />
          </div>
        </SidebarInset>
      </SidebarProvider>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @vital-design/sidebar-cloud-01
```

Installs **`app-sidebar.tsx`** and `src/public/images/cloud.jpg` (imported by the component). It depends on `@vital-design/sidebar` and the icons used in the sample tree. Compose `SidebarProvider` and `SidebarInset` in the app.

> **Assets:** The frost photo is imported and shipped. Sample logos use public paths (`/images/vital-logo-text-h.svg`, `/images/vital-logo.svg`) that only the docs examples provide; they are not installed by the registry.

## When to use

- **Base Cloud sidebar** — frosted glass over a cloud photo; start here, then see [Inline Submenus](/docs/blocks/sidebar/cloud/inline-submenus) and [Dropdown Submenus](/docs/blocks/sidebar/cloud/dropdown-submenus) for nested nav
- **No submenus** — flat nav only (Projects is a single item, not a parent)
- No account / user footer — only the bullet collapse control stays docked
- Use `variant="sidebar"` or `floating`. Skip `inset` — the frost photo does not fit inset padding and unrounded corners.

## Floating

Pass `variant="floating"` for a rounded panel with a gap around it.

```tsx
import { CloudSidebar } from '@/blocks/sidebar-cloud-01/app-sidebar';
import {
  SidebarInset,
  SidebarProvider,
  SidebarTrigger,
} from '@/components/ui/Sidebar';
import { Skeleton } from '@/components/ui/Skeleton';
import { type CSSProperties } from 'react';

// Keeps the fixed sidebar inside this demo box. In an app, drop the frame:
// the sidebar is fixed to the viewport.
const DEMO_FRAME =
  'relative h-160 w-full overflow-hidden ' +
  '[&_[data-slot=sidebar-container]]:!absolute ' +
  '[&_[data-slot=sidebar-container]]:!h-full';

const providerStyle = {
  '--sidebar-width': '180px',
  '--sidebar-width-icon': '56px',
} as CSSProperties;

export function SidebarCloud01FloatingExample() {
  return (
    <div className={DEMO_FRAME}>
      <SidebarProvider
        defaultOpen
        enableKeyboardShortcut={false}
        className="h-full min-h-0"
        style={providerStyle}
      >
        <CloudSidebar variant="floating" collapsible="icon" />
        <SidebarInset>
          <header className="flex h-12 shrink-0 items-center gap-2 border-b border-sidebar-border px-3 md:hidden">
            <SidebarTrigger />
          </header>
          <div className="flex flex-col gap-4 p-6">
            <Skeleton className="h-4 w-1/3" />
            <Skeleton className="h-4 w-1/2" />
            <Skeleton className="h-36 w-full rounded-lg" />
          </div>
        </SidebarInset>
      </SidebarProvider>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Composition

`CloudSidebar` is a skinned `Sidebar` (`ComponentProps<typeof Sidebar>`). Sample header, nav, and empty footer dock are composed **inside** that file, so `<CloudSidebar />` matches this preview.

```tsx
import { CloudSidebar } from '@/blocks/sidebar-cloud-01/app-sidebar';
import {
  SidebarInset,
  SidebarProvider,
  SidebarTrigger,
} from '@/components/ui/Sidebar';

export function Layout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <SidebarProvider
      defaultOpen
      style={
        {
          '--sidebar-width': '180px',
          '--sidebar-width-icon': '56px',
        } as React.CSSProperties
      }
    >
      <CloudSidebar collapsible="icon" />
      <SidebarInset className="bg-background">
        <header className="flex h-12 items-center gap-2 border-b px-3 md:hidden">
          <SidebarTrigger />
        </header>
        {children}
      </SidebarInset>
    </SidebarProvider>
  );
}
```

- Recommended widths on the provider: **`--sidebar-width: 180px`**, **`--sidebar-width-icon: 56px`**
- **Mobile:** the desktop bullet is hidden. Place a `SidebarTrigger` in `SidebarInset` (`md:hidden` header)
- After install, edit the `data` / `workspaces` objects. Replace the preview-only `/images/…` paths or provide matching public files in your app.

For a blank shell without the product skin, compose [Sidebar](/docs/components/sidebar) yourself.

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @vital-design/sidebar-cloud-02
```

Installs **`app-sidebar.tsx`** and `src/public/images/cloud.jpg` (imported by the component). It depends on `@vital-design/sidebar` plus avatar, dropdown-menu, and the icons used in the sample tree. Compose `SidebarProvider` and `SidebarInset` in the app.

> **Assets:** The frost photo is imported and shipped. Sample logos / avatar use public paths (`/images/vital-logo-text-h.svg`, `/images/vital-logo.svg`, `/images/ray.jpg`) that only the docs examples provide; they are not installed by the registry.

## When to use

- **A sidebar with submenus** — nested items render as inline `SidebarMenuSub`
- Product panel with **frosted glass** (`white/80` + `blur(12px)`) over a **cloud photo**
- Menu hover/active as **text-only primary** (no fill), with **100ms ease-in** transitions
- **Active edge rail** (4×20px, primary) on the current item (mirrors for `side="right"`)
- Built-in **bullet collapse** control (30×30, grayscale-600) docked to the footer
- Sample account footer (avatar + dropdown) lives in the same file — edit after install
- Use `variant="sidebar"` or `floating`. Skip `inset` — the frost photo does not fit inset padding and unrounded corners.
