
Installs **`app-sidebar.tsx`** and `src/public/images/cloud.jpg` (imported by the component). It depends on `@vital-design/sidebar`, `@vital-design/collapsible`, plus avatar, dropdown-menu, and the icons used in the sample tree. Compose `SidebarProvider` and `SidebarInset` in the app.

> **Assets:** The frost photo is imported and shipped. Sample logos / avatar use public paths (`/images/vital-logo-text-h.svg`, `/images/vital-logo.svg`, `/images/ray.jpg`) that only the docs examples provide; they are not installed by the registry.

## When to use

- Same shell as [Inline Submenus](/docs/blocks/sidebar/cloud/inline-submenus), but parents with children **fold** via `Collapsible` (`defaultOpen`)
- Chevron on the parent rotates when the panel is open; hidden in icon-collapsed mode
- Product panel with **frosted glass** over a **cloud photo**, account footer, bullet collapse
- Use `variant="sidebar"` or `floating`. Skip `inset` — the frost photo does not fit inset padding and unrounded corners.

## Floating

Pass `variant="floating"` for a rounded panel with a gap around it.

```tsx
import { CloudSidebar } from '@/blocks/sidebar-cloud-06/app-sidebar';
import {
  SidebarInset,
  SidebarProvider,
  SidebarTrigger,
} from '@/components/ui/Sidebar';
import { Skeleton } from '@/components/ui/Skeleton';
import { type CSSProperties } from 'react';

// Keeps the fixed sidebar inside this demo box. In an app, drop the frame:
// the sidebar is fixed to the viewport.
const DEMO_FRAME =
  'relative h-160 w-full overflow-hidden ' +
  '[&_[data-slot=sidebar-container]]:!absolute ' +
  '[&_[data-slot=sidebar-container]]:!h-full';

const providerStyle = {
  '--sidebar-width': '180px',
  '--sidebar-width-icon': '56px',
} as CSSProperties;

export function SidebarCloud06FloatingExample() {
  return (
    <div className={DEMO_FRAME}>
      <SidebarProvider
        defaultOpen
        enableKeyboardShortcut={false}
        className="h-full min-h-0"
        style={providerStyle}
      >
        <CloudSidebar variant="floating" collapsible="icon" />
        <SidebarInset>
          <header className="flex h-12 shrink-0 items-center gap-2 border-b border-sidebar-border px-3 md:hidden">
            <SidebarTrigger />
          </header>
          <div className="flex flex-col gap-4 p-6">
            <Skeleton className="h-4 w-1/3" />
            <Skeleton className="h-4 w-1/2" />
            <Skeleton className="h-36 w-full rounded-lg" />
          </div>
        </SidebarInset>
      </SidebarProvider>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Composition

`CloudSidebar` is a skinned `Sidebar` (`ComponentProps<typeof Sidebar>`). Sample header, nav, and footer are composed **inside** that file, so `<CloudSidebar />` matches this preview.

```tsx
import { CloudSidebar } from '@/blocks/sidebar-cloud-06/app-sidebar';
import {
  SidebarInset,
  SidebarProvider,
  SidebarTrigger,
} from '@/components/ui/Sidebar';

export function Layout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <SidebarProvider
      defaultOpen
      style={
        {
          '--sidebar-width': '180px',
          '--sidebar-width-icon': '56px',
        } as React.CSSProperties
      }
    >
      <CloudSidebar collapsible="icon" />
      <SidebarInset className="bg-background">
        <header className="flex h-12 items-center gap-2 border-b px-3 md:hidden">
          <SidebarTrigger />
        </header>
        {children}
      </SidebarInset>
    </SidebarProvider>
  );
}
```

- Recommended widths on the provider: **`--sidebar-width: 180px`**, **`--sidebar-width-icon: 56px`**
- **Mobile:** the desktop bullet is hidden. Place a `SidebarTrigger` in `SidebarInset` (`md:hidden` header)
- After install, edit the `data` object (labels, logos, avatar). Replace the preview-only `/images/…` paths or provide matching public files in your app.

For a blank shell without the product skin, compose [Sidebar](/docs/components/sidebar) yourself.

# Data Table

> Generic data table with grouping, add rows per group, search, sorting, column resizing and reordering, row selection, and inline and popover cell editing.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/blocks/data-table

## Preview

```tsx
import { ReviewTaskTable } from '@/blocks/data-table/review-task-table';

export function DataTableExample() {
  return <ReviewTaskTable />;
}
```

The table ships with a review-task example. Click a cell to edit it: 任務 and 備註 edit inline, while 狀態, 協作者, 期限, and 標籤 open a popover. Hover a header to sort, and drag a header edge to resize. Check rows to bring up the selection bar. Use **分群** to group rows and **顯示欄位** to hide or reorder columns.

### One level of grouping

Every group gets its own header and its own 新增任務 row, which starts the new row with that group's values.

```tsx
import { ReviewTaskTable } from '@/blocks/data-table/review-task-table';

export function DataTableOneLevelExample() {
  return <ReviewTaskTable grouping={['project']} />;
}
```

### Two levels of grouping

The outer group can select every row inside it. A project with no tasks still shows, through `groupingConfig.empty`.

```tsx
import { ReviewTaskTable } from '@/blocks/data-table/review-task-table';

export function DataTableTwoLevelsExample() {
  return <ReviewTaskTable grouping={['project', 'status']} />;
}
```

## Use your own rows

The block is meant to be copied and changed. `data-table.tsx` is generic; the review-task example lives in `columns.tsx`, `data.ts`, and `review-task-table.tsx`. Replace those three with your own.

1. Define your row type. It needs a string `id`.

   ```ts
   export type Member = { id: string; name: string; team: string };
   ```

2. Write the data columns. The table adds the checkbox and actions columns itself. It reads three `meta` fields:

   | Field        | Effect                                                   |
   | ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------- |
   | `label`      | Name in 顯示欄位 and for screen readers. Defaults to the id. |
   | `editable`   | Cells get the editable hover.                            |
   | `searchable` | The search box matches this column's value.              |

   `enableHiding: false` keeps a column on in 顯示欄位. Cells save edits with `table.options.meta.updateRow(row.id, patch)`.

   ```tsx
   export const memberColumns: ColumnDef<Member>[] = [
     {
       id: 'name',
       accessorFn: (row) => row.name,
       header: ({ column }) => (
         <DataTableColumnHeader column={column} title="姓名" />
       ),
       meta: { label: '姓名', searchable: true },
       enableHiding: false,
       cell: ({ row }) => row.original.name,
     },
   ];
   ```

3. Render the table. Keys in `groupingConfig` are the fields the 分群 menu offers. Leave out `createRow` to hide the 新增 rows.

   ```tsx
   <DataTable
     data={members}
     columns={memberColumns}
     groupingConfig={{ team: { label: '團隊' } }}
     itemName="成員"
     rowLabel={(member) => member.name}
     createRow={(values) => ({
       name: '',
       team: '',
       ...values,
       id: crypto.randomUUID(),
     })}
   />
   ```

## Composition

This block is built on the following Vittal Design primitives:

- `Avatar`, `Button`, `Calendar`, `Card`, `Checkbox`, `DropdownMenu`, `Editable`, `Popover`, `SearchBar`, `Select`, `Switch`, `Table`, `Tag`, `Toolbar`
- `CaretDownSolidIcon`, `CaretUpSolidIcon`, `CheckSolidIcon`, `AngleDownIcon`, `XmarkIcon`, `EllipsisIcon`, `PlusIcon`
- [`@tanstack/react-table`](https://tanstack.com/table/v8) for table state

## Files

| File                           | Description                                                     |
| ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `data-table.tsx`               | Generic table: state, grouping layout, pinning, selection       |
| `review-task-table.tsx`        | Example entry — wires the table to the review-task columns      |
| `columns.tsx`                  | Example columns, with text, status, people, date, and tag cells |
| `data.ts`                      | Example rows, people, tags, and grouping config                 |
| `group-tree.ts`                | Builds the group tree from rows and grouping keys               |
| `action-bar.tsx`               | Search, 分群 menu, 顯示欄位 card, and the row menu                    |
| `add-row.tsx`                  | 新增 row at the end of the table or a group                       |
| `data-table-column-header.tsx` | Sortable header with hover arrows                               |
| `group-row.tsx`                | Group header row and nesting rails                              |
| `pinning.ts`                   | Pinned column offsets and display order                         |
| `popover-edit.tsx`             | Popover cell plus people, tags, and date editors                |
| `resize-handle.tsx`            | Column resize handle with a full-height guide                   |
| `select-column.tsx`            | Checkbox and actions columns, and group selection               |
| `selection-bar.tsx`            | Floating bar for the checked rows                               |

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @vital-design/data-table
```

This installs the block under `src/blocks/data-table/` and pulls every required primitive automatically.

# Table Pagination

> Single-row table footer with page controls, a page jump, and rows per page.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/blocks/table-pagination

## Preview

```tsx
import { TablePagination } from '@/blocks/table-pagination/table-pagination';
import {
  Table,
  TableBody,
  TableCell,
  TableHead,
  TableHeader,
  TableRow,
} from '@/components/ui/Table';
import { useState } from 'react';

const STATUSES = ['Active', 'Done', 'Pending'] as const;
const OWNERS = ['Alex Chen', 'Riley Park', 'Jordan Lee'] as const;
const ROWS = Array.from({ length: 91 }, (_, index) => ({
  id: index + 1,
  name: `Item ${index + 1}`,
  status: STATUSES[index % STATUSES.length],
  owner: OWNERS[index % OWNERS.length],
}));

export function TablePaginationExample() {
  const [page, setPage] = useState(1);
  const [pageSize, setPageSize] = useState(10);
  const visibleRows = ROWS.slice(
    (page - 1) * pageSize,
    page * pageSize,
  );

  return (
    <div className="w-full overflow-hidden rounded-md border border-grayscale-opacity-200">
      <Table>
        <TableHeader>
          <TableRow>
            <TableHead className="w-20">No.</TableHead>
            <TableHead>Name</TableHead>
            <TableHead>Status</TableHead>
            <TableHead>Owner</TableHead>
          </TableRow>
        </TableHeader>
        <TableBody>
          {visibleRows.map((row) => (
            <TableRow key={row.id}>
              <TableCell>{row.id}</TableCell>
              <TableCell>{row.name}</TableCell>
              <TableCell>{row.status}</TableCell>
              <TableCell>{row.owner}</TableCell>
            </TableRow>
          ))}
        </TableBody>
      </Table>
      <TablePagination
        className="rounded-none"
        page={page}
        pageSize={pageSize}
        total={ROWS.length}
        onPageChange={setPage}
        onPageSizeChange={(nextPageSize) => {
          setPageSize(nextPageSize);
          setPage(1);
        }}
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## When to use

Use this block for the Vital table footer: page controls, a jump field, a page-size select, and the current range, in one row. When the row is too narrow, the jump field and the page-size select hide. The page controls and the range stay visible.

[Pagination](/docs/components/pagination) stays the primitive. Build a different footer from those parts when this row does not fit.

## Usage

Own `page`, `pageSize`, and `total` in the screen. Reset the page when the page size changes.

```tsx
import { TablePagination } from '@/blocks/table-pagination/table-pagination';
import { useState } from 'react';

export function OrdersFooter() {
  const [page, setPage] = useState(1);
  const [pageSize, setPageSize] = useState(10);

  return (
    <TablePagination
      page={page}
      pageSize={pageSize}
      total={91}
      onPageChange={setPage}
      onPageSizeChange={(nextPageSize) => {
        setPageSize(nextPageSize);
        setPage(1);
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

`pagination`, `jump`, and `summary` replace those regions. The block does not render the table. Place it under [Table](/docs/components/table).

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @vital-design/table-pagination
```

This installs `src/blocks/table-pagination/table-pagination.tsx` and its Pagination, Input, and Select dependencies.

# Tree Select

> Searchable hierarchical path picker built from Command and Popover.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/blocks/tree-select

## Preview

```tsx
import {
  TreeSelect,
  type TreeSelectItem,
  type TreeSelectValue,
} from '@/blocks/tree-select/tree-select';
import { useState } from 'react';

const locationItems: TreeSelectItem[] = [
  {
    label: 'Taiwan',
    parentValue: null,
    value: 'tw',
    hasChildren: true,
  },
  {
    label: 'Japan',
    parentValue: null,
    value: 'jp',
    hasChildren: true,
  },
  { label: 'Taipei', parentValue: 'tw', value: 'tpe' },
  { label: 'Kaohsiung', parentValue: 'tw', value: 'khh' },
  { label: 'Tokyo', parentValue: 'jp', value: 'tky' },
  { label: 'Osaka', parentValue: 'jp', value: 'osa' },
];

export function TreeSelectExample() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState<TreeSelectValue | null>(null);

  return (
    <TreeSelect
      items={locationItems}
      label="Locations"
      value={value}
      onValueChange={setValue}
      placeholder="Select location"
      searchPlaceholder="Search locations"
      emptyMessage="No locations found."
    />
  );
}
```

## Composition

This block is built on the following Vittal Design primitives:

- [`Command`](/docs/components/command), [`Popover`](/docs/components/popover)
- `AngleDownIcon`, `AngleRightIcon`

## Usage

Pass a flat list where each item names its parent, and mark items that open another level with `hasChildren`. Selecting a leaf returns its value and the path from the top level.

```tsx
import {
  TreeSelect,
  type TreeSelectValue,
} from '@/blocks/tree-select/tree-select';
import { useState } from 'react';

const items = [
  {
    label: 'Taiwan',
    parentValue: null,
    value: 'tw',
    hasChildren: true,
  },
  { label: 'Taipei', parentValue: 'tw', value: 'tpe' },
];

export function LocationField() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState<TreeSelectValue | null>(null);

  return (
    <TreeSelect
      items={items}
      label="Locations"
      value={value}
      onValueChange={setValue}
    />
  );
}
```

The block turns off cmdk's filter (`shouldFilter={false}`) and filters the level on screen itself, so search never matches items in other levels. Backspace in an empty search returns to the parent level, and closing the popup returns to the top level.

The block does not load data. To load children on demand, edit `openPage` and the item list in the installed file.

## Props

| Prop                | Type                               | Default               | Description                                 |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------- | --------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `items`             | `TreeSelectItem[]`                 | —                     | Flat list of every level                    |
| `label`             | `string`                           | —                     | Accessible name of the trigger and the list |
| `value`             | `TreeSelectValue \| null`          | —                     | Selected leaf and its path                  |
| `onValueChange`     | `(value: TreeSelectValue) => void` | —                     | Called when a leaf is selected              |
| `placeholder`       | `string`                           | `'Select'`            | Trigger text when nothing is selected       |
| `searchPlaceholder` | `string`                           | `'Search'`            | Search input placeholder                    |
| `emptyMessage`      | `string`                           | `'No results found.'` | Shown when a level has no matches           |
| `className`         | `string`                           | —                     | Classes on the trigger                      |

## Files

| File              | Description                                   |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `tree-select.tsx` | Block entry — trigger, page stack, and search |

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @vital-design/tree-select
```

This installs `src/blocks/tree-select/tree-select.tsx` and its Command, Popover, and icon dependencies.

# Colors

> Vittal Design color system — primitive palettes, semantic aliases, and named component tokens.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/design-tokens/colors

## Overview

Vittal Design follows the [shadcn/ui](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/theming)
naming convention for its semantic layer. Colors are defined under
`tokens/` (Style Dictionary), built into `src-v2/styles/tokens/generated.css`
as CSS custom properties on `:root`, with dark overrides on `.dark`,
and exposed to Tailwind via `@theme inline` (`--color-*`).

```ts
// 3 layers, generated from tokens/*.json by Style Dictionary
primitive  →  semantic  →  component
```

- **Primitive scales** (`--primary-50…900`, `--grayscale-100…900`,
  `--grayscale-opacity-100…900`, `--success-100…900`, etc.) — internal
  foundation. Reach for these when you need a specific shade for
  charts, illustrations, or fine-grained tinting. Tailwind utility:
  `bg-primary-500`, `text-grayscale-700`, etc.
- **Semantic tokens** (`--background`, `--primary`, `--card`,
  `--destructive`, …) — the public API. These describe **intent**
  and pair with `-foreground` siblings for legible content on the
  surface. Tailwind utility: `bg-primary text-primary-foreground`.
- **Component tokens** (`--avatar-*-fg`, `--tag-*-solid`) — closed
  palettes used by specific components.

## Dark mode

Add `class="dark"` to an ancestor, usually `<html>`. With
[next-themes](https://github.com/pacocoursey/next-themes), set
`attribute="class"`. The theme does not follow
`prefers-color-scheme`. Reinstall `@vital-design/vital-theme` so
`cssVars.dark` is written into the app stylesheet.

Every color swatch on this page shows two values: **L** is the light
value and **D** is the dark value. Each chip is drawn on its own
mode's page color, so translucent values look the way they render.

### What changes under `.dark`

- **Primitive scales** take their dark values from
  `tokens/dark/colors.json`. A scale class such as
  `text-grayscale-opacity-800` or `bg-primary-500` switches on its own.
- **Semantic tokens that alias a scale** are rebuilt from the dark
  scale: `primary` → `primary.500`, `foreground` →
  `grayscale-opacity.900`, `border` → `grayscale-opacity.200`.
- **A few semantic tokens set their own dark value** in
  `tokens/dark/colors.json`: `background`, `card`, and `popover`
  (`#232327`), and `input` (`#444447`).
- **These keep their light value:** literal `*-foreground` whites,
  the avatar and tag palettes below, and the shadow and
  gradient tokens on [Effects](/docs/design-tokens/effects).

The `.dark` ancestor paints `background` and `foreground`, so text
that sits on the page uses the dark ink. It also sets
`color-scheme: dark`, so native controls, scrollbars, and browser focus
outlines render dark.

### Writing components for both modes

- Paper uses `bg-background`, not `bg-white`.
- When a fill turns light in dark mode, such as `bg-grayscale-700` or
  `bg-grayscale-opacity-700`, put `text-background` on it so the text
  turns dark with it. Tag, Tooltip, and solid Toast do this.
- Child elements that fade the parent's text color use
  `text-current/90`, not `text-white/90`.
- `bg-white` and `text-white` stay white. Use them for marks that must
  stay white, such as switch, slider, and radio thumbs, and for text on
  saturated fills that keep one value in both modes.
- When a step lacks contrast in one mode, pick another step with the
  `dark:` variant. The data table selection bar uses
  `text-info-400 dark:text-info-200`.
- Don't hardcode colors with arbitrary values such as
  `bg-[#f8f8f9]`. Use the nearest scale step.

## Grayscale (Opacity)

The opacity variant uses `rgba(35, 35, 50, α)` so it tonally adapts
over any background. Use it for hover tints, dividers, disabled fields,
and other states where translucency is desired. `--grayscale-opacity-900`
is the only solid hex.

| `--grayscale-opacity-600` | `text-grayscale-opacity-600` | `rgba(35, 35, 50, 0.55)` | `rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.55)` |
| `--grayscale-opacity-500` | `text-grayscale-opacity-500` | `rgba(35, 35, 50, 0.40)` | `rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.40)` |
| `--grayscale-opacity-400` | `text-grayscale-opacity-400` | `rgba(35, 35, 50, 0.25)` | `rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.25)` |
| `--grayscale-opacity-300` | `text-grayscale-opacity-300` | `rgba(35, 35, 50, 0.15)` | `rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.15)` |
| `--grayscale-opacity-200` | `text-grayscale-opacity-200` | `rgba(35, 35, 50, 0.08)` | `rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.08)` |

## Semantic Tokens

Intent-based aliases that point to primitive colors. Each surface
ships with a paired `-foreground` token — use them together so text
remains legible regardless of theme overrides.

```tsx
<button className="bg-primary text-primary-foreground">Save</button>
<div className="bg-card text-card-foreground border border-border">…</div>
```

### Surfaces

Page chrome, cards, popovers, and muted/accent regions. `background`
is the page; `card` and `popover` are elevated containers; `muted`
and `accent` are subtle background tints (e.g. table stripes, hover
states).

| Name                   | Utility                   | Light                    | Dark                        |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------- | ------------------------ | --------------------------- |
| `--background`         | `bg-background`           | `#FFFFFF`                | `#232327`                   |
| `--foreground`         | `text-foreground`         | `#232332`                | `#FFFFFF`                   |
| `--card`               | `bg-card`                 | `#FFFFFF`                | `#232327`                   |
| `--card-foreground`    | `text-card-foreground`    | `#232332`                | `#FFFFFF`                   |
| `--popover`            | `bg-popover`              | `#FFFFFF`                | `#232327`                   |
| `--popover-foreground` | `text-popover-foreground` | `#232332`                | `#FFFFFF`                   |
| `--muted`              | `bg-muted`                | `rgba(35, 35, 50, 0.03)` | `rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.03)` |
| `--muted-foreground`   | `text-muted-foreground`   | `rgba(35, 35, 50, 0.70)` | `rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.70)` |
| `--accent`             | `bg-accent`               | `rgba(35, 35, 50, 0.08)` | `rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.08)` |
| `--accent-foreground`  | `text-accent-foreground`  | `#232332`                | `#FFFFFF`                   |

### Form

Borders, input strokes, and focus rings. `border` is the 0.08 hairline
for dividers and single edges, and it is also the default color of a bare
`border` class. `border-overlap` is solid, for edges that stack or cross,
such as avatar outlines in a group or tree rails, where a translucent line
would darken. `input` strokes form fields; `ring` paints focus outlines.

| Name               | Utility                 | Light                    | Dark                        |
| ------------------ | ----------------------- | ------------------------ | --------------------------- |
| `--border`         | `border-border`         | `rgba(35, 35, 50, 0.08)` | `rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.08)` |
| `--border-overlap` | `border-border-overlap` | `#DEDEE2`                | `#444447`                   |
| `--input`          | `border-input`          | `#DEDEE2`                | `#444447`                   |
| `--ring`           | `ring-ring`             | `#0E86FE`                | `#33CFFF`                   |

### Charts

Five-step palette for data visualization. Defaults rotate through
`primary → success → warning → info → destructive` so chart series
inherit brand color regardless of theme overrides.

| Name        | Utility      | Light     | Dark      |
| ----------- | ------------ | --------- | --------- |
| `--chart-1` | `bg-chart-1` | `#0E86FE` | `#33CFFF` |
| `--chart-2` | `bg-chart-2` | `#2BCD86` | `#2BCD86` |
| `--chart-3` | `bg-chart-3` | `#FFA700` | `#FFA700` |
| `--chart-4` | `bg-chart-4` | `#00C3FF` | `#00C3FF` |
| `--chart-5` | `bg-chart-5` | `#EB5000` | `#EB5000` |

### Sidebar

Application sidebar shell slots (shadcn-compatible). Used by the
[Sidebar](/docs/components/sidebar) primitive utilities such as
`bg-sidebar`, `text-sidebar-foreground`, and `border-sidebar-border`.
Product blocks may override individual slots (for example
`[--sidebar:transparent]` on the cloud shell).

| `--sidebar-foreground`         | `grayscale.900`         |

| `--sidebar-accent-foreground`  | `primary.700`           |
| `--sidebar-border`             | `grayscale-opacity.200` |
| `--sidebar-ring`               | `primary.300`           |

| ------------------------------ | --------------------------------- | ------------------------ | --------------------------- |

| `--sidebar-foreground`         | `text-sidebar-foreground`         | `#232327`                | `#FFFFFF`                   |

Tokens unique to Vittal Design with no shadcn equivalent. Kept

Each named avatar color exposes three tokens — `fg` (text /

These tokens have light values only, so avatars keep the same colors

# Typography

> Font family, type scale, weights, and text style conventions used across Vittal Design.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/design-tokens/typography

## Font Family

Vittal Design ships a single sans-serif stack via the `--font-sans`
CSS variable, registered as the Tailwind `font-sans` token.

```css
--font-sans:
  Roboto,
  'Noto Sans TC',
  'PingFang TC',
  'Microsoft JhengHei',
  sans-serif;
```

The stack prioritises:

1. **Roboto** — Latin / UI text
2. **Noto Sans TC** / **PingFang TC** / **Microsoft JhengHei** —
   Traditional Chinese fallbacks

```html
<p class="font-sans">Vittal Design 元件庫</p>
```

Vittal Design 元件庫 — Roboto, 你好, 1234567890

## Type Scale

Vittal Design relies on Tailwind's default type scale — there are no
project-specific font-size tokens. Reach for these utilities for
content typography.

### Heading 1 — `text-4xl`

Build elegant interfaces faster.

```html
<h1 class="text-4xl font-semibold tracking-tight">…</h1>
```

### Heading 2 — `text-3xl`

Composable, accessible primitives.

```html
<h2 class="text-3xl font-semibold tracking-tight">…</h2>
```

### Heading 3 — `text-2xl`

Section heading

```html
<h3 class="text-2xl font-semibold">…</h3>
```

### Heading 4 — `text-xl`

Subsection heading

```html
<h4 class="text-xl font-semibold">…</h4>
```

### Lead — `text-lg`

A larger paragraph used to introduce a section or summarize the
page.

```html
<p class="text-lg text-grayscale-opacity-700">…</p>
```

### Paragraph — `text-base`

The default body size. Use this for paragraph copy in
long-form content.

```html
<p class="text-base text-grayscale-opacity-800">…</p>
```

### Small — `text-sm`

Form labels, table cells, button text, and other UI copy default
to this size.

```html
<p class="text-sm text-grayscale-opacity-700">…</p>
```

### Caption — `text-xs`

Helper text, captions, metadata, and small labels.

```html
<p class="text-xs text-grayscale-opacity-600">…</p>
```

> See the [Tailwind type scale docs](https://tailwindcss.com/docs/font-size)
> for the full range (`text-xs` through `text-9xl`).

## Weights

font-normal
The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.

font-medium
The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.

font-semibold
The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.

font-bold
The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.

```html
<p class="font-normal">Body text</p>
<p class="font-medium">Form labels and emphasised UI text</p>
<p class="font-semibold">Headings and high-weight UI text</p>
<p class="font-bold">Reserved for marketing and display text</p>
```

## Text Color

Vittal Design's grayscale palette uses progressive transparency, so
the same text token reads consistently on light and tinted
backgrounds. Use the semantic `--text-*` tokens for intent, or pick
a grayscale step directly when you need exact contrast control.

| Usage            | Semantic                      | Grayscale step               |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| Primary content  | `text-(--foreground)`         | `text-grayscale-opacity-900` |
| Body / paragraph | —                             | `text-grayscale-opacity-800` |
| Secondary text   | `text-(--muted-foreground)`   | `text-grayscale-opacity-700` |
| Muted text       | `text-(--text-tertiary)`      | `text-grayscale-opacity-600` |
| Placeholder      | `text-(--text-disabled)`      | `text-grayscale-opacity-400` |
| On accent bg     | `text-(--primary-foreground)` | —                            |

Primary — grayscale-opacity-900
Body — grayscale-opacity-800
Secondary — grayscale-opacity-700
Muted — grayscale-opacity-600
Placeholder — grayscale-opacity-400

## Inline Elements

### Code

Use

var(--primary-500)

inside CSS or the matching Tailwind utility in markup.

### Link

Read the

tailwind setup guide

before scaffolding a new app.

# Border Radius

> Corner radius tokens shared by inputs, buttons, cards, and dialogs.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/design-tokens/radius

## Tokens

Vittal Design exposes six radius steps via CSS custom properties.
They are mapped to Tailwind's `rounded-*` utilities, so you can use
either form.

| Name            | Value    | Utility        |
| --------------- | -------- | -------------- |
| `--radius-none` | `0px`    | `rounded-none` |
| `--radius-sm`   | `4px`    | `rounded-sm`   |
| `--radius-md`   | `8px`    | `rounded-md`   |
| `--radius-lg`   | `15px`   | `rounded-lg`   |
| `--radius-xl`   | `16px`   | `rounded-xl`   |
| `--radius-full` | `9999px` | `rounded-full` |

## Usage Guidance

| Token           | Recommended usage                                             |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--radius-none` | Square corners — utility surfaces, inline edge-to-edge groups |
| `--radius-sm`   | Small inputs, compact buttons, tags                           |
| `--radius-md`   | Default form controls, table cells, cards                     |
| `--radius-lg`   | Medium buttons, alert containers                              |
| `--radius-xl`   | Cards, dialogs, large buttons                                 |
| `--radius-full` | Pill / circular shapes — chips, avatars, status dots          |

```css
/* CSS */
.card {
  border-radius: var(--radius-md);
}
```

```html
<!-- Tailwind utility -->
<div class="rounded-md">…</div>
```

## Combining With Sizes

Pair radius tokens with size utilities to get consistent component
shapes. Vittal's button, input, and chip components all key off the
same scale internally.

rounded-sm

rounded-md

rounded-lg

rounded-xl

rounded-full

# Effects

> Elevation shadows, focus rings, button shadows, and gradient tokens.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/design-tokens/effects

These tokens have light values only. They don't change under `.dark`,
so shadows are hard to see on dark surfaces. See
[Colors → Dark mode](/docs/design-tokens/colors#dark-mode).

## Elevation

Four elevation shadows for layering content. `accent` is the
softest; `top-level` is reserved for modal-class surfaces.

| Name                 | Utility            |
| -------------------- | ------------------ |
| `--shadow-accent`    | `shadow-accent`    |
| `--shadow-base`      | `shadow-base`      |
| `--shadow-emphasis`  | `shadow-emphasis`  |
| `--shadow-top-level` | `shadow-top-level` |

```css
.card {
  box-shadow: var(--shadow-base);
}
```

```html
<div class="shadow-base">…</div>
```

## Focus Rings

Outer rings rendered as `box-shadow` so they don't shift layout.
Match the colour to the control's intent:

- `--shadow-focus-*` — solid 2px ring tinted with the matching `200`
  step
- `--shadow-focus-ring-*` — softer translucent ring used for
  inline-edited controls (inputs, search bars)

| Name                              |
| --------------------------------- |
| `--shadow-focus-primary`          |
| `--shadow-focus-success`          |
| `--shadow-focus-info`             |
| `--shadow-focus-warning`          |
| `--shadow-focus-destructive`      |
| `--shadow-focus-ring-primary`     |
| `--shadow-focus-ring-destructive` |

```css
input:focus-visible {
  box-shadow: var(--shadow-focus-ring-primary);
}
```

## Button Shadows

Pre-baked drop shadows that match the five button themes. The
`-active` variants are the pressed-state counterparts.

| Name                                 |
| ------------------------------------ |
| `--shadow-button-primary`            |
| `--shadow-button-primary-active`     |
| `--shadow-button-success`            |
| `--shadow-button-success-active`     |
| `--shadow-button-info`               |
| `--shadow-button-info-active`        |
| `--shadow-button-warning`            |
| `--shadow-button-warning-active`     |
| `--shadow-button-destructive`        |
| `--shadow-button-destructive-active` |

```css
.button-primary {
  box-shadow: var(--shadow-button-primary);
}
.button-primary:active {
  box-shadow: var(--shadow-button-primary-active);
}
```

## Gradients

A single gradient family used for primary buttons and accent
surfaces.

| Name                        |
| --------------------------- |
| `--gradient-primary`        |
| `--gradient-primary-button` |

```css
.cta {
  background-image: var(--gradient-primary);
}
```

`--gradient-primary-button` is an alias of `--gradient-primary`
provided for forward compatibility — both currently resolve to the
same `linear-gradient(45deg, #33CFFF 0%, #0E86FE 100%)`.

# Registry

> Install Vittal Design components individually using the shadcn CLI.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/registry

## Overview

Vittal Design publishes a **shadcn-compatible registry** that lets you install individual components directly into your project. Each component is copied into your codebase, giving you full ownership and the ability to customize freely.

The registry is the canonical delivery channel for net-new `src-v2/` components. Existing projects can keep using the published `@fed/vital-design` npm package for compatibility, but newer components and theme assets are expected to come from the registry path.

Registry URL: `https://vittal.design/r`

## Installation

### 1. Initialize `shadcn` if needed

```bash
npx shadcn@latest init
```

### 2. Add the Vittal Design registry to `components.json`

```json
{
  "registries": {
    "@vital-design": "https://vittal.design/r/{name}.json"
  }
}
```

### 3. Install a registry item

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @vital-design/button
```

### Examples

```bash
# Add the Button component
npx shadcn@latest add @vital-design/button

# Add the Select component
npx shadcn@latest add @vital-design/select

# Add the Combobox component
npx shadcn@latest add @vital-design/combobox
```

> You can still install an item via its direct JSON URL, but the `@vital-design/<name>` alias is the recommended path because it also resolves `@vital-design/*` dependencies declared by registry items.

## Available UI Components

| Name                                                   | Registry Key     | Description                                     |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| Avatar                                                 | `avatar`         | Profile image with color variants               |
| [Breadcrumb](/docs/components/breadcrumb)              | `breadcrumb`     | Navigation trail of parent pages                |
| Button                                                 | `button`         | Filled and text variants with themes            |
| ButtonGroup                                            | `button-group`   | Composable button group layout primitive        |
| SplitButton                                            | `split-button`   | Primary action plus a chevron that opens a menu |
| Checkbox                                               | `checkbox`       | Checkbox with indeterminate support             |
| Chip                                                   | `chip`           | Toggle pill component                           |
| RadioGroup                                             | `radio-group`    | Radio button group                              |
| Switch                                                 | `switch`         | Toggle switch                                   |
| Tag                                                    | `tag`            | Read-only label with colors                     |
| SearchBar                                              | `search-bar`     | Styled search input                             |
| [InputGroup](/docs/components/input#inputgroup)        | `input-group`    | Composable input shell with addons and actions  |
| [Input](/docs/components/input#input)                  | `input`          | Single-line text field                          |
| [Textarea](/docs/components/input#textarea)            | `textarea`       | Multi-line text field                           |
| [PasswordInput](/docs/components/input#password-input) | `password-input` | Text field with visibility toggle               |
| [Item](/docs/components/item)                          | `item`           | Content rows with media, text, and actions      |
| [Separator](/docs/components/separator)                | `separator`      | Horizontal or vertical divider                  |
| Select                                                 | `select`         | Single and multiple dropdown                    |
| Combobox                                               | `combobox`       | Searchable input picker                         |

## Dependencies

When you install a component, the CLI also installs any declared dependencies. Components that depend on other Vittal Design components will pull them in automatically.

Common shared dependencies:

- `cn` — class merging + Tailwind conflict resolution (`cn()`), replaces `clsx` + `tailwind-merge`
- Base UI primitives for migrated `src-v2/` components (e.g., `@base-ui/react` for Switch, Checkbox, Avatar, and Radio Group)
- Vittal Design icons are installed as exact `@vital-design/icon-*` registry dependencies and copied to `src/components/icons/*`

> **Distribution note:** New components are published to the registry-first `src-v2/` layer. The legacy `src/` npm package remains available for compatibility, so do not assume every new component or theme asset is also available through `@fed/vital-design`.

## After Installation

1. Complete the [Tailwind Setup](/docs/getting-started/tailwind-setup) for registry-installed components. If you stay on the legacy npm package, keep its existing `src/` integration and install `styled-components` as needed.
2. Import the generated component from the local path configured by your project's `components.json`

# Changelog

> Changes to the Vital Design registry that affect how you install or use it.

Source: https://vittal.design/docs/changelog

This page tracks the **registry-backed** design system on vittal.design: components, blocks, icons, and tokens. It does not track the legacy `@fed/vital-design` npm package.

That package is built from `src/` and stays available for existing apps. New work ships through the registry. If you still import from the package, see the [Migration Guide](/docs/getting-started/migration-guide).

Entries are grouped by the month they shipped, newest first. We only record changes that affect how you install or use the registry — new components, breaking usage, tokens, and install steps. Documentation-only updates, such as new examples, are not listed.

## November 2026

### Fixed installs of Data Table and Input

#### Components

- **Input:** now installs `class-variance-authority`, which it imports. A new project that had not installed it failed to build after adding `input`, `editable` or `table-pagination`. Split Button now lists it too.
- **Resizable, Command:** now install `react-resizable-panels@^4.14.5` and `cmdk@^1.1.1` instead of whichever versions are latest, so a later major version cannot break a new install. Reinstalling them upgrades older versions, such as `react-resizable-panels` 3 to 4.

#### Blocks

- **Data Table:** now installs `@tanstack/react-table@^8.21.3`. Without a version range, a new project got version 9, which the block does not support. Reinstalling `data-table` in a project that uses version 9 moves it back to 8; check your own tables first.

### Data Table shows the row you just added

Adding a row while searching looked like it did nothing: the search filtered the new row out. Now 新增 clears the search and opens the group the row lands in, so the new row shows right away, ready to edit.

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @vital-design/data-table
```

If you changed your copy, bring over the changes in `data-table.tsx` (`addRow`) and `group-tree.ts` (`groupIdsOf`).

See [Data Table](/docs/blocks/data-table).

### Calendar requires react-day-picker 10

#### Components

- **Calendar:** now installs `react-day-picker@^10.0.2` instead of whichever version is latest, and no longer fails type checking on version 10 (`'table' does not exist in type 'Partial<ClassNames>'`). The removed `table` class name had no effect, so the calendar looks the same.

  Reinstall `calendar` to pick this up. If your project uses `react-day-picker` 9, this upgrades it to 10, which removed deprecated props such as `fromYear` and `toYear`; check the [upgrade guide](https://daypicker.dev/upgrading) if you pass react-day-picker props through `Calendar` or use the package elsewhere.

  `calendar` no longer adds `date-fns` to your project, because the component does not import it. If your own code imports `date-fns`, as the date picker example does, install it yourself.

### Single focus ring on Button, dark native controls

Reinstall the theme and the buttons:

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @vital-design/vital-theme @vital-design/button @vital-design/split-button
```

- **Button, LinkButton:** keyboard focus shows only the Vittal Design focus ring. The browser outline that used to appear with it is gone. In forced-colors mode (such as Windows High Contrast), where shadows are not drawn, the outline still appears.
- **SplitButton:** looks the same as before. Reinstall it together with `button`; an older copy has no visible focus with the new Button.
- **Theme:** `.dark` sets `color-scheme: dark`, so native checkboxes, selects, date pickers, scrollbars, and browser focus outlines render dark.

### Alert Dialog

#### Components

- **Alert Dialog (new):** a modal confirmation for actions the user must answer before continuing, such as deleting something. It is built on Base UI Alert Dialog, so it has `role="alertdialog"` and doesn't close on an outside click. It composes like `Dialog` (trigger, portal, backdrop, viewport, popup), with `AlertDialogBody`, `AlertDialogMedia` for a status icon, `AlertDialogHeader`, `AlertDialogTitle`, `AlertDialogDescription`, `AlertDialogFooter`, and `AlertDialogClose`. `AlertDialogPortal` takes `container` to render inside another node. Install it with `@vital-design/alert-dialog`.

### Sidebar props for embedded and multiple sidebars

#### Components

- **Sidebar:** new optional props for sidebars that live inside another app's page or share a page with a second sidebar:

  - `SidebarProvider` `cookieName` writes the open state under another cookie name; `cookieName={null}` writes no cookie.
  - `SidebarProvider` `isMobile` replaces the built-in `768px` check. `isMobile={false}` never switches to the mobile Sheet.
  - `SidebarTrigger` takes `children` to replace its icon and `render` to use another element, such as `render={<Button variant="ghost" size="icon-md" />}`. A rendered element keeps its own look. Calling `event.preventDefault()` in `onClick` stops the toggle.
  - `Sidebar` takes `render` to change its root element, such as `<aside />` or `<nav />`. It is ignored on mobile, where the panel is a Sheet.
  - `SidebarMenuButton` no longer throws outside a `SidebarProvider`; it renders as expanded, without its tooltip.

  Leaving the new props out keeps the current behavior. Reinstall `sidebar` to pick this up.

### Status, file, and arrow icons from the design list

New icon items, all drawn by the design team in the 20×20 frame:

- Status: `icon-circle-check`, `icon-circle-check-solid`, `icon-circle-xmark`, `icon-circle-xmark-solid`, `icon-circle-info`, `icon-circle-info-solid`, `icon-circle-exclamation-solid`, `icon-circle-minus-solid`, `icon-circle-question`, `icon-exclamation-solid`, `icon-circle-dashed`, `icon-circle-dot`.
- Files and arrows: `icon-file-lines`, `icon-file-arrow-up-solid`, `icon-arrow-right-long`, `icon-arrow-up-right-from-square`, `icon-arrow-up-right-from-square-solid`.
- Other: `icon-clock-solid`, `icon-ellipsis-vertical`, `icon-grip-dots-vertical`.

`InfoIcon` is renamed `CircleInfoIcon` (`@vital-design/icon-circle-info`) to match the design list, and now uses the design artwork. The old name and registry item still work but are deprecated; `InfoIcon` re-exports `CircleInfoIcon`. Switch to the new name.

Updated artwork:

- `ClockIcon` uses the redrawn design artwork; the hand is redrawn.
- `ClearIcon` uses the redrawn design artwork; the circle is centred in the frame (it sat 0.25px high) and the × is larger.
- `CalendarDaysIcon` is about 0.25px larger on each side, matching the design file.
- `CircleUserIcon`, `SidebarIcon`, and `ThumbtackSolidIcon` look the same but are now drawn with strokes, so the `strokeWidth` prop changes their line weight like the other icons.

Component changes:

- `data-table`: the drag handle in the column-visibility popover is now a 20px `GripDotsVerticalIcon` instead of six drawn dots.
- `sidebar-cloud-04`: the Support item uses `CircleInfoIcon`, and the external-link mark uses `ArrowUpRightFromSquareIcon`.

**Temporary artwork.** These icons still use placeholder artwork until the design team confirms the final version. Only the SVG will change:

- Font Awesome Pro in the design file, so the previous Vittal artwork is used instead: `MagnifyingGlassIcon`, `PlusIcon`, `SpinnerIcon`, `ShieldCheckIcon`, `SquareArrowOutUpRightIcon`.
- Font Awesome Free shapes not yet redrawn: `FlagIcon`, `UserIcon`.
- Not in the design file yet: `PanelLeftIcon`.
- Drawn by design but not yet confirmed: `XmarkIcon`, `EyeIcon`.

### Tree Select

- **[Tree Select](/docs/blocks/tree-select):** a new block for searchable hierarchical path pickers, built from `Command` and `Popover`. Pass a flat item list; selecting a leaf returns its value and the path from the top level. It replaces the Hierarchical Picker example that was on the Command page.

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @vital-design/tree-select
```

### Portal container and positioning props on popup content

#### Components

- **Tooltip, Select, Combobox, Autocomplete, Dropdown Menu:** `TooltipContent`, `SelectContent`, `ComboboxContent`, `AutocompleteContent`, `DropdownMenuContent`, and `DropdownMenuSubContent` now take the same portal and positioning props as `PopoverContent`:

  - `portalContainer` renders the popup inside another node, such as a CSS-scoped root, instead of `document.body`.
  - `anchor` positions the popup against an element other than the trigger.
  - `collisionBoundary`, `collisionPadding`, `collisionAvoidance`, `positionMethod`, `sticky`, `arrowPadding`, and `disableAnchorTracking` go to the positioner.
  - `keepMounted` goes to the portal. `SelectContent` doesn't have it, because Base UI's Select portal doesn't accept it.

  All are optional; leaving them out keeps the current behavior. `DropdownMenuSubContent` used to pass `anchor` to the popup element; it now positions the submenu. Reinstall `tooltip`, `select`, `combobox`, `autocomplete`, or `dropdown-menu` to pick this up.

### Popover anchor, portal container, and positioning props

#### Components

- **Popover:** `PopoverContent` accepts `anchor`, so a popover can be positioned against an element other than its trigger, or opened with no trigger at all. It also accepts `portalContainer`, like `DropdownMenuContent`, to render the popup inside a scoped root instead of `document.body`. If you patched these props into your copy, you can drop the patch. See [Custom Anchor](/docs/components/popover#custom-anchor) and [Portal Container](/docs/components/popover#portal-container).
- `PopoverContent` also passes `collisionBoundary`, `collisionPadding`, `collisionAvoidance`, `positionMethod`, `sticky`, `arrowPadding`, and `disableAnchorTracking` to the positioner, and `keepMounted` to the portal. All are optional; leaving them out keeps the current behavior. Reinstall `popover` to pick this up.

### Table of Contents

#### Components

- **Table of Contents:** now a registry item. Install it with `npx shadcn@latest add @vital-design/table-of-contents`. It's a compact rail of section ticks that expands into the full list of headings on hover or keyboard focus. See [Table of Contents](/docs/components/table-of-contents).

### Dark color tokens

Reinstall the theme to pick up dark colors:

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @vital-design/vital-theme
```

Light values stay on `:root`. The same custom properties change when an ancestor has `class="dark"`. `prefers-color-scheme` does not switch them. See [Colors → Dark mode](/docs/design-tokens/colors#dark-mode).

Primitive scales, and semantic aliases that point at those scales, have dark values. `background`, `card`, and `popover` are `#232327`, and `input` is `#444447`. The `.dark` ancestor uses that paper and the dark foreground. `border` and `border-overlap` alias scales, so they follow them: white at 0.08 and `#444447`.

**Scale classes switch too.** Under `.dark`, a scale class such as `bg-grayscale-50` or `text-primary-500` resolves to that scale's dark value. This is part of the theme's contract, so a scale class in your own code changes with the mode. Fixed Tailwind colors and arbitrary values do not: `bg-white` stays white and is reserved for marks such as switch thumbs, and `text-white` stays white.

Components used to paint their paper with `bg-white`, which stays white in dark mode. They now use `bg-background`, and some also fix text that was hard to read on dark paper. Reinstall the theme and the items you use:

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @vital-design/vital-theme
npx shadcn@latest add @vital-design/alert @vital-design/autocomplete @vital-design/button @vital-design/calendar
npx shadcn@latest add @vital-design/card @vital-design/checkbox @vital-design/combobox @vital-design/command
npx shadcn@latest add @vital-design/dialog @vital-design/dropdown-menu @vital-design/field @vital-design/input
npx shadcn@latest add @vital-design/input-group @vital-design/item @vital-design/number-input @vital-design/pagination
npx shadcn@latest add @vital-design/popover @vital-design/radio-group @vital-design/resizable @vital-design/select
npx shadcn@latest add @vital-design/sheet @vital-design/split-button @vital-design/table @vital-design/tag
npx shadcn@latest add @vital-design/textarea @vital-design/time-picker @vital-design/toast @vital-design/toolbar
npx shadcn@latest add @vital-design/tooltip
npx shadcn@latest add @vital-design/data-table @vital-design/sidebar-cloud-01 @vital-design/sidebar-cloud-02 @vital-design/sidebar-cloud-03
npx shadcn@latest add @vital-design/sidebar-cloud-04 @vital-design/sidebar-cloud-05 @vital-design/sidebar-cloud-06
```

The theme also adds a `dark:` variant that matches inside a `.dark` ancestor.

Known limitations, still waiting on design:

- `warning-foreground` follows the grayscale ink, so it turns white under `.dark`, and text on warning fills loses contrast. The other white foregrounds, such as `primary-foreground`, stay white.
- Avatar and Tag palettes, shadows, and gradients have no dark values.
- Solid buttons keep white text.
- The frosted backdrop in the sidebar-cloud blocks stays light, so their menu text is hard to read in dark mode.
- The info Tooltip and info Toast keep their current dark backgrounds.

### SplitButton menus

#### Components

- **SplitButton:** `splitRender` turns the chevron into a menu trigger, so `<SplitButton splitRender={<DropdownMenuTrigger />}>` inside a `DropdownMenu` opens, positions, and closes the menu without your own state or anchor. `open` is now optional, and `splitLabel` sets the chevron's accessible name. Existing `open` + `splitOnClick` code keeps working. See [SplitButton](/docs/components/split-button). Reinstall `split-button` to pick this up.

### Tag semantics

#### Components

- **Tag:** no longer renders `role="option"` or `aria-selected`. A clickable Tag with `selected` now sets `aria-pressed` on its button. If your tests find Tags with `getByRole('option')`, query by text or `data-slot="tag"` instead. Reinstall `tag` to pick this up.
- **Data Table:** the tags editor shows each choice as a `Tag`, the same pill as the cell, instead of plain text. Reinstall `data-table` to pick this up.

### Pagination

- **[Pagination](/docs/components/pagination):** added composable page links, first/last and previous/next controls, disabled states, and an ellipsis that opens a menu of the hidden pages. Use anchors for navigation or compose native buttons with `render` for in-place updates. Installing `@vital-design/pagination` also installs the angle icons it uses.
- **[Table Pagination](/docs/blocks/table-pagination):** a single-row table footer with page controls, a page jump, rows per page, and the current range. Narrow rows hide the jump field and the page-size select.

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @vital-design/pagination @vital-design/table-pagination
```

### Breadcrumb

#### Components

- **Breadcrumb:** now available from the registry as `breadcrumb`. See [Breadcrumb](/docs/components/breadcrumb).

### Icons use the design names and 20×20 frames

**Breaking:** icon names now match the design team's icon list. The old registry items are removed.

| Old item                                  | New item                              |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `@vital-design/icon-chevron-left`         | `@vital-design/icon-angle-left`       |
| `@vital-design/icon-chevron-right`        | `@vital-design/icon-angle-right`      |
| `@vital-design/icon-chevron-double-left`  | `@vital-design/icon-angles-left`      |
| `@vital-design/icon-chevron-double-right` | `@vital-design/icon-angles-right`     |
| `@vital-design/icon-chevron-down`         | `@vital-design/icon-angle-down`       |
| `@vital-design/icon-chevron-up`           | `@vital-design/icon-angle-up`         |
| `@vital-design/icon-close`                | `@vital-design/icon-xmark`            |
| `@vital-design/icon-disabled`             | `@vital-design/icon-ban`              |
| `@vital-design/icon-calendar`             | `@vital-design/icon-calendar-days`    |
| `@vital-design/icon-search`               | `@vital-design/icon-magnifying-glass` |

Update imports to the new component names: `AngleLeftIcon`, `AngleRightIcon`, `AnglesLeftIcon`, `AnglesRightIcon`, `AngleDownIcon`, `AngleUpIcon`, `XmarkIcon`, `BanIcon`, `CalendarDaysIcon`, `MagnifyingGlassIcon`. Reinstall the components you use; every component that depended on a renamed item now depends on the new one.

The carets take the `Solid` suffix, because a plain name means the Regular style: `CaretDownIcon` and `CaretUpIcon` are now `CaretDownSolidIcon` and `CaretUpSolidIcon` (`@vital-design/icon-caret-down-solid`, `@vital-design/icon-caret-up-solid`). The old names and registry items still work but are deprecated; `CaretDownIcon` re-exports `CaretDownSolidIcon`. Switch to the new names.

New icon items: `icon-angle-down-solid`, `icon-angle-up-solid`, `icon-angle-left-solid`, `icon-angle-right-solid`, `icon-angle-left-to-line`, `icon-angle-right-to-line`, `icon-check-solid`, `icon-minus-solid`, `icon-bars`, `icon-circle-user`, `icon-home`, `icon-inbox`, `icon-life-ring`, `icon-planet-ringed`, `icon-sidebar`, `icon-thumbtack`, `icon-thumbtack-solid`, `icon-bell-slash`, `icon-caret-left-solid`, `icon-caret-right-solid`, `icon-note`, `icon-placeholder`, `icon-placeholder-solid`. `PlaceholderIcon` is the design's `*icons`: a stand-in for a slot that takes any icon. See [Icons → Regular and Solid](/docs/components/icons#regular-and-solid).

Every icon now uses a 20×20 frame with padding, so a `size-*` class sets the frame, not the glyph. Components size icons to the Figma frame: icons inside `Button` (`data-icon`) are 18px (`md`, `icon-md`) and 20px (`lg`, `icon-lg`) with no margin, and `Sidebar` menu icons are 20px. If you set your own icon sizes, check them against the new frames.

Component changes that follow the design list:

- `checkbox` uses `CheckSolidIcon` and `MinusSolidIcon`.
- `number-input` steppers use `CaretUpSolidIcon` and `CaretDownSolidIcon`.
- `split-button` uses the regular angle on white themes and the solid angle on coloured themes.
- The angle, angles, and angle-to-line icons use the redrawn design artwork, so the glyph is 10px tall in the 20px frame instead of 8.3px. This shows in `calendar` and `split-button`.
- `EllipsisIcon` no longer has a built-in 0.55 fill opacity; it takes the text color like every other icon. In `breadcrumb` the collapsed ellipsis is now `grayscale-500`, the same as the other inactive items. If you added `[fill-opacity:1]` to undo it, remove it.
- `data-table` group rows use a 20px `CaretDownSolidIcon` (rotated when collapsed), and the popover option check uses `CheckSolidIcon` like `checkbox`. The selection bar's close icon is 20px and the add-row plus is 18px.

**Temporary artwork.** These icons keep their names and sizes, but the artwork is a placeholder until the design team draws the final version. Only the SVG will change:

- Font Awesome Pro in the design file, so the previous Vittal artwork is used instead: `MagnifyingGlassIcon`, `PlusIcon`, `SpinnerIcon`, `ShieldCheckIcon`, `SquareArrowOutUpRightIcon`.
- Font Awesome Free shapes not yet redrawn: `ClockIcon`, `FlagIcon`, `UserIcon`, `EllipsisIcon`.
- Not in the design file yet: `InfoIcon`, `ClearIcon`, `PanelLeftIcon`.
- Drawn by design but not yet confirmed: `XmarkIcon`, `AngleLeftIcon`, `AngleRightIcon` (and their Solid versions), `AnglesLeftIcon`, `AnglesRightIcon`, `CircleUserIcon`, `ThumbtackSolidIcon`.

### Border tokens

`--border` is now the 0.08 hairline (`grayscale-opacity-200`), the line Figma uses for dividers. It was a solid `#DEDEE2`. A new `--border-overlap` token keeps the solid `#DEDEE2` for edges that stack or cross, where a translucent line would darken. Use it with `border-border-overlap`.

The theme also sets a default border color, so a bare `border`, `border-t`, or `border-b` draws the `--border` hairline. Before, Tailwind v4 drew it in the text color.

Avatar, `AvatarGroupCount`, and the group rails in the Data Table block move to `--border-overlap`, so they look the same as before. The Dialog footer divider and any `border-border` you use for dividers get lighter. A `FieldLabel` that wraps a `Field` (the choice-card layout) draws its outline with a bare `border`, so it also goes from the text color to the hairline. Reinstall the theme and these items:

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @vital-design/vital-theme
npx shadcn@latest add @vital-design/avatar
```

### Data Table block

**Breaking.** The three data table blocks are replaced by one generic block, `@vital-design/data-table`. You pass it your own `data` and `columns`; it groups rows by any field, up to two levels, with a 新增 row per group. It also has search, sorting, resizable and reorderable columns, row selection with a floating action bar, and inline and popover cell editing. The checkbox and actions columns stay pinned and cast a shadow while other columns scroll under them. A review-task example shows how to wire it up. The block uses the new `@vital-design/icon-gear`.

These ids are retired and leave the registry: `@vital-design/data-table-group-01` (candidate tree), `@vital-design/data-table-group-02` (ESG emission tree), and `@vital-design/data-table-group-04` (editable cells). Copies you already installed keep working, since a block is your own code. To move over, install the new block and port your columns and rows; grouping by a field replaces the fixed tree rows. Not carried over yet: a row count in group headers, more than one left-pinned column, and `columnResizeMode="onEnd"`.

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @vital-design/data-table
```

See [Data Table](/docs/blocks/data-table).

### Dialog and Sheet heights on mobile

#### Components

- **Dialog:** the popup's max height now follows the viewport it sits in (`max-h-full`) instead of `calc(100vh-2rem)`. On mobile browsers, `100vh` is taller than the visible area while the address bar shows, so a tall dialog ran under the toolbar and lost its bottom spacing. It now keeps the viewport's 1rem padding and scrolls inside. If you added your own `max-h-[calc(100dvh-…)]` to work around this, you can drop it. Reinstall `dialog` to pick this up.
- **Sheet:** `top` and `bottom` sheets cap at `80dvh` instead of `80vh`, to match the `h-dvh` that `left` and `right` sheets already use. Reinstall `sheet` to pick this up.

## October 2026

### React 19

The registry and the docs site are developed and tested on React 19. New projects should use React 19. See [Installation](/docs/getting-started/installation).

### Link button

#### Components

- **Button:** added `LinkButton`, a link styled as a button. It shares Button's variants, themes, and sizes, renders `<a>` (or a router link via `render`), and keeps link semantics. Use it instead of `<Button nativeButton={false} render={<a />}>`, which reports links as buttons. See [Button → Link](/docs/components/button#link).

### Table stripes and column resize

#### Table

[Table](/docs/components/table) can stripe body rows. `striped` paints even rows. `striped="odd"` paints the other rows. Set `--table-stripe` and `--table-row-hover` on the table to change the colors.

Reinstall the table to pick this up:

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @vital-design/table
```

**Breaking:** hover, expanded, and selected row backgrounds no longer use `bg-grayscale-opacity-100`. They read `--table-row-hover`. With `striped` left off, that variable still falls back to `--grayscale-opacity-100`, so the default look stays the same.

- `hover:bg-grayscale-opacity-100` → `hover:bg-[var(--table-row-hover,var(--grayscale-opacity-100))]`
- `data-[state=selected]:bg-grayscale-opacity-100` → `data-[state=selected]:bg-[var(--table-row-hover,var(--grayscale-opacity-100))]`

`TableHead` is now `position: relative`. An absolutely positioned child lines up with the header cell. If one of yours was lined up with an ancestor outside the cell, point it at the cell instead.

#### Icons

Caret up and caret down are new registry icons. See [Icons](/docs/components/icons).

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @vital-design/icon-caret-up
npx shadcn@latest add @vital-design/icon-caret-down
```

#### Data tables

[Data Table group 01](/docs/blocks/data-table-group-01) and [group 02](/docs/blocks/data-table-group-02) can resize columns. Drag the header edge. `columnResizeMode` defaults to `onChange`. Use `onEnd` on a wide table with many pinned columns so the columns stay put until you release.

Reinstall both blocks. Group 02 also swaps its sort icon from chevron up to the caret pair, and drops `@vital-design/icon-chevron-up`. `@vital-design/icon-chevron-down` stays for the row rail. The sort label truncates so the caret stays visible when a column gets narrow.

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @vital-design/data-table-group-01
npx shadcn@latest add @vital-design/data-table-group-02
```

## September 2026

### Registry on vittal.design

The documentation site and the shadcn-compatible registry now publish together at [vittal.design](https://vittal.design). This entry is a snapshot of what is available today. Later entries will list only what changed.

#### Install

Add the registry, then install items with the shadcn CLI. See [Installation](/docs/getting-started/installation).

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @vital-design/button
```

Registry URL: `https://vittal.design/r/{name}.json`

#### Components

**Foundation:** [Alert](/docs/components/alert), [Avatar](/docs/components/avatar), [Badge](/docs/components/badge), [Button](/docs/components/button), [Button Group](/docs/components/button-group), [Chip](/docs/components/chip), [Icons](/docs/components/icons), [Item](/docs/components/item), [Label](/docs/components/label), [Separator](/docs/components/separator), [Skeleton](/docs/components/skeleton), [Spinner](/docs/components/spinner), [Split Button](/docs/components/split-button), [Tag](/docs/components/tag)

**Inputs:** [Checkbox](/docs/components/checkbox), [Editable](/docs/components/editable), [Field](/docs/components/field), [Input](/docs/components/input), [Number Input](/docs/components/number-input), [Radio Group](/docs/components/radio-group), [Search Bar](/docs/components/search-bar), [Slider](/docs/components/slider), [Switch](/docs/components/switch), [Textarea](/docs/components/textarea)

**Pickers and menus:** [Autocomplete](/docs/components/autocomplete), [Calendar](/docs/components/calendar), [Combobox](/docs/components/combobox), [Command](/docs/components/command), [Dropdown Menu](/docs/components/dropdown-menu), [Popover](/docs/components/popover), [Select](/docs/components/select), [Time Picker](/docs/components/time-picker)

- Cloud Sidebar: [flat](/docs/blocks/sidebar/cloud/flat), [inline submenus](/docs/blocks/sidebar/cloud/inline-submenus), [collapsible submenus](/docs/blocks/sidebar/cloud/collapsible-submenus), [dropdown submenus](/docs/blocks/sidebar/cloud/dropdown-submenus), [secondary nav](/docs/blocks/sidebar/cloud/secondary-nav), [header actions](/docs/blocks/sidebar/cloud/header-actions)

#### Platform

- Components use **Base UI** primitives and **Tailwind CSS 4**
- Style isolation follows the `data-slot` convention in [Tailwind CSS Setup](/docs/getting-started/tailwind-setup)
- Agent index: [llms.txt](/llms.txt)
